semin-durr:3-3.t: The words of the Exalted: {يُدَبِّرُ الأمر} — there are three views on it. First: it is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a second khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ». Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Third: it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), a clause with no grammatical position.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَعْدَ الله}: accusative (manṣūb) as the emphasizing maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of emphasis], because the meaning of «إليه مَرْجِعُكُمْ» is: He has promised you that.
And His words: {حَقّاً} are another maṣdar, emphasizing the meaning of this promise, and what governs it in the accusative is concealed, i.e. «أَحُقُّ ذلك حقاً» (I affirm that as a truth). It was also said: «حقاً» is accusative through «وَعْدَ» with «في» implied, i.e. «وَعْدَ الله في حق» (Allah's promise in truth), meaning by likening it to an adverb (ẓarf). Al-Akhfash the Younger said: "The implied form is: «وقتَ حق» (at a time of truth)," and he recited:
2566 - أحقاً عبادَ الله أنْ لَسْتُ ذاهباً ... ولا والِجاً إلا عليَّ رقيبُ
(Is it truly so, O servants of Allah, that I do not go out nor come in without a watcher over me?)
His words: {إِنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ}: the majority read the hamza with kasra (إِنَّه), as a resumptive clause. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], Ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, al-Aʿmash and Sahl ibn Shuʿayb read it with fatḥa (أَنَّه). There are several interpretations of this reading. First: it is the fāʿil (agent) of the verb that governs «حقاً» in the accusative, i.e. «حَقَّ حَقَّاً بَدْءُ الخلق ثم إعادتُه» (truly true is the origination of creation and then its repetition), as in the poet's words:
2567 - أحقاً عبادَ الله أَنْ لستُ جائِياً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Is it truly so, O servants of Allah, that I do not come…)
— the verse [as above]. This is the position of al-Farrāʾ, for he said: "The implied form is: «يحقُّ أنه يبدأ الخلق» (it is true that He originates creation)." Second: it is accusative through the verb that governed «وعد الله» in the accusative, i.e. Allah the Exalted promised the origination of creation and then its repetition, the meaning being the repetition of creation after its origination. Third: it is with the lām of the genitive omitted, i.e. «لأنه» (because He…). Al-Zamakhsharī and others mentioned these three views. Fourth: it is a badal (substitute) from «وَعْدَ الله»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Fifth: it is nominative through «حقاً» itself, i.e. through the nunated maṣdar; this only works if «حقاً» is made non-emphasizing, because the emphasizing maṣdar has no governing power unless it stands in for its verb — and there is some discussion of this. Sixth: «حقاً» is likened to an adverb, serving as a fronted khabar, and «أنَّه» is in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), as in their saying «أحقاً أنك ذاهب» (Is it true that you are going?), of which they said: its implied form is «أفي حقٍ ذهابك» (Is your going in truth?).
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «حَقٌّ أنه» with «حق» in the nominative and «أنَّ» with fatḥa, as mubtadaʾ and khabar. Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "That «حق» is the khabar of a mubtadaʾ and «أنه» is the mubtadaʾ is the [correct] way of parsing it, just as you say «صحيحٌ أنك تخرج» (it is correct that you are going out), because the noun of «أنَّ» is definite, while what precedes it in this example is indefinite." I say: the apparent sense of this phrasing suggests that the reverse is permissible, and this has indeed occurred in the chapter of «إنَّ», as in the poet's words:
2568 - وإن حراماً أن أَسُبَّ مُجاشعاً ... بآبائيَ الشُّمِّ الكرامِ الخَضَارمِ
(And it is indeed forbidden that I should revile Mujāshiʿ by my lofty, noble, generous forefathers.)
And his words:
2569 - وإن شفاءً عَبْرَةٌ أَنْ سَفَحْتُها وهل عند رسمٍ دارسٍ مِنْ مُعَوَّل ...
(And indeed a cure is a tear, that I should shed it — yet is there any recourse at an effaced trace of a dwelling?)
— taking «أنْ سفحتُها» as a badal from «عبرة». And with «كان», an indefinite has been made the subject of which a definite is predicated, as in the poet's words:
2570 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا يكُ موقفٌ منكِ الوَدَاعا
(…and let not a halting with you be the farewell.)
And his words:
2571 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يكون مزاجَها عَسَلٌ وماءُ
(…its mixture being honey and water.)
Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ allowed the nominative of «وعد», making it the khabar of «مرجعكم». And he allowed the nominative of «وعد» and «حق» as mubtadaʾ and khabar, and that is good, but no one read it so." I say: yes, no one read both «وعد» and «حق» in the nominative together; as for the nominative of «حق» alone, it has been stated above that Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it so, and its justification has been given. It is not permissible for «وعدَ الله» to govern «أنه», because it has been qualified by His words «حقاً»; Abū al-Fatḥ [Ibn Jinnī] said this.
And it was read «وَعَدَ اللَّهُ» in the form of the past verb with the Name of Majesty in the nominative as its fāʿil; on this reading «أنه يَبْدَأ» is governed by it, if this reader reads «أنه» with fatḥa.
The majority read «يَبْدأُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, from «بدأ»; Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa read «يُبْدِىء» from «أَبْدأ»; «بَدَأ» and «أبدأ» have the same meaning.
His words: {لِيَجْزِيَ} are attached to His words «ثم يُعيده», and «بالقسطِ» is attached to «يَجْزي». It may also be a ḥāl, either from the fāʿil or from the object, i.e. He recompenses them while being in conjunction with justice, or while they are in conjunction with it. «القِسْط» means justice.
His words: {والذين كَفَرُواْ} admit two views. First: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause after it is its khabar. Second: it is accusative, conjoined to the relative noun before it, and the clause after it explains their recompense. «شراب» may be a fāʿil, or a mubtadaʾ; the first is preferable.
His words: {بِمَا كَانُواْ}: the apparent view is that it is attached to the [notion of] settled being (istiqrār) concealed in the preposition-phrase that serves as the khabar, the implied form being: «استقر لهم شراب من جهنم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا» (there is settled for them a drink from Hell and a painful punishment because of what they used to…). Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed two views for it and mentioned no others. First: it is another naʿt (adjective) of «عذاب». Second: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ — and this has no meaning, and there is no need to depart from the first view.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
The words of the Exalted: {ضِيَآءً}: either a second object, taking «الجَعْل» in the sense of transforming (taṣyīr), or a ḥāl (circumstantial), taking it in the sense of bringing into being (inshāʾ). The majority read «ضياء» with an explicit yāʾ before the alif, its origin being wāw because it is from «الضوء». Qunbul, from Ibn Kathīr, read here, in al-Anbiyāʾ and in al-Qaṣaṣ «ضِئاءً», changing the yāʾ into a hamza, so that there is an alif between two hamzas. This was interpreted as a case of metathesis (maqlūb): its lām [third radical] was moved forward and its ʿayn [second radical] moved back, so the yāʾ fell at the end after a superfluous alif and was changed into a hamza, as in «رداء». Or, if you wish, you may say: when the word was metathesized it became «ضياواً» with wāw, the ʿayn reverting to its original wāw because the cause of its change into yāʾ — the kasra preceding it — no longer existed; then the wāw was replaced by a hamza, as in «كساء». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was changed into an alif and then the alif was changed into a hamza so that two alifs would not come together."
This reading was considered unlikely on the grounds that the language is built on lightening the hamza, so how could they contrive to change a light letter into something heavier than it? I say: there is nothing strange in that, for they have changed the weak letters — alif, wāw and yāʾ — into hamza in places that can hardly be counted; except that here it is heavy because two hamzas come together. Abū Shāma said: "This is a weak reading, for the analogy of the language is to flee from the meeting of two hamzas towards lightening one of them; so how could one contrive a fronting and delaying that leads to the meeting of two hamzas that were not there originally? This is contrary to the rule of the language."
Abū Bakr Ibn Mujāhid — who was one of those who read under Qunbul — said: "Ibn Kathīr alone [read] «ضِئاء» with two hamzas throughout the Quran: the first hamza before the alif and the second after it. That is how I read it under Qunbul, and it is a mistake. The companions of al-Bazzī and Ibn Fulayḥ used to reject this and read «ضياء» like everyone else." I say: Abū Bakr often presumes against his teacher and declares him mistaken — you will come across several places of that kind — and this ought not to be, for Qunbul is of a standing that prevents anyone from speaking against him.
And His saying «ضياء» with respect to the sun is because «الضوء» (radiance) is stronger than «النور» (light); this was discussed at the beginning of al-Baqara. «ضياء ونوراً» may both be maṣdars (verbal nouns), made to be the two heavenly bodies themselves for hyperbole, or [they may be] on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. «ذات ضياء وذا نور» (possessing radiance and possessing light). «ضياء» may also be the plural of «ضوء», like «سَوْط / سِياط» and «حَوْض / حياض».
«منازل» is accusative as an adverb of place. Al-Zamakhsharī took it to be on the omission of a muḍāf, either from the first [element], i.e. «قَدَّر مَسيره» (He determined its course [in stations]), or from the second, i.e. «قدَّره ذا منازل» (He determined it as possessing stations). On the first implied form «منازل» is an adverb as already stated; on the second it is a second object, with «قَدَّر» being made to include the meaning «صَيَّره ذا منازل بالتقدير» (He made it, by determination, possess stations). Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān], after mentioning the two implied forms without attributing them to al-Zamakhsharī, said: "Or: «قدَّر له منازل» (He determined stations for it); then [the preposition] was omitted and the verb reached it directly, so it became accusative. According to these implied forms it is accusative as an adverb, a ḥāl or an object, as in His words: {والقمر قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ} [Yā Sīn: 39]." Abū al-Baqāʾ had also preceded him in that.
The pronoun in «قَدَّرناه» refers to the moon alone, because it is what the Arabs relied on in their reckoning of dates. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It may be that He intends both of them together, in that both play a role in knowing the number of years and the reckoning, but mention of one of them sufficed, as in the words of the Exalted: {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62], and as the poet said:
2572 - رماني بأمرٍ كنتُ منه ووالدي ... بريئاً ومِنْ أجل الطَّوِيِّ رماني
(He accused me of a matter of which I and my father were innocent, and on account of the well he accused me.)"
[Translator's note: the closing quotation mark of Ibn ʿAṭiyya's quotation is not marked in the source; its end is placed here as the most likely reading.]

semin-durr:6-6.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لِتَعْلَمُواْ}: attached to «قَدَّره». Abū ʿAmr was asked about «الحساب»: "Do you put it in the accusative or the genitive?" He said: "And who knows what the number of the reckoning is?" Meaning: he was asked whether you conjoin it to «عَددَ» and so put it in the accusative, or to «السنين» and so put it in the genitive; and it is as though he said: it cannot be in the genitive, since that would require that the number of the reckoning be known, and no one is able to know its number. «ذلك» points to what has preceded, i.e. Allah did not create that which has been mentioned except in conjunction with the truth; so [«بالحق»] is a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the fāʿil (agent) or from the object. It was also said: the bāʾ has the meaning of the lām, i.e. «للحق» (for the truth), but there is no need for that.
Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «يُفَصِّل» with the yāʾ of the third person, in accordance with the Name of Allah the Exalted; the rest read with the nūn of majesty, a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to the first person for magnification.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
The words of the Exalted: {واطمأنوا}: it may be conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), and that is the apparent view; or the wāw may be circumstantial (wāw al-ḥāl), the implied form being «وقد اطمأنُّوا» (having become content). His words «والذين هم» may be a case of conjoining attributes, meaning that they combine not hoping for the meeting with Allah and heedlessness of the signs; or this relative noun may be other than the first, so that it is conjoined to the noun of «إن», i.e. «إن الذين لا يَرْجُون، وإن الذين هم» (indeed those who do not hope…, and indeed those who are…).
[Translator's note: the source has «عدم رجال لقاء الله», evidently a misprint for «عدم رجاء لقاء الله» (not hoping for the meeting with Allah); translated accordingly.]

semin-durr:8-8.t: And {أولئك} is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «مَأْواهم» is a second mubtadaʾ, and «النار» is the khabar (predicate) of this second one; the second and its khabar are the khabar of «أولئك», and «أولئك» with its khabar is the khabar of «إن الذين». «بما كانوا» is attached to what is contained in the clause «مَأْواهم النار»; the bāʾ is causal and «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the verb after it is brought in the imperfect to indicate the continuity of that at all times. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The bāʾ is attached to something omitted, i.e. «جُوزوا بما كانوا» (they were recompensed for what they used to…)."

semin-durr:9-9.t: The words of the Exalted: {تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهِمُ الأنهار}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «يَهْديهم», or resumptive, or conjoined to what precedes it with the conjunction omitted. His words «في جنات» may be attached to «تَجْري», or be a ḥāl from «الأنهار», or be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar of «إنَّ», or be attached to «يَهْدي».

semin-durr:10-10.t:
The words of the Exalted: {دَعْوَاهُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «سبحانَك», governed by an implied verb that may not be made overt, is the khabar (predicate); the khabar here is the mubtadaʾ itself, the meaning being that their supplication is this utterance. So «دعوى» may have the meaning of supplication (duʿāʾ), and «اللهم» indicates this, because it is a vocative meaning «يا الله» (O Allah). This «دعاء» here may also have the meaning of worship, so «دَعْوى» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its agent. Then, if you wish, you may make this a case of verbal predication (isnād lafẓī), i.e. their supplication in Paradise is this very utterance, so that «سبحانك» itself is the khabar, brought in as a quotation in its accusative form [governed] by that verb; or, if you wish, you may make it a case of semantic predication (isnād maʿnawī), so that it is not required that they say only this utterance; rather they say it and whatever conveys its meaning of all the attributes of transcendence and sanctification. You have had the like of this before at the words of the Exalted: {وَقُولُواْ حِطَّةٌ} [al-Baqara: 58], so turn to it.
«تحيَّتُهم» is a mubtadaʾ and «سَلامٌ» its khabar, and it is like what precedes it. The maṣdar here may be annexed to its agent, i.e. their greeting with which they greet one another is "peace"; or it may be annexed to its object, i.e. their greeting with which the angels greet them is "peace," and this is supported by {وَالمَلاَئِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن كُلِّ بَابٍ سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُم} [al-Raʿd: 23]. «فيها» in both places is attached to the maṣdar before it, and «قبل» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what follows it, so that it is attached to something omitted, but that is not strong. [Translator's note: «قبل» does not occur in this verse; the word meant is probably «فيها», which may be a ḥāl from what follows it.] Some said: "«تحيتهم» may be one of those cases in which the maṣdar is annexed to both its agent and its object together, because the meaning is: they greet one another; and it would be like the words of the Exalted: {وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَاهِدِينَ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 78], where He annexed it to Dāwūd and Sulaymān, who were the two judges, and to the one judged." This rests on another question, namely: is it permissible to combine the literal and the figurative [in one expression] or not? If we say yes, then that is permissible, because annexing the maṣdar to its agent is literal and to its object figurative; whoever forbids that answers that the minimum of the plural is two, and that is why He said «لحكمهم» (their judgement).
His words: {وَآخِرُ دَعْوَاهُمْ} is a mubtadaʾ, and «أَنْ» is the one lightened from the heavy [«أنَّ»]; its noun is the pronoun of the matter and affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), which has been omitted, and the nominal clause after it is in the position of nominative as its khabar, as in the poet's words:
2573 - في فتية كسيوفِ الهند قد علموا ... أَنْ هالِكٌ كلُّ مَنْ يحفى ويَنْتَعِلُ
(Among young men like the swords of India, who have come to know that perishing is everyone who goes barefoot or wears sandals.)
And «أنْ» with its noun and khabar is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ. Al-Jurjānī claimed that «أَنْ» here is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being «وآخر دعواهم الحمد لله»; this is a claim for which there is no evidence, contrary to the explicit statement of Sībawayh and the grammarians. Al-Mubarrad also claimed that the lightened «أَنْ» may be made to govern while lightened, just as when doubled; this has already been discussed.
Lightening «أَنْ» and reading «الحمد» in the nominative is the reading of the generality. ʿIkrima, Abū Mijlaz, Abū Ḥaywa, Qatāda, Mujāhid, Ibn Yaʿmar, Bilāl ibn Abī Burda, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Yaʿqūb read it doubled, with the dāl of «الحمد» in the accusative as its noun. This supports that it is the lightened [«أنْ»] in the reading of the generality, and refutes al-Jurjānī.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ}: this [conditional of] impossibility is a negation in meaning, its implied form being: «لا يُعَجِّلُ لهم الشرَّ» (He does not hasten evil for them). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how are His words «فَنَذَرُ الذين لا يَرْجُون لقاءَنا» connected to it, and what is their meaning? I say: His words «ولو يُعَجِّل» contain the meaning of negating the hastening, as though it were said: «ولا نُعَجِّل لهم بالشرِّ ولا نَقْضي إليهم أجلَهم» (We do not hasten evil for them nor bring their term to an end)."
His words: {استعجالهم} — there are several views on it. First: it is accusative as a maṣdar of likening, its implied form being «استعجالاً مثلَ استعجالِهم» (a hastening like their seeking of haste); then the qualified noun «استعجال» was omitted and its adjective «مثل» put in its place, leaving «ولو يعجل اللَّهُ مثل استعجالِهم»; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. Makkī said: "This is the position of Sībawayh." I say: it has been stated more than once that Sībawayh's position in such cases is that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from that implied maṣdar, even if the well-known view of the parsers is otherwise; so attributing what I first mentioned to Sībawayh is open to question.
Second: its implied form is «تعجيلاً مثلَ استعجالهم» (a hastening like their seeking of haste), and then the same was done to it as [described] before. This is the implied form of Abū al-Baqāʾ: he made the omitted [maṣdar] correspond to the verb before it, for «تعجيلاً» is the maṣdar of «عَجَّل», while what Makkī mentioned corresponds to the maṣdar after it. What appears [correct] is what Abū al-Baqāʾ supposed, because corresponding to the verb is more appropriate, and He would then have likened His hastening, exalted is He, to their seeking of haste — unlike Makkī's implied form, which is not evident, since «استعجال» is not the maṣdar of «عجَّل».
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its origin is: «ولو يُعَجِّل الله للناسِ الشرَّ تعجيلَه لهم الخير» (if Allah were to hasten evil for people as He hastens good for them); then «استعجالهم بالخير» was put in the place of «تعجيله لهم الخيرَ» to convey the speed of His answering them and His granting of their request, as though their seeking haste for good were [itself] a hastening for them." Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What «عَجَّل» signifies is other than what «استعجل» signifies, because «عَجَّل» indicates occurrence while «استعجل» indicates seeking haste; the former comes from Allah and the latter is attributed to them; so the implied form cannot be as al-Zamakhsharī said. It admits two views. First: the implied form is «تعجيلاً مثل استعجالهم بالخير» (a hastening like their seeking haste for good), so the hastening is likened to the seeking of haste, because their seeking of good and the occurrence of its hastening take precedence for them over everything. Second: there is something omitted, indicated by the maṣdar, its implied form being: «ولو يعجِّل اللَّهُ للناسِ الشرَّ إذا استعجلوا به استعجالَهم بالخير» (if Allah were to hasten evil for people when they sought haste for it, as they seek haste for good), because they used to seek haste for evil and its occurrence by way of mockery, just as they sought haste for good." Third: it is accusative through the dropping of the kāf of likening, the implied form being «كاستعجالهم» (like their seeking of haste). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is far-fetched, since if that were permissible then «زيد غلامَ عمرو» would be permissible, meaning «كغلام عمرو» (like ʿAmr's servant)." On this basis a group declared it weak, but it is not a sound declaration of weakness, since in the example he gave there is no verb that becomes transitive by itself when the preposition is omitted, whereas in the verse there is a verb for which that is valid, namely His words «يُعَجِّل».
Makkī said: "Whoever allows the preposition to be omitted from it must allow «زيدُ الأسدُ», meaning «كالأسدِ» (like the lion)." I say: his words "must allow…" to the end contain no refutation of this proponent, since he accepts it, and it is a sound and acceptable consequence, since no one rejects «زيد الأسدُ» in the sense of «كالأسد»; and on the assumption of conceding [the objection], the difference is what Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned, i.e. that the verb calls for a maṣdar of likening, so it is indicated. Some said: its implied form is «في استعجالهم» (in their seeking of haste) — Makkī transmitted it — so when «في» was omitted it became accusative; this has no meaning.
His words: {لَقُضِي}: Ibn ʿĀmir read «لقضى» with fatḥa on the fāʾ and ʿayn [radicals], active, the agent being Allah the Exalted, with «أجلهم» in the accusative. The rest read «لقُضِيَ» with ḍamma and kasra, passive, with «أَجَلُهم» in the nominative because it stands in the place of the fāʿil [i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. Al-Aʿmash read «لقَضَيْنا», attributed to the pronoun of the One who magnifies Himself, and this supports the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir.
His words: {فَنَذَرُ} — there are three views on it. First: it is conjoined to His words {وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ الله}, in the sense that it has the force of a negation; the verification of that was given in al-Zamakhsharī's question and his answer to it. However, Abū al-Baqāʾ rejected its conjunction to «يُعَجِّل», saying: "It cannot be conjoined to «يُعَجِّل», since if it were, it would enter into the impossibility that «لو» entails, and that is not the case, because the hastening did not occur, whereas leaving them in their transgression did occur." I say: this refutation would only hold if it were conjoined to «يُعَجِّل» alone, retaining its meaning; but it has been stated that the speech has come to have the force of {لا نعجِّل لهم الشرَّ فَنَذَرُهم} (We do not hasten evil for them, so We leave them), so that «فَنَذَرُهم» is conjoined to the negative clause, not to the impossible verb alone, such that what he said would follow. Second: it is conjoined to an implied clause: «ولكن نُمْهِلُهم فَنَذَرُ» (but We grant them respite, so We leave…); Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. Third: it is a resumptive clause, i.e. «فنحن نَذَرُ الذين» (so We leave those who…); al-Ḥūfī said this.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لِجَنبِهِ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and that is why an explicit ḥāl was conjoined to it; the implied form is «دعانا مضطجعاً لجنبه» (he called upon Us lying on his side), or «مُلْقِياً لجَنْبه» (laid down on his side). The lām keeps its proper meaning according to the Basrans; some claimed that it has the meaning of «على» (on), but there is no need for that. There is disagreement about the possessor of the ḥāl (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl). It was said: it is «الإنسان», and what governs it is «مَسَّ»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted it from someone else and considered it weak on two grounds. First: on this view the ḥāl falls after the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا», and that is not the [proper] way. I say: it is as though he means that the condition should not be answered until it has taken all its governed elements, and this ḥāl is governed by the condition, namely «مَسَّ», yet it has been answered before taking its governed element. Then he said: "Second: the meaning is the frequency of his supplication in all his states, not that harm afflicts him in all his states; and many verses in the Quran come in accordance with this."
Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "On this second [objection], it follows from harm touching him in these states that he supplicates in these states, because it is the apodosis of [a protasis] in which these states were mentioned. [A restriction in the protasis is a restriction in the apodosis, as when you say «إذا جاءنا زيدٌ فقيراً فقد أَحْسَنَّا إليه» (if Zayd comes to us poor, we have been good to him); the meaning is:] we were good to him in the state of his poverty."
It was [also] said: the possessor of the ḥāl is the agent pronoun in «دعانا», and this is clear, i.e. he called upon Us in all his states, because a human being is never free of one of these three states. Then it was said: what is meant by «الإنسان» is the genus, and these states relate to the whole, i.e. among them are some who supplicate lying down and some who supplicate standing; or one individual may be meant, who combines these three states according to the times, supplicating at one time in this state and at another time in another.
His words: {كَأَن لَّمْ يَدْعُنَآ}: the discussion of the like of this was given at His words {كَأَنْ لَّمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكُمْ}. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "So the pronoun of the affair (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) was omitted, as in the poet's words:
2574 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كأنْ ثَدْياه حُقَّانِ
(…as though her breasts were two round caskets.)"
— that is, according to the version of those who transmit it «ثَدْيان» with alif [i.e. nominative]; it is also transmitted «كأنْ ثَدْيَيْه» with yāʾ, on the basis that it was made to govern an overt noun, and that is anomalous (shādhdh). The first half of this verse is:
وصَدْرٍ مُشْرقِ النَّحْرِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And a chest with a radiant throat…)
This clause of likening is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «مرَّ», i.e. he went on his way resembling one who had never called [Us] to remove harm. «مَسَّه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ضُرّ». The author of al-Naẓm said: "{وَإِذَا مَسَّ الإنسان} — its description is of the future, while «فلمَّا كشفنا» is of the past; this arrangement indicates that the meaning of the verse is that it was like this in the past and will be like this in what is to come, so the future verb in the verse indicates the future meaning it contains."
The kāf of «كذلك زُيِّن» is in the position of accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. like that adorning and turning away from earnest supplication. The omitted agent of «زُيِّن» is either Allah the Exalted or Satan. {مَا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ} is in the position of nominative because it stands in the place of the agent [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. «ما» may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) or have the meaning of «الذي» (that which).

semin-durr:13-13.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مِن قَبْلِكُمْ}: attached to «أَهْلكنا»; it cannot be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «القرون», because it is an adverb of time and so cannot be a ḥāl of a concrete entity, just as it cannot be a khabar (predicate) of one. The verification of this was given at the beginning of al-Baqara, and the discussion of «لمَّا» has also been given.
His words: {وَجَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُم} may be conjoined to «ظلموا», so that it has no grammatical position according to Sībawayh, while according to others its position is genitive, because it is conjoined to what is in the position of genitive through the adverb being annexed to it. It may also be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. they did wrong by denial while their messengers had come to them with the proofs and evidences of their truthfulness. «بالبينات» may be attached to «جاءتهم», or attached to something omitted as a ḥāl from «رسلهم», [i.e.] they came in conjunction with the clear proofs, accompanied by them.
His words: {وَمَا كَانُواْ}: the apparent view is that it is conjoined to «ظلموا». Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ); he said: "And the lām is to emphasize the negation of their believing." By parenthetical he means that it falls between the verb and its maṣdar of likening in His words «كذلك نَجزي». [Translator's note: the source has «فني إيمانهم», evidently a misprint for «نفي إيمانهم» (the negation of their believing); translated accordingly.] The pronoun in «كانوا» refers to «القرون». Muqātil allowed it to be the pronoun of the people of Mecca; on this view it is a shift (iltifāt), since there is a departure from the pronoun of address in His words «قبلكم» to the third person, the meaning being: «وما كنتم لتؤمنوا» (and you were not going to believe). «كذلك» is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. «مثلَ ذلك الجزاء نجزي» (with the like of that recompense We recompense). It was also read «يَجْزي» with the yāʾ of the third person, which is a shift from the first person in His words «أَهْلكنا» to the third person.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لِنَنظُرَ}: attached to the «جَعْل» (making). Yaḥyā al-Dhimārī read it with a single nūn and a doubled ẓāʾ [«لِنَظُّرَ»]. Yaḥyā said: "That is how I saw it in the Muṣḥaf of ʿUthmān," meaning that he saw it with a single nūn, not that he saw it doubled, because this particular vowel-marking only arose after ʿUthmān. They accounted for it as an assimilation (idghām) of the second nūn into the ẓāʾ, which is very poor; the best that can be said of it is that he went to an extreme in concealing the nasalization (ghunna) of the quiescent nūn, so the listener thought it an assimilation. His seeing it with a single nūn does not indicate that he read it with the ẓāʾ doubled or undoubled. Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Nor does it indicate the omission of the nūn from the pronunciation." There is some question about this, for how would he read what was not written in the Muṣḥaf that he saw?
His words: {كَيْفَ} is accusative through «تعملون» as a maṣdar, i.e. «أيَّ عملٍ تعملون» (what kind of work you do), and it suspends (muʿalliqa) [the operation of] «النظر» (seeing).

semin-durr:15-15.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَوْ بَدِّلْهُ}: the changing may be in the essence or in the attributes, i.e. put a verse of punishment in place of a verse of mercy. If it is said: on the first [interpretation] there is a repetition with His words {ائت بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هاذآ}, the answer is that the meaning of the first is: bring a Quran other than it while it remains, or change it by removing its essence altogether; so the two requests differ.
«تِلْقاء» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of the pattern «تِفْعال»; no maṣdar with kasra on the tāʾ has come except this and «التِّبْيان». It was read anomalously (shādhdh) with fatḥa on the tāʾ, which is the analogical form of maṣdars that indicate repetition, like «التَّطْواف» and «التَّجوال». «التِّلقاء» is sometimes used in the sense of «قبالتك» (facing you), and is then accusative in the manner of adverbs of place.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَلاَ أَدْرَاكُمْ بِهِ}: i.e. «ولا أَعْلمكم الله به» (nor would Allah have made it known to you), from «دَرَيْتُ», i.e. «علمتُ» (I knew). One says «دَرَيْتُ بكذا» and «أَدْرَيْتك بكذا», i.e. I encompassed it by way of knowledge (dirāya); likewise in «علمت به»: knowledge is made to include the meaning of encompassing, so it takes the same transitivity.
Ibn Kathīr — with a difference [in transmission] from al-Bazzī — read «ولأَدْراكم» with a lām prefixed to «أَدْراكم», affirmatively. The meaning is: and He would have made it known to you without my mediation, either through the mediation of an angel or of a messenger other than me from among mankind; but He singled me out for this distinction. In the reading of the majority, «لا» is emphatic, because what is conjoined to a negated [element] is negated; this «لا» is not the one by which the verb is negated, because negating the verb with it is not valid when it occurs as an apodosis, and what is conjoined to the apodosis is an apodosis. If you said «لو كان كذا لا كان كذا» it would not be permissible; rather you say «ما كان كذا». Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Sīrīn and Abū Rajāʾ read {ولا أَدْرَأْتُكم به} with a quiescent hamza after the rāʾ. There are two accounts of this reading. First: [the hamza] is substituted for an alif, and the alif is changed from a yāʾ because the letter before it has fatḥa; this is a dialect of ʿUqayl reported by Quṭrub: in «أعطيتك» they say «أعطأتك». Abū Ḥātim said: "Al-Ḥasan changed the yāʾ into alif, as in the dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith, who say «عَلاَك» and «إلاك», then put a hamza in it according to the dialect of those who say «العَأْلَم» for «العالم»." It was also said: rather the hamza was substituted for the yāʾ itself, as in «لَبَأْتُ بالحج» and «رثَأْت فلاناً», i.e. «لبَّيْتُ» and «رَثَيْتُ». Second: the hamza is original and its derivation is from «الدَّرْء», which is repelling, as in His words {وَيَدْرَؤُاْ عَنْهَا العذاب} [al-Nūr: 8]; one says «أَدْرأته», i.e. I made him a repeller, the meaning being: and I would have made you, by its recitation, adversaries who repel me with disputation. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it was said: it is a mistake, because its reader thought it was from «الدَّرْء», which is repelling. And it was said: it is not a mistake, and the meaning is: had Allah willed, He would have repelled you from believing in it."
Shahr ibn Ḥawshab and al-Aʿmash read «ولا أَنْذَرْتُكم» (nor would I have warned you), from «الإنذار» (warning), and that is how it is in the codex (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd].
The pronoun in «قبله» refers to the Quran; it was also said: to the revelation; and it was said: to the time of the revelation. «عُمُراً» is likened to an adverb of time, so it is accusative in the same way, i.e. a long period. It was also said: it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. «مقدار عُمُر» (the measure of a lifetime). Al-Aʿmash read «عُمْراً» with a quiescent mīm, as they say «عَضْد» for «عَضُد».

semin-durr:18-18.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مَا لاَ يَضُرُّهُمْ}: «ما» is a relative noun, or an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows], and it refers to the idols. That is why its form was observed, so it is singular in His words {مَا لاَ يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلاَ يَنفَعُهُمْ}, and its meaning [was observed], so it is plural in His words «هؤلاء شفعاؤنا».
His words: {أَتُنَبِّئُونَ}: some read «أتُنْبِئون», lightened, from «أنبأ»; one says «أنبأ» and «نبَّأ» (to inform), like «أخبرَ» and «خبَّر». His words: {بِمَا لاَ يَعْلَمُ}: «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي» (that which), or an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows], like the one before. On both views the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. «يعلمه» (He knows it). The agent is the pronoun of the Creator, exalted is He, and the meaning is: do you inform Allah of that which Allah does not know? And if Allah does not know a thing, the existence of that thing is impossible, because nothing escapes His knowledge, exalted is He. That thing is the intercession, so «ما» stands for the intercession.
The meaning is: had there been intercession, the Creator, exalted is He, would have known it. His words {فِي السماوات وَلاَ فِي الأرض} emphasize its negation, because nothing existent goes beyond them. «ما» may also stand for the idols, with the agent of «يعلمُ» a pronoun referring to them; the meaning is then: do you inform Allah about the idols, which know nothing in the heavens or on earth? And if it is established that they do not know, how could they intercede? An intercessor must know the one with whom intercession is made and the one for whom it is made. That is how al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] parsed it, making «ما» stand for the idols, not for the intercession; but the first is more evident. «ما» in «عَمَّا يشركون» may have the meaning of «الذي», i.e. above their partners whom they associate with Him in worship; or it may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. above their associating others with Him.
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read here «عَمَّا تُشْركون» [Translator's note: the source prints «يُشْركون» with yāʾ here, but the context — the reading in the second person contrasted with "the rest read in the third person" — shows that «تُشْركون» is meant], and in two places in al-Naḥl: the first {سُبْحَانَهُ وتعالى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ يُنَزِّلُ الملائكة} [verse 1], and the second {بالحق تعالى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ} [verse 3], and in al-Rūm {هَلْ مِن شُرَكَآئِكُمْ مَّن يَفْعَلُ مِن ذَلِكُمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ سُبْحَانَهُ وتعالى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ} [verse 40], with the second person of address. The rest read in the third person in all of them. Both the address and the third person are clear.
Here «يُشْركون» was brought in the imperfect rather than the past to draw attention to the continuity of their state, as they came worshipping, and also to draw attention to the fact that they will be upon associationism (shirk) in the future just as they were upon it in the past.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَإِذَآ أَذَقْنَا}: conditional; its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is the «إذا» of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya) in His words {إِذَا لَهُمْ مَّكْرٌ}, and what governs the «إذا» of surprise is the [notion of] settled being (istiqrār) contained in «لهم».
You have already had the disagreement about this «إذا»: is it a particle, an adverb of time in its proper sense, or an adverb of place? Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was said: the second «إذا» is also temporal, and the second and what follows it is the apodosis of the first." This view that he related is a worthless opinion whose meaning cannot be understood.
His words: {في آيَاتِنَا} are attached to «مَكْر»; He made the signs the locus of the scheming, for hyperbole. It is weak for the preposition-phrase to be a naʿt (adjective) of «مكر». His words «مكراً» are accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and it must be accusative, because if you formed a verb from «أَفْعل» and attributed it to its tamyīz as the agent, it would be valid to say «سَرُع مَكْرُه» (his scheming was swift); moreover, the condition for permitting the genitive is that the tamyīz applies to the thing qualified by the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), as in «زيدٌ أحسنُ فقيه» (Zayd is the best jurist). «أَسْرَعُ» is taken from the triliteral «سَرُع»; al-Fārisī reported this. It was also said: rather from «أسرع». Regarding forming the elative «أفعل» and the two verbs of wonder (taʿajjub) from «أفعل» there are three positions: permissibility absolutely, prohibition absolutely, and distinguishing: if the hamza is for making transitive it is forbidden, and if not it is permitted. The detailed treatment is in the books of the grammarians. Some said: "«أسرع» here is not for comparison (tafḍīl)," but this is nothing, since the context refutes it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it — I mean «أسرع» being for comparison — analogous to the saying «لهي أسودُ مِنَ القار» (it is blacker than pitch). Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "As for his making «أسود من القار» analogous to «أسرع», it is unsound, because the verb of «أسود» is not of the pattern «أَفْعَل»; it is of the pattern «فَعِل», as in «سَوِدَ فهو أسود». Wonder and the formation of the elative from the likes of «سَوِدَ», «حَمِرَ» and «أَدِمَ» are forbidden among the Basrans only because they are colours. Some Kufans allowed that for colours absolutely, and some for black and white only." I say: his analogy with it is not unsound, because what he means is forming «أفعل» from what exceeds three letters, even if it is not of the pattern «أَفْعَل»; and «سَوِد», though triliteral, has the meaning of what exceeds three letters, since it means «اسودَّ», and «حَمِرَ» means «احمرَّ». The grammarians stated this explicitly and made it the cause preventing wonder in colours. [Translator's note: the source prints «في معنى أسود ... في معنى أحمر»; given the argument, the intended forms are presumably the augmented verbs «اسودّ / احمرّ»; translated accordingly.]
Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Mujāhid, al-Aʿraj, and Nāfiʿ in one transmission read «يَمْكرون» with the yāʾ of the third person, in accordance with what preceded. The rest read in the second person of address, to emphasize the notification of their scheming, and as a shift (iltifāt) connected with His words «قل الله», since the implied form is «قل لهم» (say to them), so the address is fitting. In His words «إنْ رسلَنا» there is also a shift, since had it followed His words «قل الله», it would have said «إنَّ رسله» (His messengers).

semin-durr:22-22.t:
The words of the Exalted: {يُسَيِّرُكُمْ}: the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir is from «النَّشْر» (spreading out), the opposite of folding, the meaning being: He disperses and spreads you. [Translator's note: the source omits the wording of Ibn ʿĀmir's reading; it is «يَنْشُرُكم».] Al-Ḥasan read «يُنْشِركم» from «أَنْشَر», i.e. to bring to life, and that is also the reading of Ibn Masʿūd. Some of the Syrians read «يُنْشِّركم» with doubling, for multiplicity, from «النَّشْر», which is the reflexive counterpart of «الانتشار». The rest read «يُسَيِّركم» from «التَّسْيير»; the doubling in it is for making transitive: you say «سار الرجل» (the man travelled) and «سَيَّرْتُه أنا» (I made him travel). Al-Fārisī said: "It is a doubling of intensification, not a doubling of making transitive, because the Arabs say «سِرْتُ الرجلَ» and «سيَّرته»," and from it are the words of al-Hudhalī:
2575 - فلا تجزعَنْ مِنْ سُنَّةٍ أنت سِرْتها ... فأولُ راضٍ سنةٍ مَنْ يَسِيْرُها
(Do not be distressed at a custom which you yourself set going; the first to accept a custom is the one who sets it going.)
What Abū ʿAlī said is not evident, because the more common usage in the language of the Arabs is that «سار» is intransitive, so taking the doubled form from the more common [usage] is more appropriate. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "There is an objection to this verse, so that it is not evidence for this, namely that the pronoun may be like an adverb, just as you say «سِرْتُ الطريق» (I travelled the road)." Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "As for Ibn ʿAṭiyya's making the pronoun like an adverb, as when you say «سِرْتُ الطريقَ», this is not permissible according to the majority, because «الطريق» for them is a specific adverb like «الدار», which the verb does not reach — other than «دخلت» according to Sībawayh, and «انطلقت» and «ذهبت» according to al-Farrāʾ — except through «في», save in poetic necessity. And if that is so, then its pronoun is even more appropriately not reached by the verb directly." Ibn al-Ṭarāwa claimed that «الطريق» is a non-specific adverb, so the verb reaches it by itself, but the grammarians rejected that.
His words: {حتى إِذَا}: «حتى» is attached to «يُسَيِّركم». The discussion of this «حتى» that enters upon «إذا», and what was said about it, has been given. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "[If you say:] how did He make being in the ships the limit of travelling on the sea, when travelling on the sea is only by being in the ships? I say: He did not make being in the ships the limit of the travelling; rather [the limit is] the content of the conditional clause falling after «حتى» with all that is within its scope, as though He said: He makes you travel until, when this event occurs and such-and-such takes place — the coming of the stormy wind, the piling up of the waves, the expectation of destruction and the supplication for rescue."
Abū al-Dardāʾ and Umm al-Dardāʾ read «في الفُلْكيّ» with the yāʾ of relation (nisba). Its account admits two views. First: what is meant by it is the deep, abundant water in which alone ships sail, as though it were said «كنتم في اللُّجِّ الفُلْكِيِّ» (you were in the ship-bearing deep), and the pronoun in «جَرَيْنَ» refers to the ships because «الفلكي» indicates them both verbally and by implication. Second: it is a case of relating [a noun] to an adjective, as in their saying «أَحْمَريّ», as in the poet's words:
2576 - أَطَرَباً وأنت قِنَّسْرِيُّ ... والدهرُ بالإِنسان دوَّارِيُّ
(Do you yearn, when you are old and hardened, while time keeps turning upon man?)
and like their relating to a proper name in their saying «الصَّلَتَانيّ», as in the poet's words:
2577 - أَنَا الصَّلَتَانِيُّ الذي قد عَلِمْتُمُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I am al-Ṣalatānī, the one you have come to know…)
— so he added the two yāʾs of relation to his name.
His words: {وَجَرَيْنَ} may be conjoined to «كنتم», or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) with «قد» implied. The pronoun refers to «الفلك», and what is meant by it here is the plural. It has been stated that it is a broken plural, that its change [of form] is notional, so that its ḍamma is like the ḍamma of «بُدْن», and that it is not a collective noun (ism jamʿ), as al-Akhfash claimed.
His words: {بِهِم} contain a shift (iltifāt) from the second person to the third. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the benefit of turning the speech from address to the third person? I say: hyperbole, as though He were relating their state to others, to make them wonder at it and to call forth from them disapproval and condemnation." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«بهم» is a departure from address to the third person, and that is good because His words {كُنتُمْ فِي الفلك} are in the understood sense: until, when some of you are in the ships." End of quotation. So he supposed an absent noun — that omitted muḍāf — to which the third-person pronoun refers; and the like of it is {أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ} [al-Nūr: 40], its implied form being «أو كذي ظلمات» (or like one in darkness). On this view it is not a shift at all. Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What appears is that the wisdom of the shift here is that His words {هُوَ الذي يُسَيِّرُكُمْ} are an address containing a reminder of favour and a display of blessing to those addressed; those made to travel by land and sea are believers and unbelievers, and the address is comprehensive, so it was good to address them with it so that the righteous might persist in gratitude and the wicked might perhaps remember this blessing. And since at the end of the verse there is what entails that when they are saved they transgress in the land, He turned away from addressing them with that to the third person, so as not to address the believers with what is not fitting to come from them, namely transgression without right."
His words: {بِرِيحٍ} are attached to «جَرَيْنَ». It may be asked: how can one verb take two governed elements through a preposition identical in form and meaning? The answer is that the first bāʾ is for making transitive, as in «مررت بزيد» (I passed by Zayd), and the second is causal, so the two meanings differ; that is why both are attached to one governor. The second bāʾ may also be for the ḥāl, so that it is attached to something omitted, the implied form being «جَرَيْنَ بهم ملتبسةً بريح» (they sailed with them in conjunction with a wind), the ḥāl then being from the pronoun of the ships.
His words: {وَفَرِحُواْ بِهَا}: this clause may be conjoined to «جَرَيْنَ», or be a ḥāl, with «قد» implied with it according to some, i.e. «وقد فَرِحوا» (having rejoiced); the possessor of the ḥāl is the pronoun in «بهم».
His words: {جَآءَتْهَا}: the apparent view is that this verbal clause is the apodosis of «إذا», and that the pronoun in «جاءَتْها» is the pronoun of the good wind, i.e. a stormy wind came to the good wind, i.e. it succeeded it. Al-Zamakhsharī began with this, and al-Farrāʾ preceded him in it. He allowed the pronoun to be for the ships, and preferred this on the grounds that the ships are what is being spoken about. [Translator's note: the source does not make clear whether "he allowed… and preferred" refers to al-Zamakhsharī or al-Farrāʾ.]
His words: {وظنوا} may be conjoined to «جاءتها», which is the apodosis of «إذا»; or it may be conjoined to «كنتم», and that is the view of al-Ṭabarī, which is why he said: "«وظنُّوا» — its apodosis is «دَعَوا الله»."
Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Its apparent [sense] is conjunction to the apodosis of «إذا», not that it is conjoined to «كنتم»; but it is possible, as when you say «إذا زارك فلانٌ فأكرمه، وجاءك خالد فأحسِنْ إليه» (if so-and-so visits you, honour him; and [if] Khālid comes to you, be good to him), as though the conditional particle were mentioned." Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «حِيط», triliteral.
His words: {دَعَوُاْ الله}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is the apodosis of the conditional sense contained in the meaning, its implied form being: «لما ظَنُّوا أنهم أُحيط بهم دَعَوُا الله» (when they thought they were encompassed, they called upon Allah)." This is empty talk. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a badal (substitute) from «ظنُّوا», because their supplication is one of the concomitants of their expecting destruction, so it is bound up with it." Al-Shaykh transmitted from his teacher Abū Jaʿfar that it is an answer to an implied question, as though it were said: "So what was their state at that time?" and it was said: "They called upon Allah." «مخلصين» is a ḥāl, «له» is attached to it, and «الدين» is its object.
His words: {لَئِنْ أَنْجَيْتَنَا}: the lām is the one that paves the way (al-muwaṭṭiʾa) for the omitted oath, and «لنكونَنَّ» is its apodosis; the oath and its apodosis are in the position of accusative through an implied verb of saying, and that implied saying is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, the implied form being: «دَعَوا قائلين: لئن أَنْجَيْتنا من هذه لنكوننَّ» (they called, saying: if You save us from this, we shall surely be…). It is also possible for «دَعَوا» to be treated like «قالوا» (they said), because supplication has the meaning of saying, since it is one of its kinds; this is a Kufan position.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِذَا هُمْ يَبْغُونَ}: the apodosis (jawāb) of «لمَّا»; it is the «إذا» of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya). His words «بغير الحق» are a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. in conjunction with what is other than the truth. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of His words «بغير الحق», when transgression (baghy) is never with right? I say: yes [it can be], namely the Muslims' taking possession of the land of the unbelievers, demolishing their houses, burning their crops and cutting down their trees, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did with Banū Qurayẓa." He had explained «البغي» as corruption and going to excess in it, from «بغى الجرحُ» — said when a wound spreads into corruption. That is why al-Zajjāj said: "It is rising [by degrees] in corruption," and al-Aṣmaʿī also said: "«بغى الجرحُ»: it rose towards corruption; and «بَغَت المرأة»: she was licentious." Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It is not valid to say of the Muslims that they transgress against the unbelievers, unless it is mentioned that the origin of «البغي» is seeking in an absolute sense and does not include corruption; then it divides into seeking with right and seeking without right." [Translator's note: the source has «صلَ البغي», evidently a misprint for «أصلَ البغي» (the origin of baghy); translated accordingly.] I say: it has been stated that this verse refutes al-Fārisī['s view] that «لمَّا» is an adverb meaning «حين» (when), because what follows the «إذا» of surprise does not govern what precedes it; and since he assumed «لمَّا» to be an adverb, it necessarily must have a governor.
His words: {مَّتَاعَ الحياة}: Ḥafṣ read «متاعَ» in the accusative, and its accusative is on five views. First: it is accusative as an adverb of time, like «مَقْدَم الحاج» (the arrival of the pilgrims), i.e. the time of the enjoyment of life. Second: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. «مُتَمتعين» (enjoying). What governs this adverb and this ḥāl is the [notion of] settled being (istiqrār) in the khabar (predicate), which is «عليكم». They cannot both be accusative through the maṣdar [«بغيكم»], because that would entail separating the maṣdar from its governed element by the khabar, and it has been stated that nothing is predicated of a relative [element] until its ṣila (relative clause) is complete. Third: it is accusative as an emphasizing maṣdar through an implied verb, i.e. «يتمتعون متاع الحياة» (they enjoy the enjoyment of life). Fourth: it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) through an implied verb indicated by the maṣdar, i.e. «يبغون متاعَ الحياة» (they seek the enjoyment of life); it cannot be accusative through the maṣdar, for the reason already given. Fifth: it is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of enjoyment; what governs it is either the istiqrār implied in «عليكم» or an implied verb. It is also possible that what governs it — when it is taken as an adverb, a ḥāl, or an object of purpose — is the transgression (baghy) itself, not by making «على أنفسكم» the khabar, but by making it attached to the baghy itself, with the khabar omitted because of the length of the speech, the implied form being: «إنما بَغْيُكم على أنفسكم متاعَ الحياة مذمومٌ أو مكروهٌ أو منهيٌّ عنه» (your transgression against yourselves for the enjoyment of life is blameworthy, or detestable, or forbidden).
The rest of the Seven read «متاعُ» in the nominative. There are several views on it. First, and it is the most evident: it is the khabar of «بَغْيكم», and «على أنفسِكم» is attached to the baghy.
It is possible that «عليكم» is the khabar and «متاع» a second khabar; and it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هو متاع» (it is an enjoyment). The meaning of «على أنفسكم» is: against some of you and your own kind, as in His words {وَلاَ تقتلوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 29] and {وَلاَ تلمزوا أَنفُسَكُمْ} [al-Ḥujurāt: 11]; or the meaning is: the evil consequence of transgression returns upon you and does not go beyond you, as in His words {وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا} [al-Isrāʾ: 7] and {وَمَنْ أَسَآءَ فَعَلَيْهَا} [Fuṣṣilat: 46].
Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «متاعاً الحياة» with «متاعاً» and «الحياةَ» in the accusative. «متاعاً» is as already stated. As for «الحياة», it may be a direct object, governed by the maṣdar; in that case «متاعاً» cannot be an emphasizing maṣdar, because the emphasizing [maṣdar] does not govern. «الحياة» may also be accusative as a badal (substitute) from «متاعاً», because it contains it [i.e. a badal of inclusion].
It was also read «متاعِ الحياة» with «متاع» in the genitive, and this was accounted for as a naʿt (adjective) of «أنفسكم»; in that case a muḍāf must be omitted, the implied form being «على أنفسكم ذواتِ متاع الحياة» (against yourselves, possessors of the enjoyment of life) — so some accounted for it. It may also be a case in which the preposition is omitted while its governing effect remains, i.e. «إنما بَغْيُكم على أنفسِكم لأجِل متاع» (your transgression against yourselves is for the sake of enjoyment); this is supported by the accusative reading on the view of those who make it an object of purpose. Omitting the preposition while keeping its governing effect is rare, and this reading is not far from it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The maṣdar may have the meaning of the active participle, i.e. «متمتعات» (enjoying)," meaning that he makes the maṣdar a naʿt of «أنفسكم» without omitting a muḍāf, either by way of hyperbole or by giving the maṣdar the meaning of the active participle. Then he said: "It is weak for it to be a badal, since it is possible to make it an adjective." I say: if it is made a badal, despite its weakness, of which type of badal is it to be made? What appears is that it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), and in that case an omitted pronoun is necessary, i.e. «متاع الحياة الدنيا لها» (the enjoyment of the life of this world [belonging] to them).
It was also read «فيُنَبِّئَكُم» with the yāʾ of the third person, the agent being the pronoun of the Creator, exalted is He.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ}: this clause is presented to liken this world to the vegetation of the earth, and Allah the Exalted has explained the point of resemblance by what He mentioned. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is a compound simile (tashbīh murakkab): the state of this world, in the speed of its passing and the extinction of its pleasures after their approach, is likened to the state of the vegetation of the earth in its drying up and going to stubble after it had become dense and thick and adorned the earth with its greenness and luxuriance." I say: the compound simile in the terminology of the rhetoricians (al-bayāniyyūn) is either one whose two terms are both compound, i.e. likening a compound to a compound, as in the words of Bashshār ibn Burd:
2578 - كان مُثَارَ النَّقْعِ فوقَ رؤوسنا ... وأسيافَنا ليلٌ تهاوى كواكبُهْ
(As though the dust raised above our heads, and our swords, were a night whose stars are falling.)
— for he likens the configuration resulting from the falling of radiant, elongated bodies of proportionate size scattered through the sides of something dark, to a night whose stars have fallen; or one whose two terms differ in being single and compound. Its divisions are [treated] elsewhere.
His words: {كَمَآءٍ} are the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject); «أنزلناه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ماء», and «من السماء» is attached to «أَنْزلناه»; it is weak to make it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the accusative pronoun. His words «فاختلطَ به»: there are two views on this bāʾ. First: it is causal. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "So it intertwined because of it until parts of it mingled with others." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "A group connected «النبات» to His words «فاختلط», i.e. the plants mingled with one another because of the water." Second: it is for accompaniment, in the sense that the water functions as nourishment for it, so it accompanies it. Some claimed that the pause is at His words «فاختلط», the verb [containing] a pronoun referring to the water, and that one begins {بِهِ نَبَاتُ الأرض} as mubtadaʾ and khabar; on this view the pronoun in «به» may refer to the water, or to the mingling contained in the verb; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Pausing at His words «فاختلط» is not permissible, especially in the Quran, because it is a dismantling of the sound, connected speech and the eloquent meaning, and a resort to riddling and convolution."
His words: {مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ}: there are two views. First: it is attached to «اختلط»; al-Ḥūfī held this. Second: it is a ḥāl from «النبات»; Abū al-Baqāʾ held this, and it is the apparent view; what governs it is omitted according to the established rule, i.e. «كائناً أو مستقراً ممَّا يأكل» (being, or settled, among what [people and cattle] eat). If it were said that «مِنْ» is for explaining the genus, that would be permissible. His words «حتى» express a limit, so there must be something whose limit it is; and the verb before it, «اختلط», is not suitable to be that, because of the shortness of its duration.
So it was said: there is an omitted verb, i.e. the plants continued to grow until such-and-such happened. It was also said: «فاختلط» is used loosely, meaning: its mingling continued until such-and-such happened. «إذا» after this «حتى» has been commented upon before.
His words: {وازينت}: the majority read «ازَّيَّنَتْ» with the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) and doubled zāy and yāʾ. The origin is «وتَزَيَّنت»; when it was intended to assimilate the tāʾ into the zāy after it, it was changed into zāy and made quiescent, and the connecting hamza was brought in because beginning with a quiescent letter is impossible, so it became «ازَّيَّنت» as you see. The detailed treatment of this was given at the words of the Exalted {فادارأتم فِيهَا} [al-Baqara: 72]. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Aʿmash read «وتَزَيَّنَتْ» on the pattern «تَفَعَّلَتْ», which is the origin referred to. Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, al-Sulamī, Ibn Yaʿmar, al-Ḥasan, al-Shaʿbī, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, Ibn Hurmuz and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read «وأَزْيَنَتْ» on the pattern «أَفْعلَتْ»; «أفْعَل» here means "came to possess such-and-such," as in «أَحْصَدَ الزرعُ» (the crop became ready for harvest) and «أَغَدَّ البعيرُ» (the camel developed a gland swelling); the meaning is: it came to possess adornment, i.e. its adornment arrived and its time came. On this reading the yāʾ ought by right to have been changed into alif, so that one would say «أَزَانَتْ», like «أَنَابت»: it would be weakened by transferring its vowel to the quiescent letter before it, so that letter then becomes vowelled and what precedes [the yāʾ] has fatḥa, so it is changed into alif, as was stated in the likes of «أقام» and «أناب». However, it remained sound anomalously, as in their saying «أَغْيَمت السماء» (the sky became cloudy) and «أَغْيَلَت المرأة» (the woman nursed while pregnant). That has occurred in the Quran, as in {استحوذ} [al-Mujādila: 19], whose analogical form is «استحاذ», like «استقام».
Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī read — and Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributed it to an unspecified group — «وازْيَأَنَّتْ», with a connecting hamza followed by a quiescent zāy, then a light yāʾ with fatḥa, then a hamza with fatḥa, then a doubled nūn. They said: its origin is «وازيانَّتْ», on the pattern «احْمَارَّت», with an explicit alif; but they disliked combining two quiescent letters, so the alif was changed into a hamza, as in the reading «الضألّين» and «جَأَنّ». On this is their saying «احمأرَّت» with hamza, and [the poet] recited:
2579 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... إذا ما الهَواديْ بالعَبيطِ احمأرَّتِ
(…when the [horses'] necks became red with fresh blood.)
You have had this fully treated at the end of al-Fātiḥa. The teachers of ʿAwf ibn Abī Jamīla read «وازْيأنَّتْ» with the origin referred to, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributed it to Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī. [Translator's note: as printed, this form is identical to the one just described; the "origin referred to" would be «وازْيانَّتْ» with alif, which is probably what is intended here.] It was also read «وازَّايَنَتْ», the origin being «تزاينت», which was then assimilated.
His words: {أَهْلُهَآ}, i.e. the owners of its vegetation. «أتاها» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا», so it is what governs it. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the adornment; and it was said: to the produce, i.e. the provision, in which case there is no omission.
«ليلاً ونهاراً» are two adverbs of the coming or of the command. The «جَعْل» here is transforming (taṣyīr). «حصيد» is «فعيل» with the meaning of «مفعول» (passive participle); that is why it does not take the feminine tāʾ even though it refers to a feminine, as in their saying «امرأة جريح» (a wounded woman).
His words: {كَأَن لَّمْ تَغْنَ}: this clause may be a ḥāl from the first object of «جَعَلْناها», or resumptive, as an answer to an implied question. Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam read «تتغَنَّ» with two tāʾs, on the measure «تتفعَّل», and like it are the words of al-Aʿshā:
2580 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... طويلَ الثَّواءِ طويلَ التَّغَنّ
(…long in staying, long in dwelling.)
It means residing; its verification was given in al-Aʿrāf. Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read {كأن لم يَغْنَ} with the yāʾ of the third person. On this pronoun there are three views. The best is that it refers to «الحصيد», because it is the nearest thing mentioned. It was also said: it refers to «الزخرف» (the adornment), i.e. as though the adornment had not stood. And it was said: it refers to the vegetation or the crop that you supposed as a muḍāf, i.e. as though its crop and vegetation had not flourished.
By «بالأمس» what is meant is past time, not the day before your day, so it is like the words of Zuhayr:
2581 - وأعلمُ علمَ اليومِ والأمسِ قبلَه ... ولكنني عن عِلْمِ ما في غدٍ عَمِ
(I know the knowledge of today and of yesterday before it, but to the knowledge of what is in tomorrow I am blind.)
He did not intend their literal senses. The difference between the two «أمس» is that the one meaning the day before your day is indeclinable (mabnī), because it includes the meaning of the definite article, while this one is declinable, takes the article, and is annexed.
His words: {كذلك نُفَصِّلُ} is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. like this detailing that We have detailed in the past, We detail in the future.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَلاَ يَرْهَقُ}: there are three views on it. First: it is resumptive. Second: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs this ḥāl is the [notion of] settled being (istiqrār) contained in the preposition-phrase «للذين», since it serves as the khabar (predicate) of «الحسنى»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and he gave its implied form as «استقرَّ لهم الحسنى مضموماً لهم السَّلامة» (the best is settled for them, with safety added for them). This is not permissible, because whenever the imperfect occurs as a ḥāl negated by «لا», the wāw of the ḥāl cannot enter upon it, just as with the affirmative; and if something occurs that suggests that, it is interpreted by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject). Its verification has been given more than once. Third: it is in the position of nominative, conjoined to «الحسنى»; in that case a maṣdar-forming particle must be implied, with which it can validly be made something of which the preposition-phrase is predicated, the implied form being «للذين أحسنوا الحسنى، وأنْ لا يرهق» (for those who do good is the best, and that [dust] shall not cover…), i.e. «وعدم رَهَقِهم» (and their not being covered). When «أن» was omitted, the imperfect verb became nominative, because this is not one of the places where «أنْ» is implied as governing the subjunctive. This is like the words of the Exalted {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ} [al-Rūm: 24], i.e. «أن يُرِيَكم» (that He shows you), and the saying «تَسْمع بالمُعَيْدِيّ خيرٌ من أن تراه» (that you hear of al-Muʿaydī is better than that you see him), and the poet's words:
2582 - ألا أيُّهذا الزاجري أحضرُ الوَغَى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O you who rebuke me that I attend the battle…)
— i.e. «أن أحضر» (that I attend); it is transmitted with «أحضر» in the nominative and in the subjunctive. Abū al-Baqāʾ rejected this view, saying: "It cannot be conjoined to «الحسنى», because when a verb is conjoined to a maṣdar it needs «أَنْ», either stated or implied, and «أنْ» is not implied, because the verb is nominative." His statement "«أنْ» is not implied, because the verb is nominative" is not good, because in the words of the Exalted {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ} [al-Rūm: 24] «أنْ» is implied, even though it is nominative. Implying «أنْ» does not entail the subjunctive of the imperfect; rather the well-known [rule] is that when «أن» is implied in places other than those in which the grammarians stated it is implied as a subjunctive governor, the verb is nominative, and the subjunctive is very rare.
«الرَّهَق» is covering. One says «رَهِقَه يَرْهَقُه رَهَقا», i.e. it covered him quickly; from it are {وَلاَ تُرْهِقْنِي مِنْ أَمْرِي} [al-Kahf: 73] [Translator's note: the source prints [al-Kahf: 37]; the verse is al-Kahf 73] and {فَلاَ يَخَافُ بَخْساً وَلاَ رَهَقاً} [al-Jinn: 13]. One says «رَهِقْتُه» and «أَرْهَقْتُه», like «رَدِفْتُه» and «أَرْدَفْتُه», so «فَعَل» and «أَفْعل» have the same meaning; from it is «أَرْهَقْت الصلاةَ», when you delay it until the time of the next one comes upon it, and «رجلٌ مُرْهَق», i.e. one whom guests come upon. Al-Azharī said: "«الرَّهَق» is a noun from «الإِرهاق», which is that a person burdens himself with what he cannot bear"; and one says «أَرْهَقْتُه عن الصلاة», i.e. I hurried him away from it. Some said: the origin of «الرَّهَق» is approaching; from it is «غلامٌ مراهِق», i.e. [a boy] close to puberty; and in the ḥadīth: «ارهَقُوا القِبلة», i.e. come close to it; and from it is «رَهِقَتِ الكلابُ الصيدَ», i.e. the dogs caught up with the game.
«القَتَر» and «القَتَرة» are dust with blackness in it, and they recited [the verse] of al-Farazdaq:
2583 - مُتَوَّجٌ برِداء المُلك يَتْبَعُه ... موجٌ ترى فوقه الراياتِ والقترا
(Crowned with the mantle of kingship, a surging host follows him, above which you see the banners and the dust.)
— i.e. the dust of the army. It was also said: «القَتَر» is smoke, and from it is «قُتار القِدْر» (the smell of the cooking-pot). It was also said: «القَتْر» is diminishing, and from it is {لَمْ يُسْرِفُواْ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُواْ} [al-Furqān: 67]; one says «قَتَرْتُ الشيء» and «أَقْتَرْتُه» and «قتَّرته», i.e. I diminished it; and from it is {وَعَلَى المقتر قَدَرُهُ} [al-Baqara: 236], which has been discussed. «القُتْرَةُ» is the hunter's hide; it was also said: the pit, and from it are the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:
2584 - رُبَّ رامٍ من بني ثُعَلٍ ... مُتْلِجٍ كَفَّيْهِ في قُتَرِهْ
(Many an archer of Banū Thuʿal, thrusting his hands into his hide…)
— i.e. in his pit that he digs. Al-Ḥasan, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, Abū Rajāʾ and al-Aʿmash read «قَتْرٌ» with a quiescent tāʾ; they are two dialectal forms, «قَتْر» and «قَتَر», like «قَدْر» and «قَدَر».

semin-durr:27-27.t:
The words of the Exalted: {والذين كَسَبُواْ}: there are seven views on it. First: «والذين» is conjoined to «للذين أحسنوا», i.e. for those who do good is the best, and for those who earn evil deeds is the recompense of an evil deed with its like; so the division is balanced, as when you say «في الدار زيدٌ والحجرةِ عمروٌ» (in the house is Zayd, and in the room ʿAmr). The grammarians call this conjunction to the governed elements of two governors. There are three positions on it. First: permissibility absolutely, and that is the view of al-Farrāʾ. Second: prohibition absolutely, and that is the position of Sībawayh. Third: distinguishing: if the preposition-phrase comes first, as in «في الدار زيد والحجرةِ عمرو», it is permissible; if not, it is forbidden, as in «إن زيداً في الدار وعمراً القصر», i.e. «وإن عمراً في القصر» (and ʿAmr is in the palace). Sībawayh and his followers account for what has occurred of it by implying the preposition, as in the words of the Exalted {واختلاف الليل والنهار ... لآيَاتٍ} [al-Jāthiya: 5] with «آيات» in the accusative in the reading of the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], as will come, and as in the poet's words:
2585 - أكلَّ امرىءٍ تحسبين امرأً ... ونارٍ توقَّدُ بالليل نارا
(Do you consider every male a [true] man, and every fire kindled at night a [hospitable] fire?)
and the words of the other:
2586 - أَوْصَيْتَ مَنْ تَوَّه قلباً حُرَّاً ... بالكلبِ خيراً والحماةِ شَرَّا
(You enjoined on one whose noble heart you led astray good towards the dog and evil towards the mother-in-law.)
Further explanation of this will come in the course of this work. Among those who held that this relative noun is genitive, conjoined to the relative noun before it, are Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī. Second: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «جزاء سيئة» a second mubtadaʾ, and its khabar (predicate) is «بمثلها», the bāʾ in it being redundant (zāʾida), i.e. «وجزاءُ سيئةٍ مثلها» (and the recompense of an evil deed is its like), as in the words of the Exalted {وَجَزَآءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِّثْلُهَا} [al-Shūrā: 40] — just as it has been added in the khabar in the poet's words:
2587 - فلا تطمعْ أبيت اللعنَ - فيها ... ومَنْعُكها بشيءٍ يُسْتطاع
(Do not covet her — may you refuse the curse — for your withholding her is something attainable.)
i.e. «شيء يستطاع», and as in the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:
2588 - فإن تَنْأَ عنها حقبةً لا تلاقِها ... فإنَّك ممَّا أَحْدَثْتَ بالمجرِّب
(If you stay far from her for a long time without meeting her, then, by what you have caused, you are one who has been tried.)
— i.e. «المجرِّب». This is the view of Ibn Kaysān on the verse. Third: the bāʾ is not redundant, and the implied form is «مُقَدَّر بمثلها» (measured by its like) or «مستقر بمثلها» (settled with its like); the second mubtadaʾ and its khabar are the khabar of the first. Fourth: the khabar of «جزاء سيئة» is omitted. Al-Ḥūfī gave its implied form as «لهم جزاء سيئة» (for them is the recompense of an evil deed); he said: the implied «لهم» is indicated by His words {لِّلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ الحسنى}, so that this one matches that one. Abū al-Baqāʾ gave its implied form as «جزاء سيئة بمثلها واقع» (the recompense of an evil deed with its like is occurring), it with its khabar likewise being the khabar of the first. On these two implied forms the bāʾ is attached to «جزاء» itself, because this root takes its object with bāʾ; the Exalted said {جَزَيْنَاهُمْ بِمَا كَفَرُواْ} [Sabaʾ: 17] and {وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ} [al-Insān: 12], among others. If you say: where is the linking element between this clause and the relative noun that is the mubtadaʾ? I say: on al-Ḥūfī's implied form it is the pronoun made genitive by the lām implied as khabar; and on Abū al-Baqāʾ's implied form it is omitted, its implied form being «جزاءُ سيئة بمثلها منهم واقعٌ» (the recompense of an evil deed with its like, from them, is occurring), as in «السَّمْن مَنَوان بدرهم» (butter: two manns [of it] for a dirham). This is a regular omission, as you have learned more than once. [Translator's note: in the source the clause "and on Abū al-Baqāʾ's implied form it is the pronoun made genitive by the lām implied as khabar" appears a second time before the final clause — evidently a copyist's repetition; it is not repeated here.]
Fifth: the khabar is the negative clause in His words {مَّا لَهُمْ مِّنَ الله مِنْ عَاصِمٍ}; «مِنْ عاصم» is then either the fāʿil (agent) of the preposition-phrase before it, because it relies on the negation, or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the preposition-phrase placed before it; «مِنْ» is redundant in it on both views.
«من الله» is attached to «عاصم». If this clause is the khabar of the relative noun, then the mubtadaʾ and its khabar have been separated by two parenthetical clauses; there is a disagreement on that from al-Fārisī, to which attention has been drawn, together with what he adduced for it.
Sixth: the khabar is the clause of likening in His words {كَأَنَّمَا أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ}; «كأنما» is a restrained particle (makfūf), and this «ما» is redundant, called the restraining and preparing [mā] (kāffa wa-muhayyiʾa), as has been discussed. On this view the mubtadaʾ and its khabar are separated by three parenthetical clauses.
Seventh: the khabar is the clause in His words {أولئك أَصْحَابُ النار}; on this view [the mubtadaʾ and khabar] are separated by four parenthetical clauses, namely: {جَزَآءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِهَا}; the second «وتَرْهَقُهم ذلة»; the third {مَّا لَهُمْ مِّنَ الله مِنْ عَاصِمٍ}; the fourth «كأنما أُغْشيت». Separation by three clauses ought not to be permitted, let alone four.
His words: {وَتَرْهَقُهُمْ}: there are two views. First: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū al-Baqāʾ did not specify its possessor; its possessor is the relative noun or its pronoun. There is weakness in it because it is directly preceded by the wāw, unless it is made the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. Second: it is conjoined to «كسبوا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "That is weak, because a future [verb] is not conjoined to a past one; and if it is said that it has the meaning of the past, that is very weak." It was also read «ويَرْهقهم» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, because its feminine gender is figurative.
His words: {قِطَعاً}: Ibn Kathīr and al-Kisāʾī read «قِطْعاً» with a quiescent ṭāʾ, and the rest read it with fatḥa. As for the first reading, people's expressions about it differ. The lexicographers said: «القِطْع» is the darkness at the end of the night. Al-Akhfash said on His words «بقِطْع من الليل»: with a blackness of the night. Some said: a portion of the night. Al-Akhfash recited:
2589 - افتحي الباب فانظري في النجومِ ... كم علينا من قِطْعِ ليلٍ بَهيم
(Open the door and look at the stars: how much of the dark night's last part remains over us?)
As for the reading of the rest, it is the plural of «قِطْعة», like «دِمْنة / دِمَن» and «كِسْرة / كِسَر». The parsing of «مظلماً» differs according to the two readings. On the reading of al-Kisāʾī and Ibn Kathīr it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «قِطْعاً», described thus to intensify the description of their faces as black; and it may be a ḥāl, in which there are three views. First: it is a ḥāl from «قِطْعاً»; that is permissible because it has been specified by being qualified by the preposition-phrase after it, «من الليل». Second: it is a ḥāl from «الليل». Third: it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition-phrase, since it serves as an adjective.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: if you make «مظلماً» a ḥāl from «الليل», what governs it? I say: it is one of two things: either it is «أُغْشِيَتْ», on the grounds that «من الليل» is an adjective of His word «قِطْعاً», and its reaching the qualified noun is like its reaching the adjective; or it is the verbal sense in «من الليل»."
Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "As for the first view, it is far-fetched, because the basic rule is that what governs the ḥāl is what governs its possessor; what governs «من الليل» is the istiqrār, and «أُغْشِيَتْ» governs His word «قطعاً», which is qualified by «من الليل»; so they differ. That is why the last view is preferable, i.e. portions settled from the night, or being from the night, in the state of its darkness." I say: by his saying "the governor is «أُغْشِيَتْ»" al-Zamakhsharī means only that the qualified noun «قِطْعاً» is governed by «أُغْشِيَتْ», and what governs the qualified noun governs the adjective; the adjective is «من الليل», so it is governed by «أُغْشِيَتْ», and it is the possessor of the ḥāl; and what governs the ḥāl is what governs its possessor. From that it follows, in this way, that what governs the ḥāl is what governs its possessor. «قِطْعاً» may also be the plural of «قطعة», i.e. a generic noun (ism jins), in which case it may be qualified with the masculine, as in «نَخْلٌ مُنْقَعِر» (uprooted palm-trees), and with the feminine, as in «نخل خاوية» (hollow palm-trees).
As for the reading of the rest, Makkī and others said: "«مظلماً» is a ḥāl from «الليل» only. It cannot be an adjective of «قِطَعاً», nor a ḥāl from it, nor from the pronoun in «من الليل», because then it would have had to be «مظلمة»." I say: they mean that the qualified noun would then be plural, and likewise the possessor of the ḥāl, so agreement would be required. Some allowed what these forbade, saying it is permissible because it has the meaning of "much"; this is forced.
Ubayy read {تغشى وجوهَهم قِطْعٌ} in the nominative, with «مظلمٌ». Ibn Abī ʿAbla read likewise, except that he gave the ṭāʾ fatḥa. If you make «مظلماً» an adjective of «قطعاً», you have placed the non-explicit adjective before the explicit one.
