Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "If it is an adjective" — meaning «مظلماً» as an adjective of «قطع» — "then by right it should have come before the clause, but it may come after it; the implied form of the clause is «قطعاً استقرَّ من الليل مظلماً» (portions, settled from the night, dark), like His words {وهذا كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ} [al-Anʿām: 155]." Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It is not necessary to suppose the governor of the genitive phrase to be a verb, so that it would be a clause; rather the apparent [course] is to suppose it an active participle, so that it is a case of qualification by a single word, the implied form being «قطعاً كائناً من الليل مظلماً» (portions being from the night, dark)." I say: the objection is placing the non-explicit [adjective] before the explicit one, even if it is supposed to be a single word.
«قطعاً» is accusative through «أُغْشِيَتْ» as a second object.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ}: «يوم» is accusative through an implied verb, i.e. «خَوِّفْهم يوم» (warn them of the day) or «ذكِّرْهم يوم» (remind them of the day). The pronoun refers to both groups, i.e. those who did good and those who earned [evil]. «جميعاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may also be a tawkīd (emphasis) according to those who count it among the words of emphasis.
His words: {مَكَانَكُمْ}: «مكانكم» is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), which the grammarians explained as «اثبتوا» (stand firm); so it carries a pronoun, and that is why it was emphasized by His word «أنتم» and «شركاؤكم» was conjoined to it. Like it are the poet's words:
2590 - وقَوْلِي كلما جَشَأَتْ وجاشَتْ ... مكانَكِ تُحْمَدي أو تَسْتريحي
(And my saying, whenever [my soul] rose up and surged: "Stay in your place! You will be praised or be at rest.")
— i.e. «اثبتي» (stand firm); this is indicated by the jussive of its apodosis, «تُحْمَدي». Al-Zamakhsharī explained it as «الزموا» (keep to); he said: "«مكانكم», i.e. keep to your place and do not leave until you see what will be done with you." Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "His supposing it to be «الزموا» is not good, since if it were so it would be transitive, just as that for which it stands is transitive; for a verbal noun is treated like what it names, and that is why, when they supposed «عليك» to mean «الزم», they made it transitive like it, as in «عليك زيداً» (keep to Zayd). And according to al-Ḥūfī, «مكانكم» is accusative through an implied verb, i.e. «الزموا مكانكم» (keep to your place) or «اثبتوا» (stand firm)." I say: so al-Zamakhsharī was preceded in this explanation; and the excuse of those who explained it so is that they intended to explain the meaning. Abū al-Baqāʾ likewise explained it, saying: "«مكانكم» is an indeclinable (mabnī) adverb, because it stands in the place of the imperative, i.e. «الزموا»."
What he mentioned about its being indeclinable is a matter of disagreement among the grammarians: some held what he mentioned, and some held that it is a case-vowel. These two views rest on a disagreement about verbal nouns: do they have a grammatical position or not? If we say they have a position, then the vowels of the adverb are case-vowels; if we say they have no position, then they are vowels of indeclinability. As for his supposing it to be «الزموا», the answer to that has been given.
His words: {أَنتُمْ}: there are two views. First: it is a tawkīd of the latent pronoun in the adverb, because [the adverb] stands in the place of the agent, as was pointed out. Second — Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed it — it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «شركاؤكم» conjoined to it and its khabar (predicate) omitted; he said: "Its implied form is «أنتم وشركاؤكم مُهانون أو مُعَذَّبون» (you and your partners are humiliated, or punished)." [Translator's note: the source prints «مُهاون», evidently for «مُهانون»; translated accordingly.] On this view one pauses at His word «مكانكم» and then begins with His word «أنتم». This ought not to be said, because it involves dismantling the most eloquent speech and cutting up its arrangement without any reason calling for that; also because the reading of those who read «وشركاءَكم» in the accusative indicates its weakness, since that can only be on the first view; and because of His words «فزيَّلْنا بينهم», which indicate that they and their partners were commanded to stand firm in one place, so that the separation between them could take place.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya also said: "«أنتم» may be a tawkīd of the pronoun in the implied verb, which is «قفوا» (stop) or the like."
Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is not good, since if it were an emphasis of that pronoun attached to the verb, it would be permissible to place it before the adverb, since on this view the adverb has not taken on a pronoun; so its being placed after it would be required — and that is not permissible: you do not say «أنت مكانَك», and it is not preserved from their speech. The soundest view is that the emphasized element may not be omitted in semantic emphasis (al-tawkīd al-maʿnawī), and so too here, because emphasis is incompatible with omission. It is not of their speech to say «أنت زيداً» to someone you see has drawn a sword, intending «اضرب أنت زيداً» (strike Zayd, you); the speech of the Arabs is only «زيداً», intending «اضرب زيداً»." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya did not mean that «أنت» is an emphasis of that pronoun in «قفوا» in the sense that the verb is intended without anything standing in for it; rather [he meant] that this adverb stands in for it, so it is an emphasis of it in origin, before the adverb stood in for it. He only said "which is «قفوا»" as an explanation of the implied meaning.
A group read «وشركاءَكم» in the accusative as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), governed by the verbal noun. [Translator's note: the source prints «وشكركاءَكم», a misprint for «وشركاءَكم».]
His words: {فَزَيَّلْنَا}, i.e. We separated and distinguished, as in the words of the Exalted {لَوْ تَزَيَّلُواْ لَعَذَّبْنَا} [al-Fatḥ: 25]. They disagreed whether the pattern of «زيَّل» is «فَعَّل» or «فَيْعَل». The apparent view is the first, the doubling in it being for multiplicity, not for making transitive, because its triliteral [form] is transitive by itself; al-Farrāʾ reported «زِلْتُ الضَّأن من المَعِز فلم تَزِل» (I separated the sheep from the goats, and they did not separate), and one says «زِلْت الشيء مِنْ مكانه أَزيله» (I removed the thing from its place); on this view it is of the roots with yāʾ. The second: it is «فَيْعَل», like «بَيْطَر» and «بَيْقَر», from «زال يَزُول»; the origin is «زَيْوَلْنا»: the yāʾ and wāw came together, the first of them quiescent, so the well-known weakening was applied, namely changing the wāw into yāʾ and assimilating the yāʾ into it, as in «ميِّت» and «سَيّد» from «مَيْوِت» and «سَيْوِد»; on this view it is of the root with wāw. Ibn Qutayba held this, and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him.
Makkī said: "It cannot be «فَعَّلْنا» from «زال يزول», because the wāw would [necessarily] remain in it, so it would be «زَوَّلنا»." I say: this is correct, and its detailed treatment was given at His words {أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزاً إلى فِئَةٍ} [al-Anfāl: 16]. Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected its being «فَيْعَل», [saying]: "because «فعَّل» is more common than «فَيْعَل»; because its maṣdar is «التزييل», whereas if it were «فَيْعَل» its maṣdar would be «فَيْعَلة», like «بَيْطَرة», since «فَيْعَل» is assimilated (mulḥaq) to «فَعْلَل»; and because of their saying «زايَل» with its meaning, while they did not say «زاول» in the sense of "to part from"; they only said it in the sense of "to attempt" and "to mix with"." Al-Farrāʾ reported «فزايَلْنا», and a group read so. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Like «صاعَرَ خَدَّه» and «صَعَّره» (he turned his cheek in contempt), and «كالمتُه» and «كلَّمْته» (I spoke to him)." I say: he means that «فاعَل» has the meaning of «فَعَّل». «زايَلَ» means «فارَقَ» (to part from). [The poet] said:
2591 - وقال العذارى إنَّما أنت عَمُّنا ... وكان الشبابُ كالخليطِ نُزايِلُهْ
(The maidens said: "You are only our uncle"; and youth was like a companion whom we part from.)
And another said:
2592 - لعَمْري لَمَوْتٌ لا عقوبةَ بعده ... لِذي البَثِّ أَشْفَى مِنْ هوىً لا يُزايلُهْ
(By my life, a death with no punishment after it is more healing for the grief-stricken than a passion that never leaves him.)
His words {فَزَيَّلْنَا} and «قال»: these two verbs are past in form and future in meaning, because they are conjoined to a future, namely «ويوم نحشرهم»; they are analogous to the words of the Exalted {يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ القيامة فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ} [Hūd: 98]. «إيَّانا» is a fronted object, fronted for emphasis and restriction; it must be placed before its governor because it is a detached pronoun which, if placed after it, would have to be attached.

semin-durr:29-29.t: The discussion of what comes after this — {وكفى} [al-Nisāʾ: 6], the lightened «إنْ» and the lām that follows it — has already been given, sufficiently to make repeating it unnecessary.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
The words of the Exalted: {هُنَالِكَ تَبْلُواْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ}: on «هنالك» there are two views. The apparent one is that it keeps its original sense of indicating an adverb of place, i.e. at that slippery standing-place and that bewildering place. It was also said: here it is an adverb of time, by way of metaphor, and like it is {هُنَالِكَ ابتلي المؤمنون} [al-Aḥzāb: 11], i.e. at that time, and as in the poet's words:
2593 - وإذا الأمورُ تعاظَمَتْ وتشاكَلَتْ ... فهناك يَعْترفون أينَ المَفْزَعُ
(When matters grow great and confused, then they acknowledge where the refuge lies.)
And when it is possible for a thing to remain in its original sense, that is preferable.
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «تَتْلو» with two tāʾs dotted above, i.e. it seeks and follows what it sent ahead of its deeds; and from this is the poet's saying:
2594 - إنَّ المُريبَ يَتْبَع المُريبا ... كما رأيت الذِّيبَ يتلو الذِّيبا
(The suspicious one follows the suspicious one, just as you have seen the wolf following the wolf.)
— i.e. it follows it and seeks it. It may also be from recitation in the familiar sense, i.e. every soul will read what it did, written down in the scrolls of the recording [angels], according to the words of the Exalted {ياويلتنا مَالِ هذا الكتاب لاَ يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلاَ كَبِيرَةً إِلاَّ أَحْصَاهَا} [al-Kahf: 49], and His words {وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ القيامة كِتَاباً يَلْقَاهُ مَنْشُوراً اقرأ كتابك} [al-Isrāʾ: 13–14].
The rest read «تَبْلو», from «البَلاء», which is testing, i.e. it comes to know its deeds: whether they are good or evil. ʿĀṣim, in one transmission, read «نبلو» with the nūn and the single-dotted bāʾ, i.e. We test. «كل» is [then] accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). His words «وما أَسْلَفَتْ», on this reading, may be in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. «بما أسْلَفَتْ» (by what it sent ahead); when the preposition dropped, its genitive noun became accusative, as in the poet's words:
2595 - تمرُّون الديار ولم تعوجوا ... كلامُكمُ عليَّ إذنْ حَرامُ
(You pass by the dwellings without turning aside — then speaking with you is forbidden to me.)
It may also be accusative as a badal (substitute) from «كل نفس», a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). «نَبْلو» may also be from «البلاء» in the sense of punishment, i.e. We punish it because of what it sent ahead.
«ما» may be a nominal relative, or a particle relative (maṣdariyya), or an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows]; the referent pronoun is omitted on the first and last views but not the second, according to the well-known [doctrine].
Ibn Waththāb read «ورِدُّوا» with kasra on the rāʾ, likening the doubled ʿayn [radical] to the weak one, as in «قيل» and «بيع»; and like it is:
2596 - وما حِلَّ مِنْ جَهْلٍ حُبا حُلَمائِنا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The sitting-cloths of our forbearing men were never loosened through folly…)
— with kasra on the ḥāʾ. The explanation of that has been given more clearly than this.
His words: {إِلَى الله}: a muḍāf must be supposed, i.e. to the recompense of Allah, or to the place where He recompenses. The majority read «الحق» in the genitive. It was read in the accusative on one of two views: either by cutting off (qaṭʿ) — its origin being that it is a dependent [adjective] which was cut off by implying «أمدح» (I praise), as in their saying «الحمدُ للَّهِ أهلَ الحمد» (praise be to Allah, the One worthy of praise) — or as a maṣdar emphasizing the content of the preceding clause, {وردوا إِلَى الله}; al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, saying: "As when you say «هذا عبد الله الحقَّ لا الباطل» (this is ʿAbd Allāh, truly, not falsely)," as an emphasis of His words {وردوا إِلَى الله}. Makkī said: "It may be accusative as a maṣdar, but it was not read so." I say: it seems he did not come across this reading.
His words: {مَّا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ}: «ما» admits the three views [mentioned above].

semin-durr:31-31.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مِّنَ السمآء}: «مِنْ» may be for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), or partitive, or for explaining the genus; on these last two views an omitted muḍāf must be supposed, i.e. «من أهل السماء» (from the inhabitants of the heaven).
His words: {أَمْ}: this is the disconnected «أم» (al-munqaṭiʿa), because no hamza of interrogation or of equalization (taswiya) precedes it. However, here it is to be understood as «بل» (rather) alone, without the hamza. It is established that, according to the majority, the disconnected [«أم»] is understood as both [«بل» and the hamza]; it is not understood here as «بل» and the hamza only because an explicit interrogative noun, «مَنْ», falls after it; so it is like the words of the Exalted {أَمَّا ذَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ} [al-Naml: 84]. The turning away (iḍrāb) here, according to the established rule in the Quran, is an iḍrāb of transition, not an iḍrāb of cancellation.

semin-durr:32-32.t: The words of the Exalted: {فَمَاذَا بَعْدَ}: «ماذا» may as a whole be a single noun because the two are compounded, with the interrogative prevailing over the demonstrative; the meaning of the interrogative here has become negation, which is why [the statement] after it is made affirmative with «إلا». Or «ذا» may be a relative noun meaning «الذي» (that which), the interrogative likewise having the meaning of negation, the implied form being: «ما الذي بعد الحق إلا الضلال؟» (what is there after the truth except error?).

semin-durr:33-33.t:
The words of the Exalted: {كَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ}: the kāf is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and «ذلك» points to the maṣdar understood from «تُصْرفون», i.e. like their being turned away from the truth after acknowledging it in the words of the Exalted {فَسَيَقُولُونَ الله} [Yūnus: 31]. It was also said: it points to the truth. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«كذلك»: like that truth, the word of your Lord has come true."
His words: {أَنَّهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}: there are four views on it. First: it is in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) from «كلمةُ», i.e. the absence of belief has come true against them. Second: it is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. the matter is their not believing. Third: it is in the position of accusative after the dropping of the preposition. Fourth: it is in the position of genitive, with [the preposition] governing while omitted, since the origin is «لأنهم لا يُؤْمنون» (because they do not believe). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or by «الكلمة» He meant the promise of punishment, and {أَنَّهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ} is a statement of cause, i.e. «لأنهم» (because they…)."
Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and the Kufans read «كلمة» in the singular, and likewise at the end of the sūra; that has been discussed in al-Anʿām. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read {إِنهم لا يُؤْمنون} with kasra on «إنَّ», as a resumptive clause, with a sense of causation in it; this strengthens the view that takes it as causal. [Translator's note: the source prints this reading as «أَنهم» with fatḥa, but describes it as having kasra; «إِنهم» is clearly intended.]

semin-durr:34-34.t: The words of the Exalted: {قُلِ الله يَبْدَأُ الخلق}: this clause is the answer to His words {هَلْ مِن شُرَكَآئِكُمْ مَنْ يَبْدَأُ}. The answer was given only as a nominal clause, with both its parts made explicit and the predicate repeated in it, corresponding to the predicate of the interrogative noun, for emphasis and confirmation. And since the earlier question was one which they had no way to avoid acknowledging, the clause came with one of its two parts omitted, in His words {فَسَيَقُولُونَ الله} [Yūnus: 31], and there was no need for emphasis by making both its parts explicit.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
The words of the Exalted: {يهدي إِلَى الحق}: it was stated at the beginning of this work that «هدى» takes two objects, the second of them either with the lām or with «إلى», and the preposition is sometimes omitted for lightness. Here both ways of making it transitive by a preposition have been combined: the first and third [verbs] are made transitive with «إلى» and the second with the lām, and the first object has been omitted from all three verbs, the implied form being: «هل مِنْ شركائكم مَنْ يَهْدي غيره إلى الحق، قل اللَّهُ يَهْدي مَنْ يشاء للحق، أفَمَنْ يهدي غيرَه إلى الحق» (is there among your partners one who guides another to the truth? Say: Allah guides whom He wills to the truth. Is then He who guides another to the truth…). Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ — and al-Zamakhsharī followed them — claimed that the first «يهدي» is intransitive and that it means «اهتدى» (to be guided). That is open to question, because its counterpart, {قُلِ الله يَهْدِي لِلْحَقِّ}, is transitive. Al-Mubarrad also rejected the statement of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, saying: "We do not know «هَدَى» in the sense of «اهتدى»." I say: al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ established it by what they transmitted; but it is weak here only because of what I mentioned to you about its being set against the transitive [verb]. It has been stated that making it transitive with «إلى» or with the lām is a matter of rhetorical variation; that is why al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says «هَدَاه للحق» and «إلى الحق», so He combined the two usages." Someone else said: "The [verb] attributed to Allah was made transitive with the lām only because, in its domain, it indicates the intended meaning more than «إلى», since its basic function is to convey possession; so it is as though guidance is owned by Allah the Exalted." That is open to question, because what is meant by His words {أَفَمَن يهدي إِلَى الحق} is Allah the Exalted, even though the verb attributed to Him is made transitive with «إلى».
His words: {أَحَقُّ أَن يُتَّبَعَ} is the khabar (predicate) of His words «أَفَمَنْ يَهْدي»; «أَنْ» is in the position of accusative or genitive after the omission of the preposition, and that over which preference is given is omitted. The implied form of all this is: «أَفَمَنْ يهْدي إلى الحقّ أَحَقُّ بأن يُتَّبَع ممَّن لا يَهْدي» (is then He who guides to the truth more worthy of being followed than one who does not guide?). Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib mentioned that, taking «أحقّ» here in its proper sense as an elative (for preference). Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected its being for preference here, saying: "«أحق» is not for preference; rather the meaning is: worthy of being followed." Makkī also allowed two other views on the question. First: «مَنْ» is again a mubtadaʾ (subject), «أنْ» is in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) from it, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), and «أحقُّ» is the khabar as before. Second: «أن يُتَّبع» is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «أحقُّ» its khabar placed before it, and this clause is the khabar of «مَنْ يَهْدي». So there are three views on the question.
His words: {أَمَّن لاَّ يهدي} are conjoined to «أفمن». It comes here according to the most eloquent [usage], in that «أم» is separated from what it is conjoined to by the khabar, as when you say «زيدٌ قائم أم عمرو» (is Zayd standing, or ʿAmr?), and like it is {أذلك خَيْرٌ أَمْ جَنَّةُ الخلد} [al-Furqān: 15]. This differs from the words of the Exalted {أَقَرِيبٌ أَم بَعِيدٌ مَّا تُوعَدُونَ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 109]; this will come in its place.
Abū Bakr [Shuʿba], from ʿĀṣim, read with kasra on the yāʾ and the hāʾ of «يهدي» [«يِهِدِّي»], and Ḥafṣ with kasra on the hāʾ but not the yāʾ [«يَهِدِّي»]. As for the kasra of the hāʾ, it is because of the meeting of two quiescent letters: its origin is «يَهْتدي»; when assimilation was intended the tāʾ was made quiescent, and the hāʾ before it was quiescent, so the hāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Abū Bakr made the yāʾ follow the hāʾ in the kasra. Abū Ḥātim said of the reading of Ḥafṣ: "It is the dialect of lower Muḍar," and he transmitted from Sībawayh that he does not allow «يِهْدي» but allows «تِهْدي», «نِهْدي» and «إهدي»; he said: "because the kasra is heavy on the yāʾ." I say: he means that he allows kasra on the prefix of the imperfect in such [verbs], as in «تِهْدي», «نِهدي» and «إهدي», since there is no heaviness in that, but he did not allow it on the yāʾ because of the heaviness of the vowel homogeneous with it upon it. This implies a disparagement of the reading of Abū Bakr; but it has been transmitted by tawātur as a reading, so it is accepted.
Abū ʿAmr, and Qālūn from Nāfiʿ, read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, a snatched (ikhtilās) fatḥa on the hāʾ and a doubled dāl. That is because, having made the fatḥa heavy for the assimilation, they snatched the fatḥa to draw attention to the fact that the hāʾ is not originally vowelled but quiescent. Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Warsh read with a full fatḥa on the hāʾ, according to the principle of transfer [of the vowel of the tāʾ]. It has also been transmitted from Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn that they snatched a kasra on the hāʾ, according to the principle of the meeting of two quiescent letters, the snatching being to draw attention to the fact that the hāʾ is originally quiescent, as stated.
The people of Medina, except Warsh, read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, a quiescent hāʾ and a doubled dāl. A group found this reading problematic because of the combination of two quiescent letters. Al-Mubarrad said: "Whoever attempts this must give [the hāʾ] a hidden vowel." Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās said: "No one is able to pronounce it." I say: [al-Dānī] said in al-Taysīr: "The explicit transmission from Qālūn is with quiescence." I say: there is nothing unlikely in that, for it has been stated that some readers read {نِعِمَّا} [al-Nisāʾ: 58] and {لاَ تَعْدُواْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 154] combining two quiescent letters; you have had many readings at His words {يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 20]; and the like of this will come at {يَخِصِّمُونَ} [Yā Sīn: 49].
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «يَهْدي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, a quiescent hāʾ and an undoubled dāl, from «هدى يَهْدي». There are two views on it. First: «هدى» means «اهتدى». Second: it is transitive and its object is omitted, as has been set out. The statement of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ on that, and al-Mubarrad's refutation of them, have been given. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What I say is: the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī may mean: or one who does not guide anyone unless that person is guided by Allah's guidance. As for the other readings, whose import is «أم لا يَهْتدي إلا أن يهدى» (or one who is not guided unless he is guided), the meaning proceeds as stated." [Translator's note: the source prints «والذي أقوال», evidently for «والذي أقول»; translated accordingly.] Then he said: "It was also said: the speech is complete at His words «أم مَنْ لا يَهِدِّي», i.e. does not guide another." Then he said: "{إِلاَّ أَن يهدى} is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), i.e. but he needs to be guided, as you say: so-and-so does not make another hear unless he is made to hear, i.e. but he needs to hear." End of quotation. It may also be a connected exception, because in that case there is in them a receptivity to guidance, unlike the idols. It may also be an exception from the completion of the object of purpose, i.e. he does not guide for anything at all except in order that he be guided by another.
His words: {فَمَا لَكُمْ} are a mubtadaʾ and khabar. The meaning of the interrogative here is disapproval and wonder, i.e. what is there for you in taking these, when they are incapable of guiding themselves — so how could they guide others? It has been stated that some grammarians stipulated that such a construction is only complete with a ḥāl (circumstantial) after it, as in {فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التذكرة مُعْرِضِينَ} [al-Muddaththir: 49] and {وَمَا لَنَا لاَ نُؤْمِنُ} [al-Māʾida: 84], among others; here the clause after this construction cannot be taken as a ḥāl, because it is interrogative, and an interrogative clause does not occur as a ḥāl. His words «كيف تحكمون» are another question, i.e. how do you judge by falsehood and assign to Allah equals and partners?

semin-durr:36-36.t: The words of the Exalted: {لاَ يُغْنِي}: the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «شيئاً» is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], i.e. anything of availing. «من الحق» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شيئاً», because it was originally an adjective of it. «مِنْ» may also have the meaning of «بدل» (in place of), i.e. it does not avail in place of the truth. The majority read «يَفْعلون» in the third person; ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «تَفْعلون» in the second person of address, which is an eloquent shift (iltifāt).

semin-durr:37-37.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَن يفترى}: there are two views on it. First: it is the khabar (predicate) of «كان», its implied form being «وما كان هذا القرآن افتراء» (this Quran is not a fabrication), i.e. «ذا افتراء» (possessing fabrication), the maṣdar itself having been made [the predicate] for hyperbole; or it has the meaning of «مفترى» (fabricated). Second: some claimed that this «أنْ» is the one implied after the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), the origin being «وما كان هذا القرآنُ ليفترى»; when the lām of denial was omitted, «أن» became overt. He claimed that the lām and «أنْ» alternate, so that one is omitted at times and the other remains. This is a view to be shunned. On this view the khabar of «كان» is omitted, and «أنْ» with what is in its scope is attached to that khabar; the setting-out of this has been given in detail. «مِنْ دون» is attached to «يفترى», and what stands in the place of the agent [the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)] is a pronoun referring to the Quran.
His words: {ولكن تَصْدِيقَ}: «تَصْديق» is conjoined to the khabar of «كان». «لكن» has fallen in the best of places, since it is between two opposites: denial and confirmation, which includes truthfulness. The majority read «تصديق» and «تفصيلَ» in the accusative, and there are several views on it. First: conjunction to the khabar of «كان», as stated; and like it is {مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَآ أَحَدٍ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ ولكن رَّسُولَ الله} [al-Aḥzāb: 40]. Second: it is the khabar of an implied «كان», its implied form being «ولكن كان تصديقَ» (but it was a confirmation); al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ, Ibn Saʿdān and al-Zajjāj held this; it is like the preceding in meaning. Third: it is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) of an implied verb, i.e. this Quran was not to be fabricated, but it was sent down for confirmation. Fourth: it is accusative as a maṣdar, also through an implied verb, the implied form being «ولكن يُصَدِّق تصديقَ الذي بين يديه من الكتب» (but it confirms with a confirmation the scriptures before it).
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «تَصْديقُ» in the nominative, and likewise the one in Yūsuf. Its justification is the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «ولكن هو تصديق» (but it is a confirmation); like it is the poet's saying:
2597 - ولستُ الشاعرَ السَّفْسَافَ فيهمْ ... ولكن مِدْرَهُ الحربِ العَوانِ
(I am not the paltry poet among them, but the champion of the long, relentless war.)
— with «مِدْرَه» in the nominative, on the implied form «أنا مِدْره» (I am the champion). Makkī said: "According to them both — i.e. al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ — the nominative is permissible on the implied form «ولكن هو تصديق»." I say: it seems he did not learn that it is a reading.
Al-Farrāʾ and a group claimed that when the Arabs say «ولكن» with the wāw they prefer doubling the nūn, and when there is no wāw they prefer lightening it. Both lightening and doubling have occurred in the readings of the Seven, as in {ولكن الشياطين} [al-Baqara: 102] and {ولكن الله رمى} [al-Anfāl: 17]. [Translator's note: in the source the sentence "lightening has occurred in the readings of the Seven" appears once in truncated form and then again in full — evidently a copyist's repetition; it is rendered once here.]
His words: {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ}: there are several views on it. First: it is a ḥāl from «الكتاب»; a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi is permissible here because it is an object in meaning. The meaning is: and the detailed explanation of the Book, doubt being absent from it. Second: it is resumptive, so it has no grammatical position. Third: it is parenthetical between «تصديق» and {مِن رَّبِّ العالمين}, since the implied form is «ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه مِنْ رب العالمين» (but a confirmation of what was before it, from the Lord of the worlds). [Translator's note: the source prints «الذين», evidently a misprint for «الذي»; translated accordingly.]
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: to what are His words {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِن رَّبِّ العالمين} connected? I say: it falls within the scope of the rectification (istidrāk), as though it were said: but it was a confirmation and a detailed explanation, doubt being absent from it, being from the Lord of the worlds. And it may be intended to mean: but it was a confirmation from the Lord of the worlds [and a detailed explanation from Him — no doubt about that; so «من رب العالمين» is] attached to «تصديق» and «تفصيل», and {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} is parenthetical, as you say: «زيدٌ لا شكَّ فيه كريم» (Zayd — no doubt about it — is generous)." End of quotation.
His words: {مِن رَّبِّ}: several views are possible. First: it is attached to «تصديق» or to «تفصيل», the question being one of contention [between two governors] (tanāzuʿ), since in terms of meaning it can validly be attached to each of the two governors. This is what al-Zamakhsharī meant by his words "so «من رب» is attached to «تصديق» and «تفصيل»," meaning that it is attached to each of them in terms of meaning; in terms of grammatical parsing it is attached to only one of them, while the other governs its pronoun, as has been set out more than once; and the governing here is then by the second, as evidenced by the omission from the first. The second view: «مِنْ رب» is a second ḥāl. The third: it is attached to that implied verb, i.e. it was sent down for confirmation from the Lord of the worlds.

semin-durr:38-38.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَمْ يَقُولُونَ}: on «أم» there are two views. First: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), so it is understood as «بل» and the hamza according to the majority — Sībawayh and his followers — the implied form being «بل أتقولون» (rather, do you say…?); He moved on from the first speech and began to reject another saying. Second: it is connected (muttaṣila); in that case a clause must be omitted so that the balance [of alternatives] is valid, the implied form being «أيقرُّون به أم يقولون افتراه» (do they acknowledge it, or do they say: he fabricated it?). Some said: this is equivalent to the hamza alone. Some expressed that by saying: "The mīm is added to the hamza"; this is a worthless view, since the addition of the mīm is very rare, especially here. Abū ʿUbayda claimed that it has the meaning of the wāw, the implied form being «ويقولون افتراه» (and they say: he fabricated it).
His words: {قُلْ فَأْتُواْ}: the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Say: if the matter is as you claim, then bring, by way of fabrication, a sūra like it in Arabic [usage], eloquence and supreme rhetorical power." ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read «بسورةِ مثلِه» with «سورة» annexed to «مثله», on the omission of the qualified noun and putting the adjective in its place, the implied form being «بسورةِ كتابٍ مثلِه» (a sūra of a book like it) or «بسورةِ كلام مثله» (a sūra of speech like it). [Translator's note: the source prints «حذف الموصول» (the relative noun) and «أبو», evidently misprints for «حذف الموصوف» (the qualified noun) and «أو» (or); translated accordingly.] The implied form may also be «فَأْتوا بسورةِ بشرٍ مثلِه» (bring a sūra of a human being like him); so on this reading the pronoun may refer to the Quran, or to the Prophet ﷺ. In the reading of the generality, the pronoun refers to the Quran only.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَمَّا يَأْتِهِمْ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the relative noun, that is: they hastened to deny it while the interpretation had not yet come to them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of the expectation (tawaqquʿ) in His saying, the Exalted, {وَلَمَّا يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ}? I say: its meaning is that they denied it offhand, before reflection and before knowing the interpretation." Then he also said: "It is possible that the meaning is: the interpretation of what it contains of reports of the unseen has not yet come to them, that is, its outcome, so that it becomes clear to them whether it is a lie or the truth." End of quotation. There is something to consider in his putting «لم» in the place of «لَمَّا», given what you know of the difference between the two. The clause of encompassing was negated with «لم» and the clause of the coming of the interpretation with «لمَّا» because «لم» is for absolute negation, on the sound view, whereas «لَمَّا» negates an action that is continuous up to the present time; so the meaning is that the absence of the interpretation extends up to the time of the report.

And «كذلك» is an naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), that is: those before them denied in the manner of that denial, that is, before looking and reflecting.

And His saying: {فانظر كَيْفَ كَانَ}: «كيف» is the khabar (predicate) of «كان», and the interrogative suspends (muʿallaq) the looking. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Al-Zajjāj said: «كيف» is in the position of accusative as the predicate of «كان», and «انظر» may not operate on it, because what precedes an interrogative does not operate on it; this is the rule of the grammarians, because they treated «كيف» everywhere as a pure interrogative, as in your saying «كيف زيد». But «كيف» has other uses besides this: it takes the place of the maṣdar «كيفية» and sheds the meaning of interrogation, and this passage may be one of them. Among its uses is their saying «كن كيف شئت»; and consider al-Bukhārī's saying «كيف كان بدء الوحي», for he was not asking a question." End of quotation. Al-Zajjāj's saying that «انظر» may not operate on «كيف» means that it does not govern it, but it governs the clause over which the ruling of the interrogative extends; and such is the way of every suspension (taʿlīq).

[Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Ibn ʿAṭiyya's saying 'this is the rule of the grammarians' and so on is not as he stated. Rather «كيف» has two meanings. One is the pure interrogative, which is a question about manner, unless the operator is suspended from it, in which case its meaning is the meaning of the nouns with which one asks questions when the operator is suspended from them. The second is the conditional, like the saying of the Arabs: «كيف تكونُ أكونُ». As for his saying 'and «كيف» has other uses' and so on: «كيف» does not take the place of the maṣdar, nor is the word «كيفية» a maṣdar; that is merely a nisba (relational adjective) formed from «كيف». And his saying 'this passage may be one of them, and among its uses is their saying «كن كيف شئت»' cannot be one of them, because the meaning he mentioned, that «كيف» has the sense of «كيفية», has not been established for it, and the claim that «كيفية» is a maṣdar is likewise unestablished."

As for «كن كيف شئت»: here «كيف» does not mean «كيفية»; rather it is conditional, which is its second meaning, and its apodosis (jawāb) is omitted. The implied form is: «كيف شئت فكن», just as you say «قم متى شئت»: «متى» is a conditional noun, an adverbial (ẓarf), on which «قم» does not operate, and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being «متى شئت فقم». The apodosis is omitted because what precedes indicates it, as in their saying «اضربْ زيداً إن أساء إليك», the implied form being «إن أساءَ إليك فاضرِبْه»; «فاضربه» is omitted because the preceding «اضرِبْ» indicates it. As for al-Bukhārī's saying «كيف كان بدء الوحي», it is a pure interrogative: either by way of reporting, as if someone asked him and said: how was the beginning of revelation?; [or it may be his own saying, as if he asked himself: how was the beginning of revelation?] and then answered with the ḥadīth that contains the manner of that."

And his saying: {الظالمين} is an instance of putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun; it may be intended to refer to the pronoun of those to whom the pronoun in «بل كَذَّبوا» refers, and it may be intended to refer to {الذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ}.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّن يَسْتَمِعُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is the preposition and its genitive noun before it. He repeated the pronoun in the plural, observing the meaning of «مَنْ»; the more frequent usage is to observe its form (lafẓ), as in His saying:
{وَمِنهُمْ مَّن يَنظُرُ إِلَيْكَ}

semin-durr:43-43.t: {وَمِنهُمْ مَّن يَنظُرُ إِلَيْكَ}: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«ينظر» came in accordance with the form of «مَنْ». When it comes in accordance with its form, it is permissible to conjoin another to it in accordance with the meaning; but when it comes first in accordance with its meaning, it is not permissible to conjoin another in accordance with the form, because the speech would then become ambiguous." Abū Ḥayyān said: "It is not as he said. Rather it is permissible to observe the meaning first and return the pronoun according to what one intends of the meaning, whether feminine, dual or plural, and then to observe the form and return the pronoun as masculine singular; there is a detailed treatment of this in grammar." I say: its exposition has already been given at the beginning of al-Baqara.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ يَظْلِمُ الناس شيئاً}: it is possible that «شيئاً» is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), that is: something of wrongdoing, little or much; and it is possible that it is accusative as the second object of «يَظْلم», in the sense: He does not diminish the people in anything of their deeds.

His saying: {ولكن الناس}: the two brothers [Translator's note: i.e. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «لكن» with the nūn lightened, which necessarily entails kasra on the nūn because of the meeting of two sākins in connected speech, and the nominative «الناس»; the rest read it with shadda and the accusative «الناس». The explanation of this was given in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:88-88.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيُضِلُّواْ}: This lām has three aspects. First: that it is the lām of cause (lām al-ʿilla); the meaning is that You gave them what You gave them by way of gradual enticement (istidrāj), so the giving was for this cause. Second: that it is the lām of consequence and outcome (ṣayrūra / ʿāqiba), as in His saying: {فالتقطه آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً وَحَزَناً} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8], and as in his saying:
2622 - لِدُوا للموت وابنُوا للخراب ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (Beget for death and build for ruin …)
and his saying:
2623 - فللموتِ تَغْذو الوالداتُ سِخالَها ... كما لخرابِ الدُّوْرِ تُبْنَى المساكنُ (For death mothers nurse their young, just as dwellings are built for the ruin of houses)
and his saying:
2624 - وللمنايا تُرَبِّى كلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ ... وللخرابِ يَجِدُّ الناسُ عِمْرانا (For deaths every nursing mother rears her child, and for ruin people labour at building)
Third: that it is a supplication against them to that effect, as if he had said: "that they may remain firm in the error they are in and that they may be those who go astray." Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī took this view, and al-Zamakhsharī began with it. This interpretation has been regarded as unlikely because of the reading of the Kufans «ليُضِلُّوا» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, for it is unlikely that he would pray against them that they lead others astray. The rest read it with fatḥa, and al-Shaʿbī read it with kasra, thereby making three kasras follow one another, one of them on a yāʾ. [Abū] al-Faḍl al-Riyāshī read «أإنك أَتَيْتَ» as a question. Al-Jubbāʾī said: a "lā" is implied between the lām and the verb, its implied form being: "so that they may not go astray" (لئلا يَضِلوا). But the view of the Basrans in the like of this is the implication of "karāhata" (dislike), that is: "dislike that they should go astray."

His saying: {فَلاَ يُؤْمِنُواْ} admits of the accusative and the jussive. The accusative is in two ways: one, that it is conjoined to «ليضلُّوا»; the second, that it is accusative as the response to the supplication in His saying «اطمِسْ». The jussive is on the basis that "lā" is for supplication, like your saying "لا تعذِّبْني يا رب" ("Do not punish me, O Lord"); and it is close to the meaning of «ليُضلوا» in being a supplication, this being on the side of resembling a prohibition and that on the side of resembling a command. And «حتى يَرَوا» is the limit (ghāya) of the negation of their belief. The first is the view of al-Akhfash, the second is what al-Zamakhsharī began with, and the third is the view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, and he cited the poet's verse:
2625 - فلا يَنْبَسِطْ من بين عينِك ما انزوى ... ولا تَلْقَني إلا وأنفُكَ راغِمُ (So let what has contracted between your eyes not relax, and do not meet me except with your nose in the dust)
On the view that it is conjoined to «ليَضِلُّوا», what lies between the two is a parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ).

semin-durr:89-89.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أُجِيبَتْ دَّعْوَتُكُمَا}: The pronoun refers to Mūsā and Hārūn. In the exegesis: Mūsā used to pray and Hārūn to say "Amen", so the supplication was ascribed to both. Some of them said: only Mūsā is meant, but the one was referred to by the pronoun of the dual. Al-Sulamī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «دَعَواتكما» in the plural. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «قد أَجَبْتُ دعوتكما» with the tāʾ of the first person, the speaker being the Creator, the Exalted, and «دعوتَكما» is accusative as direct object. Al-Rabīʿ read «أَجَبْتُ دَعْوَتَيْكما», also with the tāʾ of the first person; and «دَعْوَتَيْكما» is a dual, and it is evidence for the one who said that Hārūn shared with Mūsā in the supplication.

His saying: {وَلاَ تَتَّبِعَآنِّ}: The majority read it with shadda on the tāʾ and the nūn. Ḥafṣ read it with a light nūn carrying kasra, together with a shadda or a light tāʾ; and the readers have confused statements on this as regards what is reported from him. As for the reading of the majority, the "lā" in it is prohibitive, and for that reason the verb after it is emphasised; it is weak for it to be negative, because emphasising a negated verb is weak, and we have no need to claim it, even though some have claimed it in His saying {لاَّ تُصِيبَنَّ الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [al-Anfāl: 25] for a necessity that called for it there; its verification and proof have already been given in its place. On the sound view, this is a prohibitive clause conjoined to a clause of command.

As for the reading of Ḥafṣ, the "lā" in it may be negative or prohibitive. If it is negative, the nūn is the nūn of the nominative (rafʿ), and the clause then has several aspects. One: that it is in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "so stay upright, not following"; except that this is objected to by what I have mentioned more than once, that the imperfect negated by "lā" is like the affirmative in that the wāw of ḥāl does not directly attach to it, unless a mubtadaʾ (subject) is implied before it so that the clause becomes nominal, that is: "and you two are not following". Second: that it is a negation in the sense of prohibition, like His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ إِلاَّ الله} [al-Baqara: 83]. Third: that it is a pure, resumptive report with no connection to what precedes it, the meaning being that the two of them were informed that they do not follow the path of those who do not know. If it is prohibitive, the nūn is of emphasis, and it is the light one; and Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī do not accept this, I mean the occurrence of the light nūn after the alif, whether the alif is the alif of the dual or the alif of separation between the nūn of the feminine and the nūn of emphasis, as in "هل تَضْرِبْنان يا نسوة" ("Will you women strike?"). Yūnus and al-Farrāʾ allowed the light nūn to occur after the alif, and the reading is derived on their view. It was also said: its origin is with shadda, and it was lightened only because of the heaviness in it, like their saying «رُبَ» for «رُبَّ». As for the shadda on the tāʾ and its lightness, they are two dialectal forms of ittabaʿa yattabiʿu and tabiʿa yatbaʿu; it has already been discussed whether they are of one meaning or differ in meaning. The summary is that tabiʿahu bi-shayʾin means "he came after him", and ittabaʿahu likewise, except that he drew level with him in walking; and atbaʿahu means "he overtook him".

semin-durr:90-90.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَجَاوَزْنَا ببني}: The discussion of it has already preceded. Al-Ḥasan read «وجَوَّزْنا» with shadda on the wāw. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وجَوَّزْنا» is from ajāza al-makān, jāwazahu and jawwazahu, and it is not from the jawwaza that occurs in the verse of al-Aʿshā:
2626 - وإذا تُجَوِّزُها حبالُ قبيلة ... أَخَذْتَ من الأخرى إليك حبالَها (When the ropes of one tribe let her pass, you take from the other tribe its ropes to yourself)
for if it were from it, the proper form would be: وجَوَّزْنا بني إسرائيل في البحر ("and We made the Children of Israel pass through the sea"), as he said:
2627 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما جَوَّز السَّكَّيَّ في الباب فَيْتَقُ (… as فَيْتَق made the bolt pass through the door)"
He means that faʿʿala here has the meaning of fāʿala and afʿala, and the doubling is not for transitivisation, since if it were so, it would be transitive by itself, as in the verse referred to, without the bāʾ.
Al-Ḥasan read «فاتَّبَعَهُم» with shadda; the difference has already been given.

His saying: {بَغْياً وَعَدْواً}: It is permissible that both be objects of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), that is: "for the sake of insolence and aggression", and the conditions for the accusative are fulfilled; and it is permissible that they be two maṣdars in the position of ḥāl, that is: "being insolent, transgressing". Al-Ḥasan read «وعُدُوَّاً» with ḍamma on the ʿayn and a doubled dāl and wāw; that has already been given in Sūrat al-Anʿām.

His saying: {حتى إِذَآ}: the limit (ghāya) of his pursuit.

His saying: {آمَنتُ أَنَّهُ}: The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read "inna" with kasra, and there are several aspects regarding it. One: that it is a resumptive report, and for that reason it was given kasra, because it occurs at the beginning of a speech. Second: that it is on the implication of saying, that is: "so he said: inna-hu", and this saying would explain His «آمنت». Third: that this clause is a badal (substitute) for His «آمنت», and substituting a nominal clause for a verbal one is permissible because it is in its meaning; in that case it has kasra because it is quoted after "qāla" (he said); this is the apparent sense. Fourth: that «آمنتُ» is made to contain the meaning of saying, because it is a saying. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The forsaken man repeated one meaning three times in three expressions, out of eagerness for acceptance", meaning that he said «آمنتُ», which is one time; and he said {أَنَّهُ لا إله إِلاَّ الذي آمَنَتْ بِهِ بنوا إِسْرَائِيلَ}, which is the second; and he said {وَأَنَاْ مِنَ المسلمين}, which is the third; and the meaning is one." This is his inclination toward the resumptive reading of «إنه».
The rest read it with fatḥa, and there are also several aspects regarding it. One: that it is in the position of accusative as direct object, that is: "I believed in the oneness of ..." because it has the meaning of "I affirmed as true". Second: that it is in the position of accusative after dropping the preposition, that is: "because it". Third: that it is in the position of genitive by that preposition, and you have come to know the disagreement concerning it.

semin-durr:92-92.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الآنَ}: It is accusative by an omitted verb, that is: "You believed now", or "Do you believe now?". And His saying «وقد عَصَيْتَ» is a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya), and its like has already been given recently.

His saying: {بِبَدَنِكَ}: There are two aspects. One: that it is the bāʾ of accompaniment, in the sense of "accompanied by your body", and that is the coat of mail (dirʿ). In the exegesis: they did not believe in his drowning, and he had a recognisable coat of mail, so he was cast on a high place of the land with his coat of mail on him so that they might recognise him; and the Arabs apply "badan" to the coat of mail. ʿAmr b. Maʿdī Karib said:
2628 - أعاذِلُ شِكَّتي بدني وسيفي ... وكلّ مُقَلَّصٍ سَلِس القِيادِ (O blamer, my armour is my coat of mail and my sword, and every long-legged, docile-to-lead horse)
and another said:
2629 - ترى الأبْدانَ فيها مُسْبَغَاتٍ ... على الأبطالِ واليَلَبَ الحصينا (You see in it ample coats of mail on the heroes, and the strong helmets)
It was also said: «ببدنك» means "naked, with nothing on you"; and it was said: "a body without a soul".
The second: that it is causal in a figurative sense, because his body was the cause of his being saved; and that is on the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ «بندائك», from nidāʾ, which is the call, that is: by what he called out among his people of his ungratefulness in His saying {ونادى فِرْعَوْنُ فِي قَوْمِهِ} [al-Zukhruf: 51], {فَحَشَرَ فنادى فَقَالَ أَنَاْ رَبُّكُمُ الأعلى} [al-Nāziʿāt: 23-24], {ياأيها الملأ مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُمْ مِّنْ إله غَيْرِي} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 38].
Yaʿqūb read «نُنْجِيْك» in the light form, from anjāhu. Abū Ḥanīfa read «بأبدانك» in the plural: either with the meaning of the coats of mail, because he used to wear many of them out of fear for himself, or by making every part of his body a "badan", as in the saying "his temples have turned grey" (shābat mafāriquhu). He said:
2630 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... شابَ المَفارِقُ واكتَسَيْنَ قَتِيرا (The temples have turned grey and have been clothed in grey hair [or: armour rivets])
Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Yazīd al-Barbarī read «نُنَحِّيْكَ» with the unpointed ḥāʾ, from tanḥiya, that is: "We cast you to one side, on the part next to the sea". In the exegesis: that He threw him onto the shore of the sea like a bull. Is «ننجِّيك» from najāt (deliverance), meaning "We remove you far from what your people fell into, at the bottom of the sea", which would be mockery of them; or from "He cast him on a najwa", that is, a raised hillock; or from najāt in the sense of "leaving"; or from najāʾ, which means "sign"? All these are meanings suited to the story. The apparent sense is that His saying «فاليوم نُنَجِّيك» is a pure report. Some claimed that it is on the intention of the interrogative hamza, but that is remote, because of omitting it without evidence, and because the giving of a reason by His saying «لتكونَ» does not suit the interrogative.
And «لتكون» is attached to «نُنَجِّيك» and «آية», that is, a sign; and «لمَنْ خلفك» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from «آية», because in origin it is an adjective of it.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَيَوْمَ}: accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf). There are several views on what governs it. First: that it is accusative by the verb contained in His saying {كَأَن لَّمْ يلبثوا}. Second: that it is accusative by «يتعارفون». Third: that it is accusative by an implied verb, that is: "remember the day". Al-Aʿmash read «يَحْشُرهم» with yāʾ of the third person, the pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted because His name has preceded in His saying: {إِنَّ الله لاَ يَظْلِمُ}.

His saying: {كَأَن لَّمْ يلبثوا}: the discussion of this «كأنْ» has already preceded. But they differed about the position of this clause, on several views. First: that it is in the position of accusative as an naʿt (adjective) of the adverbial, namely «يوم»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Abū Ḥayyān said: "This is not valid, because «يومَ يحشرُهم» is definite and clauses are indefinite, and a definite noun is not qualified by an indefinite one. It must not be said that the clauses to which nouns of time are annexed are indefinite without exception, for if they resolve in the implied form into a definite, then what is annexed to them becomes definite, and if they resolve into an indefinite, then what is annexed to them is indefinite. You say «مررت في يوم قَدِم زيدٌ الماضي», qualifying «يوم» with a definite, and «جئت ليلةَ قَدِم زيدٌ المباركة علينا». Moreover, «كأنَّ لم يلبثوا» cannot be an adjective of the day as far as the meaning is concerned, because that is a description of those gathered, not a description of the day of their gathering. Some have gone to the trouble of supposing a linking element to connect it, and implied it as «كأن لم يَلْبثوا قبله», omitting «قبله», that is, before the day; and omitting a linking element of this kind is not permissible." I say: his words "some of them" refer to Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: "The kāf and what follows it of «كأنْ» is an adjective of the day, and in the speech a pronoun referring to the qualified noun has been omitted, its implied form being: «كأنْ لم يَلْبثوا قبلَه»; «قبل» was omitted so that the hāʾ became attached to «يَلْبثوا», and it was then omitted because of the length of the noun, as it is omitted from relative clauses (ṣilāt)." Abū l-Baqāʾ also transmitted this implied form without naming who said it, saying "it was said" and then mentioning it.

The second view: that the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «يَحْشُرهم», that is: He gathers them likened to one who had stayed only an hour. This is al-Zamakhsharī's implied form. Among those who also allowed it as a ḥāl are Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ, and some of them made it the apparent view.

The third view: that the clause is an naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied form being: "He gathers them a gathering as though they had not stayed". Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Abū l-Baqāʾ and Makkī mentioned this. Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ also implied the returning element as omitted, as they did when they made the clause an adjective of the day; what is said about that has preceded.

Fourth: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is valid that His saying {كَأَن لَّمْ يلبثوا} is a general statement (kalām mujmal)", and he did not make clear the verb that {كَأَن لَّمْ يلبثوا} contains.

Abū Ḥayyān said: "Perhaps he meant what al-Ḥawfī said, that the kāf is in the position of accusative by what it contains of the meaning of the speech, namely speed." End of quotation. He said: "So the implied form would be: «ويوم يحشرهم يُسرعون كأنْ لم يَلْبثوا»." I say: then «يسرعون» would be a ḥāl from the object of «يَحْشرهم», and {كَأَن لَّمْ يلبثوا} would be a ḥāl from the agent of «يُسْرعون»; and it is also possible that «كأنْ لم» is explicative (mufassira) of the implied «يُسْرعون».

His saying: {يَتَعَارَفُونَ}: there are several views on it. First: that the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «يَلْبثوا». Al-Ḥawfī said: "«يتعارفون» is an imperfect verb in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يلبثوا», which is its governing element, as if he had said «متعارفين»; and the meaning is: they gathered knowing one another." The second: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «يَحْشُرهم», that is: He gathers them knowing one another, the governing element being the verb of gathering. On this, whoever allows multiple ḥāls allows «كأَنْ لم» to be a first ḥāl and this a second ḥāl, and whoever prohibits that makes «كأَنْ لم» something other than a ḥāl, as stated before. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because mutual recognition does not occur at the time of the gathering." The third: that it is resumptive, with Allah the Exalted informing about them of that. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: «كأن لم يَلْبثوا» and «يتعارفون», what is the position of the two? I say: the first is a ḥāl from them, that is: He gathers them likened to one who stayed only an hour; as for the second, either it is attached to the adverbial, meaning it would be a ḥāl, or it is an explanation of His saying «كأن لم يَلْبثوا إلا ساعةً», because mutual recognition does not remain with the passing of long time and turns into mutual denial."

His saying: {قَدْ خَسِرَ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is resumptive, Allah the Exalted informing that those who deny meeting Him are certainly losers, and for that reason He used the particle of affirmation. The other: that it is in the position of accusative by an implied saying, that is: "saying: those who denied have lost". Then for this implied saying you have two views: one, that it is a ḥāl from the object of «يحشرهم», that is: He gathers them saying that; the other, that it is a ḥāl from the agent of «يتعارفون». Al-Zamakhsharī took the view of both resumption and ḥāl from the agent of «يتعارفون», for he said: "It is resumptive, containing the meaning of astonishment, as if it were said: how He gathers them! Then «قد خَسِر» is on the intention of an implied saying, that is: they recognise one another among themselves, saying that." Ibn ʿAṭiyya took the view that it is a ḥāl from the object of «يحشرهم».

His saying: {وَمَا كَانُواْ مُهْتَدِينَ}: two views are possible for it. One: that it is conjoined to His saying «قد خَسِر», so its ruling is its ruling. The other: that it is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين», and it is like an emphasis of the clause that served as the ṣila, because whoever denies the meeting with Allah is not rightly guided.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ}: the discussion of this «إمَّا» has already been given in full. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "On account of it, that is, on account of the redundancy of «ما», the entry of the heavy nūn is permitted; had it been «إنْ» alone, it would not be permitted." He means that emphasising the verb with the nūn is conditional on «ما» being added after «إنْ»; and this contradicts the apparent meaning of Sībawayh's words. Emphasis in a conditional has also occurred without «إنْ», as in the saying:
2598 - مَنْ نثقفَنْ منهم فليس بآيبٍ ... أبداً وقَتْل بني قتيبةَ شافي
(Whomever of them we catch will never return; and the killing of the Banū Qutayba is a cure.)

Ibn Kharūf said: "Sībawayh permitted both bringing «ما» and not bringing it, and both bringing the nūn with «ما» and not bringing it." And the seeing (irāʾa) here is of the eye; for that reason the verb, through the hamza, is made transitive to two objects, that is: "We make you see some of those who were promised."

His saying: {فَإِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُهُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. There are two views on it, the more apparent being that it is the apodosis of the condition and of what is conjoined to it, since its meaning is suited to that. Al-Ḥawfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya took this view. The second: that it is the apodosis of His saying «أو نتوفَيَنَّك», and the apodosis of the first is omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as if it were said: «وإمَّا نُرِيَنَّك بعضَ الذي نَعِدُهم فذاك», or: if We take you before We show you, We shall show you in the Hereafter." Abū Ḥayyān said: "Al-Zamakhsharī thus made two conditions in the speech with two apodoses, but there is no need to [suppose] an omitted apodosis, since His saying «فإلينا مَرْجعهم» is suited to be an apodosis for the condition and what is conjoined to it. Moreover, al-Zamakhsharī's «فذاك» is a single noun from which an apodosis of a condition cannot be formed; he should have brought a sentence from which a valid apodosis can be made, since from «فذاك» the omitted part, by which the benefit of predication is attained, cannot be understood." I say: it is established that a demonstrative may point to two or more things while having a singular form, so «ذاك» is as if placed in the position of the clause that serves as the apodosis; and it is possible that the khabar was omitted because the meaning indicates it, the implied form being: «فذاك المراد» or "the wished-for" or the like. And his saying "since the omitted part cannot be understood" and so on is not conceded; rather it is understood, as you see, and it is something to which the mind readily goes.

His saying: {ثُمَّ الله شَهِيدٌ}: «ثم» here is not for temporal order but for the order of reports, not for the order of the events themselves. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "As in your saying «زيدٌ عالم ثم هو كريم»." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: Allah is witness over what they do in both abodes, so what is the meaning of «ثم»? I say: witnessing is mentioned but what is meant is its consequence and result, namely punishment, as if it were said: then Allah punishes for what they do."

Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ثَمَّ» with fatḥa on the thā, making it an adverbial for Allah's witnessing, so «ثَمَّ» is accusative by «شهيد», that is: Allah is a witness over them in that place, which is the place of their gathering. It is also possible that it is an adverbial for their return (marjiʿ), that is: "to Us is their return", meaning their returning in that place where the doer of good is rewarded and the evildoer punished.

semin-durr:93-93.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ}: It is permissible that it be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "We settled them in a settling of truth" (بَوَّأناهم مُبَوَّأ صِدْقٍ); and that it be a place, that is: "a place of settling in truth". «لمَنْ خَلَفَك» was read with fatḥa on the lām, making it a past verb, the meaning being: "for those who come after you of the tyrants, so that they may take heed by that". «لمَنْ خَلَقَك» was also read, with qāf, a past verb, the subject being Allah the Exalted, that is: "so that Allah may make you a sign among His servants". It is permissible that «مُبَّوَّأ» be accusative as a second object, as in His saying, the Exalted: {لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ الجنة غُرَفَاً}, that is: "We shall surely lodge them".

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِن كُنتَ}: There are two aspects regarding this «إنْ», the apparent one of which is that it is conditional. They then found a difficulty in that, namely that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was never in doubt. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how could He say to His Messenger {فَإِن كُنتَ فِي شَكٍّ} together with His saying to the unbelievers {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِّنْهُ مُرِيبٍ} [Hūd: 110]? I say: there is a great difference between His affirming doubt for them by way of emphasis and verification, and His saying «فإن كنت» in the sense of supposition and illustration." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "When it is conditional, they said: it enters upon what is possible to exist, or what is certain to exist but whose time of occurrence is unspecified, as in His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَإِنْ مِّتَّ فَهُمُ الخالدون} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 34]." He said: "What I say is that the conditional «إنْ» requires the suspension of one thing upon another, and does not necessarily imply that its occurrence is certain or even possible; rather this can be in what is rationally impossible, as in His saying, the Exalted: {إِن كَانَ للرحمن وَلَدٌ فَأَنَاْ أَوَّلُ العابدين} [al-Zukhruf: 81], and it is impossible that He should have a son; so likewise [this]: it is impossible that he should be in doubt; and in what is customarily impossible, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِن استطعت أَن تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقاً فِي الأرض} [al-Anʿām: 35]; but its occurrence in suspending the impossible is rare." Then he said: "Since this aspect was hidden from most people, they differed over how to explain this verse. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: 'The correct view is that it is an address, and the one meant is whoever else of his community could possibly doubt or oppose.' It was said: doubt is used figuratively for distress. It was said: it is used figuratively for wonder, and the aspect of figurative use in it is that each of the two involves hesitation. Al-Kisāʾī said: if you are in doubt that this is their habit with the prophets, then ask them how the patience of Mūsā, peace be upon him, was."
The second of the two aspects of «إنْ» is that it is negative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "that is: 'you were not in doubt, so ask'; meaning We do not command you to ask because you are doubting, but so that you may increase in certainty, as Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, increased by seeing the giving of life to the dead." This view was preceded in it by al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and al-Ḥusayn b. al-Faḍl, and it is as if it is a flight from the difficulty mentioned above in making it conditional; its answer has already been given in several ways.
Yaḥyā and Ibrāhīm read «يَقْرؤون الكتب» in the plural, and this shows that what is meant by "al-kitāb" is the genus and not a single book.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَوْلاَ}: «لولا» here is exhortative (taḥḍīḍiyya) and has the sense of rebuke, as in the saying of al-Farazdaq:
2631 - تَعُدُّون عقر النيبِ أفضلَ مَجْدِكُمْ ... بني ضَوْطَرى لولا الكَمِيَّ المقنَّعا (You count the hamstringing of she-camels as the best of your glory, O sons of the dull-witted woman; why not rather the armoured, helmeted warrior?)
In the codex of Ubayy and that of ʿAbd Allāh it is also read «فهلاَّ», which is explicit in exhortation. And «كانت» here is complete (tāmma), «آمنَتْ» is an adjective of «قرية», and «فَنَفَعَها» is a conjunction on the adjective.
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَوْمَ}: There are two aspects. One: that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), and Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ took this view; for that reason Sībawayh placed it in the chapter of what can only be accusative, because of its being disconnected. It is disconnected only because what follows «إلا» does not fall under the word «قرية». The second: that it is connected. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "an exception from the towns, because their inhabitants are meant; and it may be connected, the sentence being in the sense of negation, as if it were said: 'no town of the destroyed towns believed except the people of Yūnus'."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In terms of the wording it is a disconnected exception, and so the grammarians set it down; in terms of the meaning it is connected, because its implied form is: 'the people of no town believed except the people of Yūnus'." I say: the implying of this muḍāf (genitive-construct first term) is what validates its being a connected exception, and so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, Makkī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others. As for al-Zamakhsharī, the apparent sense of his wording is that what validates its being connected is that the sentence is in the sense of negation; but it is not so; rather what permits it is that "the towns" means their inhabitants, from the usage of naming the place for what occupies it, which is one of the aspects mentioned in His saying: {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82].
A group read «إلا قومُ» in the nominative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was read in the nominative as a badal (substitute); this was reported from al-Jarmī and al-Kisāʾī." Al-Mahdawī said: "The nominative is as a substitute for «قرية»." The apparent sense of these two statements is that it is a transmitted reading, while the apparent sense of the statement of Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ is that it is not a reading and that this is merely permissible; and they made the nominative on a different aspect from badal, namely that «إلا» has the meaning of «غير» in occurring as an adjective. Makkī said: "The nominative is permissible on the basis that «إلا» is made to mean «غير», an adjective of the omitted 'people' in the meaning, and then what follows «إلا» takes the i'rab of «غير» had it appeared in the place of «إلا»." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: and I think he took it from him: "had it been read in the nominative, «إلا» in it would be in the position of «غير», so it would be an adjective." It has already been mentioned that three readings have been read for the nūn of Yūnus.

semin-durr:99-99.t: His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَأَنتَ تُكْرِهُ}: Two aspects are permissible for «أنت». One: that it be nominative by an implied verb explained by the overt one after it, and this is the more preferable, because the noun has directly followed a particle that is more fitting with a verb. The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause after it its khabar (predicate); and what is in that regarding the hamza being placed before the conjunction, or there being an omitted clause there, as is the view of al-Zamakhsharī, is already known. The benefit of placing the noun directly after the interrogative is to inform that compulsion is possible and within one's power, and that the question is only who the compeller is; and it is none but He alone, no other sharing in it with Him. And «حتى» is the limit (ghāya) of compulsion.

semin-durr:100-100.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَن تُؤْمِنَ}: like His saying «أن تموتَ»; that has already been given in Āl ʿImrān.
His saying: {وَيَجْعَلُ}: Abū Bakr, from ʿĀṣim, read it with the nūn of majesty. The rest read it with the yāʾ of the third person, the subject being Allah the Exalted. Al-Aʿmash read it explicitly: {ويجعل اللَّهُ الرِّجْزَ}, with zāy and not sīn; and it has already been discussed whether the two are the same in meaning or differ.

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَاذَا فِي السماوات}: It is permissible that «ماذا» as a whole be interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «في السموات» its khabar (predicate), that is: "What thing is in the heavens?" It is permissible that «ما» be the mubtadaʾ and «ذا» have the meaning of «الذي» (the relative noun), with «في السموات» as its ṣila (relative clause) and also the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. On both analyses the mubtadaʾ and its khabar are in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, because the verb before it is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. It is permissible, though weak, that «ماذا» as a whole be a relative in the sense of «الذي» and in the position of accusative as object of «انظروا». The aspect of its weakness is that it must be one of two: either looking is looking with the eye, so it is made transitive with «إلى», or it is of the heart, so it is made transitive with «في»; and the discussion of «ماذا» has already been given.
His saying: {وَمَا تُغْنِي}: It is permissible that «ما» be interrogative, occurring in the place of a maṣdar, that is: "What benefit do the signs bring?"; and it is permissible that it be negative, and this is the apparent one. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that «ما» in His saying «وما تغني» is an object of His saying «انظروا», conjoined to His saying «ماذا», that is: 'consider the extent of the benefit that the signs and the warnings bring to the unbelievers'." The Shaykh said: "There is weakness in it, and laxity in his saying 'conjoined to «ماذا»', meaning that the interrogative clause {مَاذَا فِي السماوات} is in the position of object, except that «ماذا» alone is accusative by «انظروا», so «ماذا» is relative and «انظروا» is of the eye, because of what preceded" meaning what was said earlier, that if it were of the eye it would be made transitive with «إلى».
And «النُّذُرُ» may be the plural of «نذير», with the maṣdar meant, so the implied form would be: "and the signs and the warnings do not avail"; and it may be the plural of «نذير» with the active participle meant, in the sense of «مُنْذِر» (warner), so the implied form would be: "and the warners", and they are the messengers.

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is conjoined to an omitted statement indicated by «إلا مثلَ أيامِ الذين خَلَوا من قبلهم», as if it had been said: We destroy the nations, then We save Our messengers; it is conjoined to the narration of past states."
His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: There are two aspects regarding this kāf. The more apparent: that it is in the position of accusative, its implied form being: "In the likeness of that saving by which We saved the messengers and their believers, We save whoever believes in you, O Muḥammad." The second: that it is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), which Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū l-Baqāʾ implied with your saying: "The matter is thus" (الأمر كذلك).
His saying: {حَقّاً}: There are several aspects. One: that it is accusative by an implied verb, that is: "that is true, truly" (حَقَّ ذلك حقاً). Second: that it is a badal (substitute) for the omitted word for which the kāf stands in, its implied form being: "a saving like that, truly". Third: that «كذلك» and «حقاً» are both accusative by «نُنْجِ» that follows them. Fourth: that «كذلك» is accusative by the first «نُنَجِّي», and «حقاً» by the second «نُنْج». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the likeness of that saving We save the believers among you and destroy the polytheists, and «حَقّاً علينا» is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ), meaning: that is incumbent upon Us, truly."
Al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ read «نُنْجي المؤمنين» in the light form, from anjā; one says anjā and najjā, like abdala and baddala. The majority of the readers did not report a disagreement except in this, and not in His saying {فاليوم نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ} [Yūnus: 92] nor in His saying {ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي رُسُلَنَا}. Abū ʿAlī al-Ahwāzī has also reported disagreement in the two of them; and in the codices it is written «نُنْجِ» with a jīm and no yāʾ.

semin-durr:104-104.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَلاَ أَعْبُدُ}: It is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the verb is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "so I do not worship" (فأنا لا أعبد). Had the imperfect occurred negated with «لا» without a fāʾ, it would have been jussive; but with the fāʾ it is nominative on what I have told you, and likewise if it were not negated with «لا», as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ الله مِنْهُ} [al-Māʾida: 95], that is: "so He will take vengeance".
His saying: {وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its origin is «بأن أكونَ»", so the preposition was dropped. This dropping may be from the regular omission, which is the omission of prepositions with «أَنْ» [and «أنَّ»], or from the irregular omission, which is in the saying:
2632 - أَمَرْتُكَ الخيرَ. . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (I commanded you the good …)
{فاصدع بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ} [al-Ḥijr: 94]. I say: by the irregular he means that dropping the preposition is heard in verbs on which analogy is not permitted, namely amara and istaghfara, and I mentioned them earlier; and by his saying «أمرتك» he alluded to the famous verse:
أَمَرْتُك الخيرَ فافعلْ ما أُمِرْت به ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (I commanded you the good, so do what you were commanded …)
Some grammarians have applied analogy to this, but it is stipulated that the preposition be uniquely determined and its position also determined; this is the view of ʿAlī b. Sulaymān, who allows «بريتُ القلمَ السكين» ("I sharpened the pen with the knife") in contrast to «صَكَكْت الحجرَ بالخشبة» ("I struck the stone with the stick").

semin-durr:105-105.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنْ أَقِمْ}: It is permissible that it be on the implication of a verb, that is: "and it was revealed to me: that you establish" (وأُوحي إليَّ أَنْ أقم). Then you have two aspects regarding «أنْ». One: that it be explicative (tafsīriyya) of that implied clause; so said the Shaykh, and there is something to consider in it, since the explained may not be dropped, and he himself has rejected this in a place other than this. The second: that it be the maṣdar particle, so that it and what is within its scope are in the position of nominative by that implied verb. It is also possible that «أن» be a maṣdar particle only, and on this it is governed by His saying «أمرْتُ», with the meaning of the speech taken into account, because His saying «أن أكون» is a being among the beings of the believers; and connecting «أَنْ» with the imperative form is permissible, and its verification has already been given.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: conjoining His saying «وأَنْ أقم» to «أن أكونَ» involves a difficulty, because «أنْ» is either the one of expression (the explicative), or the one that is with the verb in the interpretation of a maṣdar; it cannot be the one of expression even if the command contains the meaning of saying, since its being conjoined to the relative one refuses that; and to say that it is a relative like the first is not supported by the form of the command, which is «أَقِمْ», because a ṣila should properly be a clause that admits truth and falsehood. I say: Sībawayh has permitted «أنْ» to be connected with the command and the prohibition, and likened that to their saying «أنت الذي تفعل» in the second person, because the aim is to connect it with what is with it in the interpretation of a maṣdar, and the command and prohibition indicate the maṣdar just as other verbs do." I say: I have previously presented the difficulty in this, namely that when it is implied as a maṣdar, the indication of command and prohibition is lost.
The Shaykh preferred that it be a maṣdar particle with an implied verb, as presented earlier. He said: "so that the awkwardness of the conjunction may vanish because of the presence of the kāf, since had «وأنْ أَقِمْ» been conjoined to «أن أكون», the construction would have been «وجهي» with the yāʾ of the first person [Translator's note: the Shaykh's point concerns «وجهك» in the following {وَأَنْ أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ}, whose kāf of the second person would not agree with «أن أكون»]; and taking the meaning into account in it is weak, while implying the verb is more frequent."
His saying: {حَنِيفاً}: It is permissible that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الذين», and that it be a ḥāl from the agent of «أَقِمْ» or its object.

semin-durr:106-106.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تَدْعُ}: It is permissible that this clause be resumptive, and permissible that it be conjoined to the clause of command, which is «أَقِمْ», so that it enters into the ṣila of «أنْ» in its two aspects, I mean its being explicative or maṣdar; its verification has already been given. And His saying {مَا لاَ يَنفَعُكَ}: it is permissible that it be an indefinite noun that is qualified, and that it be a relative noun.
His saying: {فَإِنَّكَ}: It is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «إذن» is a particle of response that has been placed between the noun and the khabar (predicate); its proper rank is after the khabar, and it was put in the middle only out of regard for the verse-endings. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إذن» is the response to the condition and a response to an implied question, as if a questioner had asked about the consequence of worshipping idols." There is something to consider in making «إذن» a requital for the condition, since the apodosis is restricted to certain things of which this is not one.

semin-durr:107-107.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن يَمْسَسْكَ}: What is in it of the art of badīʿ (rhetorical embellishment) has already been given in Sūrat al-Anʿām.
