Here He said in the apodosis of the first condition a general negation and an affirmation, and in the apodosis of the second a general negation without affirmation, because what He wills no one can repel, neither he nor any other, since His will is eternal and does not change; for that reason the construction did not come as «فلا رادَّ له إلا هو». This is the wording of the Shaykh, and there is something to consider in it; it is as if he says, in contrast to removal (of harm), for He alone does that, no one else, whereas His will, the Exalted, cannot be conceived to occur contrary to it; and it is a matter of disagreement between the Sunnis and the Muʿtazilites. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why is touching mentioned in one and will in the other? I say: it is as if He wanted to mention both things together, will and befalling, in each of harm and good, and that there is none who repels what He wills of them, nor any who removes what He inflicts of them; so He made the speech concise by mentioning touching, which is befalling, in one, and will in the other, to indicate by what He mentioned what He left out; moreover, He has mentioned befalling in the case of good in His saying: {يُصَيبُ بِهِ مَن يَشَآءُ}."

semin-durr:108-108.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {مِن رَّبِّكُمْ}: It is permissible that it be attached to «جاءكم», with «مِنْ» for the beginning of the limit (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya) figuratively; and it is permissible that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الحق».
His saying: {فَمَنُ اهتدى} and «ومَنْ ضَلَّ»: It is permissible that «مَنْ» be conditional, in which case the fāʾ is obligatory; and that it be a relative noun, in which case the fāʾ is permissible.
His saying: {وَمَآ أَنَاْ}: It is permissible that it be the Ḥijāzī or the Tamīmī «ما», because the accusative is hidden in the khabar. The rest is clear.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ الله}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), its implied form being: except what Allah wills that I possess and have power over. The other: that it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a disconnected exception, that is: but whatever Allah wills of that will come to be; so how could I possess for you harm and the bringing of punishment?"

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: the discussion of this «أَرَأَيْتَ» has already preceded, and that it contains the meaning of «أخبرني» ("tell me"), so it takes two objects, the second of which is generally an interrogative clause, which together with what precedes it forms a mubtadaʾ and khabar, as in their saying «أرأيتَك زيداً ما صنع». The views of the scholars on it were given in Sūrat al-Anʿām, so you should consider it there. Its first object in this noble verse is omitted, and the question belongs to the chapter of iʿmāl (operation, tanāzuʿ), because «أرأيت» and «أتاكم» contend over «عذاب»; this is a case of giving operation to the second, since that is the preferred view of the Basrans. When he gave operation to the second, he made a pronoun in the first and omitted it, because retaining it is restricted to poetic necessity, or is permitted to mention on rare occasions according to others; and had he given operation to the first, he would have put a pronoun in the second, since omission from it occurs only in necessity or in a small amount of speech. The meaning of the speech: say to them, Muḥammad: tell me about Allah's punishment, if it comes to you, what thing of it do you seek to hasten? Yet no punishment is something to be hastened, because of its bitterness and the severity of its striking, so it necessitates the revulsion of the natural disposition from it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: to what does the interrogative attach, and where is the apodosis of the condition? I say: it attaches to «أرأيتم», because the meaning is: tell me what it is that the criminals seek to hasten of it; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, namely «تَنْدموا على الاستعجال» ('you will regret the hastening') or «تعرفوا الخطأ فيه' ('you will recognise the error in it')." Abū Ḥayyān said: "What he implied is not acceptable, because the apodosis is implied only from what has preceded it in wording or in implication. You say «أنت ظالمٌ إن فعلت», the implied form being «إن فعلت فأنت ظالم»; likewise {وَإِنَّآ إِن شَآءَ الله لَمُهْتَدُونَ} [al-Baqara: 70], the implied form being «إن شاءَ الله نَهْتَدِ». What makes it acceptable to imply is: «إن أتاكم عذابه فأخبروني ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون»."

Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "It is possible that «ماذا يَسْتعجل منه المجرمون» is the apodosis of the condition, as in your saying: «إنْ أَتَيْتك ما تُطْعمني؟», and then the clause attaches to «أرأيتم»; and it is possible that «أثُمَّ إذا ما وقع آمنتم به» is the apodosis of the condition, and «ماذا يَسْتعجل منه المجرمون» a parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ), the meaning being: if His punishment comes to you, you will believe in it after its occurrence, when belief will not benefit you." Abū Ḥayyān said: "As for his allowing «ماذا» to be the apodosis of the condition, that is not valid, for when the apodosis of a condition is interrogative, the fāʾ is required in it. You say: «إنْ زارنا فلان فأيُّ رجل هو», «وإن زارَنا فلانٌ فأيُّ يدٍ له بذلك»; and it may not be omitted except in necessity; and the example he mentioned, «إن أتيتك ما تُطْعمني؟», is of his own making and not from the speech of the Arabs. As for his saying 'then the clause attaches to «أرأيتم»': if he means by the clause «ماذا يَسْتعجل», that is not valid, because he has made it the apodosis of the condition; and if he means by the clause the conditional clause, then he himself has explained «أرأيتم» as meaning «أخبروني», and «أخبرني» requires an attached object, and a conditional clause does not take the place of the object of «أخبرني»."

"As for his allowing «أثم إذا ما وقع آمنتم به» to be the apodosis of the condition, and «ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون» a parenthetical clause, that is also not valid, for what we mentioned, that an interrogative clause does not serve as an apodosis of a condition unless accompanied by the fāʾ of the apodosis; moreover, «ثم» here is a conjunction particle that conjoins the clause after it to the one before it, so the interrogative clause is conjoined, and if it is conjoined it cannot be the apodosis of the condition; moreover, «أرأيتم» in the sense of «أخبروني» needs an object, and a conditional clause does not take its place."

That «أرأيتم» has the meaning «أخبروني» is the apparent and well-known view. Al-Ḥawfī said: "The seeing is the seeing of the heart, which has the meaning of knowing, because it enters upon an interrogative clause whose meaning is affirmation (taqrīr), and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, the implied form of the speech being: do you see what the criminals seek to hasten of the punishment, if His punishment comes to you?" End of quotation. This is apparent in that «أرأيتم» does not contain the meaning of informing, and that the interrogative clause fills the place of the two objects; but the first is the well-known view.

His saying: {مَّاذَا يَسْتَعْجِلُ}: the discussion of this word and the views of the scholars on it has already preceded. Some here allowed that «ما» is a mubtadaʾ and «ذا» its khabar, a relative noun meaning «الذي», with «يستعجل» as its ṣila and its returning pronoun omitted, the implied form being: what thing is it that he seeks to hasten of it, that is, of the punishment, or of Allah the Exalted. Others, such as Makkī and his peers, allowed that «ماذا» in its entirety is a mubtadaʾ, that is, the two nouns are made into the equivalent of one noun, and the clause after it is its khabar. Abū ʿAlī said: "It is weak, because the clause lacks a pronoun returning to the mubtadaʾ." Abū l-Baqāʾ answered this, saying: "This view was rejected on the ground that the hāʾ in «منه» returns to the mubtadaʾ, as in your saying «زيدٌ أَخَذْتُ منه درهماً»." I say: someone like Abū ʿAlī would not miss such a thing; rather, he does not hold that the hāʾ returns to the relative, because it apparently returns to «العذاب». Abū Ḥayyān said: "The apparent meaning is that the pronoun in «منه» returns to the punishment, and through this the linking of the interrogative clause to the omitted object of «أرأيتم», which is originally a mubtadaʾ, is attained." Makkī said: "If you wish, you may make «ما» and «ذا» the equivalent of one noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, with the clause after it as the khabar, and the hāʾ in «منه» likewise returns to the punishment." I say: so the mubtadaʾ is left without a verbal link, since he made the hāʾ return to something other than the mubtadaʾ; the returning element according to him would then be omitted. But he said after that: "If you make the hāʾ in «منه» return to Allah, may His mention be glorified, and «ما» and «ذا» one noun, then «ما» is in the position of accusative by «يستعجل», and the meaning is: what thing do the criminals seek to hasten from Allah?" This saying of his indicates that, when the pronoun returns to something other than the mubtadaʾ, he made it a fronted object; and this very view is also permissible if the pronoun is made to return to the punishment. And the view of nominative as mubtadaʾ is permissible if the pronoun is made to return to Allah the Exalted, since the linking returning element is implied, as was pointed out earlier.

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَثُمَّ}: al-Zamakhsharī's disagreement with the majority on this has already preceded, in that he implies a clause between the hamza of interrogation and the conjunction particle. «ثمَّ» is a conjunction particle. Al-Ṭabarī said something that is not agreed with, for he said: "This «أثُمَّ» with ḍamma on the thā is not the one with the meaning of conjunction; rather it has the meaning of «هنالك» ('there')." If he intended an explanation of the meaning, which is remote, then he was vague in his statement, because this meaning is not known for «ثُمَّ» with ḍamma on the thā; except that Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «أثَمَّ» with fatḥa on the thā, and in that case its explanation as meaning «هنالك» is valid.

His saying: {الآنَ}: the discussion of «الآن» has already preceded. The majority read «ألآن» with the hamza of interrogation entering upon «الآن», and the views of the readers on that have been given. «الآن» is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being: «الآن آمنتم». What indicates this implied verb is the verb that preceded it, namely His saying: {أَثُمَّ إِذَا مَا وَقَعَ آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ}. The overt «آمنتم» cannot operate on it, because what precedes an interrogative does not operate on what follows it, just as what follows it does not operate on what precedes it, since it has the front of the speech (ṣadr al-kalām). This implied verb and its object rest on an implied saying, that is: it was said to them when they believed after the occurrence of the punishment: "Now you believe in it!"

The reading with the interrogative is the reading of the common readers, and you have learned its analysis. ʿĪsā and Ṭalḥa read «آمنتم به الآن» with a connecting hamza and without interrogation, and on this reading «الآن» is accusative by «آمنتم»; this is the apparent view.

His saying: {وَقَدْ كُنتُم}: a ḥāl clause. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "{وَقَدْ كُنتُم بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ} means «تُكَذِّبون» ('you deny'), because their hastening was by way of denial and rejection." I say: so he made it an instance of kināya (metonymy), because it is an indication of a thing by its concomitant, as in «هو طويلُ النِّجاد» ('he has a long baldric'), by which you allude to the tallness of his stature, since the length of his baldric is concomitant to the tallness of his stature; and it is an eloquent chapter.

semin-durr:52-52.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ قِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ}: on the reading of the common readers, this clause is conjoined to that implied verb which governs «الآن» in the accusative; on Ṭalḥa's reading it is a resumptive report about what will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection. «ذوقوا» and «هل تُجْزَوْن» are all in the position of accusative by the saying. His saying «إلا بما» is the second object of «تُجْزَون», the first being in the position of the agent [Translator's note: i.e. it is a deputy agent], and it is a complete exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh).

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَحَقٌّ هُوَ}: it is possible that «حَقٌّ» is a mubtadaʾ and «هو» is nominative as agent, filling the place of the khabar. Although «حق» is originally a maṣdar, not in the sense of an active or passive participle, it is equivalent in force to «ثابت» ("established"), and for that reason it makes an overt noun nominative. It is also possible that «حَقٌّ» is a fronted khabar and «هو» a delayed mubtadaʾ.

There is disagreement about this «يَسْتَنْبِئُونك»: whether it takes one object, two or three. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ويَسْتَنْبِئونك فيقول: أحقٌّ هو»". The apparent sense of this expression is that it takes one object, and that the interrogative clause is in the position of accusative by that implied saying, which is conjoined to «يَسْتَنْبِئُونك»; and Abū Ḥayyān understood him likewise, I mean that it takes one. Makkī said: "«أحقٌّ هو» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the second object if you take «يستنبؤنك» to mean «يَسْتَخْبِرونك» ('they ask you for news'); if you take «يستنبئونك» to mean «يَسْتَعْلِمونك' ('they ask you to inform them'), then «أحقٌّ هو» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of two objects, because «أَنْبأ», when it has the meaning of «أَعْلَم», is transitive to three objects, one of which may be sufficient, though two without the third may not; and when «أنبأ» means «أَخْبر» it takes two objects, and one without the second may not suffice; and «أنبأ» and «نبَّأ» are alike in transitivity." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its meaning is «يَسْتَخْبرونك», and on this it takes two objects, one the kāf and the other in the mubtadaʾ and khabar." According to what he said, «يَسْتنبئونك» is suspended by the interrogative, and the basic rule of «استنبأ» is that it takes two objects, one of them with «عن»; you say «اسْتَنْبأت زيداً عن عمرو», that is: I asked him to inform me about ʿAmr. Then he said: "The apparent view is that it needs three objects, one the kāf, and the mubtadaʾ and khabar fill the place of the two objects." Abū Ḥayyān said: "It is not as he said, because it is not memorised that «استعلم» is transitive to three objects; «استعملت زيداً عمراً قائماً» is not memorised, so that the interrogative clause would fill the place of two objects. And it does not follow from its meaning «يَسْتعلمونك» that it takes three, because «استعلم» does not take three, as we mentioned."

I say: Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib preceded Abū Muḥammad to this, as I related from him earlier, and the apparent view is that this is permissible, with the transitivity to a third having been brought about by the sīn, because they have stated that the sīn makes a verb transitive; so the original would be «علم زيدٌ عمراً قائماً», and then you say «استعلمْتُ زيداً عمراً قائماً». But the grammarians have stated that only «عَلِم» and «رأى», when made transitive to a third by the particularity of the hamza of transitivity, take three objects, along with «أنبأ», «نَبَّأ», «أخبر», «خبَّر» and «حدَّث».

Al-Aʿmash read «آلحقُّ» with the lām of definiteness. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is more fitting for mockery, because it contains the meaning of insinuation that it is false; this is because the lām is generic, as if it were said: is it the truth, not the falsehood? Or: is it that which you have named the truth?"

His saying: {إي}: a particle of response meaning «نعم» ("yes"), but it is restricted to oaths, that is: it is used only in an oath, unlike «نعم». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إي» means «نعم» in oaths specifically, as «هل» means «قد» in interrogation specifically; and I heard them say in affirmation «إيْوَ», joining it with the wāw of the oath, and not pronouncing it alone." Abū Ḥayyān said: "There is no proof in what he heard, because there is no proof in the speech of those he heard, owing to the corruption of their speech and of the speech of those many ages before them." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a word that precedes the oath with the meaning of «نعم», and the particle of oath may come after it, or may not; you say «إي وربي», «إي ربي»."

His saying: {وَمَآ أَنتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ}: it may be the Hijazi «ما» and it may be the Tamimi, because the accusative or nominative is not apparent in the khabar. This is according to those other than al-Fārisī and his followers, meaning that the addition of the bāʾ in the khabar of the Tamimi «ما» is permissible. This clause admits two views. One: that it is conjoined to the answer of the oath, so that the oath is answered with two clauses, one affirmative, emphasised with «إنَّ» and the lām, and the other negative, emphasised by the redundancy of the bāʾ. The second: that it is resumptive, brought to inform of their inability to render powerless. «مُعْجز» is from «أعجز», and it is transitive to one, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَن نُّعْجِزَهُ هَرَباً} [al-Jinn: 12]; so the object here is omitted, that is: "not able to make Allah powerless". Al-Zajjāj said: "That is: you are not among those who can make powerless the one who punishes you." It is also possible that it is used as an intransitive, because omission of its object has become frequent, until the Arabs said «أعْجزَ فلانٌ» when someone has gone off into the land and cannot be overtaken.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَفْتَدَتْ بِهِ}: «افتدى» may be transitive and may be intransitive. When it is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of «فَدَى» it is intransitive; you say «فَدَيْتُه فافتدى», and it can have the meaning of «فَدَى» and so take one object. The verb here admits both views: if we take it as transitive, its object is omitted, the implied form being: «لافتدَتْ به نفسَها» ("she would have ransomed herself with it"), and it is figurative, as in His saying: {كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَن نَّفْسِهَا} [al-Naḥl: 111].

And His saying: {وَأَسَرُّواْ}: it was said that «أسرَّ» is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād), used in the sense of "make manifest", as in the saying of al-Farazdaq:
2599 - ولمَّا رأى الحجَّاجَ جرَّد سيفَه ... أسَرَّ الحَرُوريُّ الذي كانوا أضمرا
(When he saw al-Ḥajjāj draw his sword, the Ḥarūrī made manifest what they had concealed.)
and the saying of another:
2600 - فأسرَرْتُ الندامةَ يوم نادى ... بِرَدِّ جِمالِ غاضِرةَ المُنادي
(I made my regret manifest on the day the crier called for the return of Ghāḍira's camels.)
It is also used in the sense of "concealed", which is the well-known meaning in the language, as in His saying: {يَعْلَمُ مَا تُسِرُّونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ} [al-Naḥl: 19]. In the verse it admits both meanings. It was also said that it is a past verb in its basic sense, which has already occurred. And it was said: rather, it has a future sense. Some have gone far afield, saying: «أسرُّوا الندامةَ» means that the lines (asirra) of their faces became manifest with regret, that is, the creases of their foreheads.

And {لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ}: it may be a particle, with its answer omitted because what precedes indicates it, that being the position of one who holds that fronting the apodosis of a condition is permissible. It may also mean «حين» ("when"), with «أسَرُّوا» governing it. His saying «ظلَمْت» is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «نفس», that is: "for every wrongdoing soul". And {مَّا فِي الأرض} is the noun of «أن», and «لكلٍ» is the khabar.

And His saying: {وَقُضِيَ}: it may be resumptive, which is the apparent view, and it may be conjoined to «رأوا», so that it falls within the scope of «لَمَّا». The pronoun in «بينهم» refers to «كل نفس» in meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Between the wrongdoers and the wronged; the mention of wrongdoing indicates that." And some said that it refers to the leaders and the followers. As for «بالقسط», the bāʾ may be for accompaniment and may be for instrumentality.

semin-durr:56-56.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ}: He put the preposition and its genitive noun first for restriction, that is: to Him, not to anyone else, you will be returned, and also for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil). The common readers read «تُرْجَعون» in the second person. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «يُرْجَعُون» with yāʾ of the third person.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ}: «مِنْ» may be for the beginning of the range (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), in which case it is attached to «جاءَتْكم», the beginning of the range being figurative; and it may be partitive, in which case it is attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «موعظة», that is: an admonition that is one of the admonitions of your Lord. His saying: {مَّوْعِظَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَشِفَآءٌ لِّمَا فِي الصدور وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ} is of the chapter where attributes are conjoined one upon another, that is: there has come to you an admonition comprising all of these things.

«شِفاء» is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) made into a description for emphasis, or it is a noun for that by which one is healed, that is, treated, so it is like medicine for what is treated. {لِّمَا فِي الصدور} may be an adjective of «شفاء», in which case it is attached to an omitted element, or the lām may be redundant in the object, because the governing element is derivative if we say that it is a maṣdar. His saying «للمؤمنين» admits these two views, and it is an instance of tanāzuʿ (contention), because each of «الهدى» and «الرحمة» seeks it.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بِفَضْلِ الله وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ}: there are several views on what this preposition-and-noun is attached to. First: that «بفضل» and «برحمته» are attached to an omitted element, its implied form being: "in the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, let them rejoice in that, so let them rejoice"; the first verb was omitted because the second indicates it, so they are two clauses. This is indicated by al-Zamakhsharī's saying: "The original of the speech is: «بفضل الله وبرحمته فَلْيفرحوا فبذلك»; the repetition is for emphasis and affirmation and to make obligatory the restriction of rejoicing to the bounty and the mercy, apart from the other benefits of this world. So one of the two verbs was omitted because what is mentioned indicates it, and the fāʾ enters with the meaning of a condition, as if it were said: if they rejoice in anything, let them single these two out for rejoicing, for nothing is more deserving of rejoicing than these two."

Second: that the first preposition-and-noun is also attached to an omitted element indicated by the context and meaning, not by the actual verb that is pronounced, the implied form being: "in Allah's bounty and mercy let them take care, and in that let them rejoice." Al-Zamakhsharī said this.

Third: that the first preposition-and-noun is attached to «جاءتكم». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible to intend: «قد جاءَتْكم موعظةٌ بفضلِ الله وبرحمته فبذلك فليفرحوا», that is, in its coming let them rejoice." Abū Ḥayyān said: "As for implying «فليعتنوا», there is no evidence for it." I say: the indication of it from the context is clear, and it is not a condition that the indication be verbal.

Abū Ḥayyān said: "As for attaching it to His saying «قد جاءتكم», it should be implied as omitted after «قل», and it should not be attached to the first «جاءتكم» because of the separation between them by «قل»." I say: this is a clear objection. It is also possible that «بفضل الله» is an adjective of «موعظة», that is: an admonition accompanied by, or connected with, Allah's bounty.

Fourth: al-Ḥawfī said: "The bāʾ is attached to what the meaning indicates, that is: the admonition has come to you by Allah's bounty."

Fifth: that the first fāʾ is redundant, and that His saying «بذلك» is a badal (substitute) of what precedes it, namely {بِفَضْلِ الله وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ}, and «ذلك» points to two things, namely the bounty and the mercy, as in His saying: {لاَّ فَارِضٌ وَلاَ بِكْرٌ عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68], and as in the saying:
2601 - إنَّ للخيرِ وللشرِ مَدَى ... وكِلا ذلك وَجْهٌ وقَبَلْ
(Good and evil each have a limit; and both of those are a face and a front.)

There are several views on these two fāʾs. One: that the first is redundant, and its exposition has preceded in the fifth view. Two: that the second fāʾ is repeated for emphasis; on this the first is not redundant, and the original construction would be: «فبذلك ليفرحوا», whereas on the earlier view the original construction would be: «بذلك فَلْيفرحوا». Three: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The first fāʾ is connected with what precedes it, and the second with an omitted verb, its implied form being: «فليَعْجبوا بذلك فَلْيفرحوا», like their saying «زيداً فاضربه», that is: «تَعمَّدْ زيداً فاضْرِبه» ('aim for Zayd, and strike him')."

The majority read «فَلْيفرحوا» with yāʾ of the third person. ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, Ubayy, Anas, al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Ibn Hurmuz and Ibn Sīrīn read it with tāʾ of the second person, and this is the reading of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the original and the analogical form."

Abū Ḥayyān said: "It is a rare dialect," meaning that the analogical form is for the one addressed to be commanded with the form «افعل»; and by this original form Ubayy read «فافرحوا», and so it is in his codex. This is a general rule: the command with lām is frequent for the third person and for the second person in the passive. An example of the first: «ليقم زيدٌ»; and likewise the noble verse in the reading of the majority. An example of the second: «ليُعْنَ بحاجتي», «ولتُضْرَبْ يا زيد». If it is active, it is rare, as in the reading of ʿUthmān and those with him. In the ḥadīth: «لتأخذوا مصافَّكم». Rather, what is frequent in this type is the command in the form «افْعَلْ», such as «قم يا زيد» and «قوموا». Likewise the command with lām is weak for the speaker alone or together with others; the first is like «لأقُمْ», where you command yourself to stand, and from it is his saying, peace be upon him: «قوموا فلأصلّ لكم».

An example of the second: «لنقمْ», that is, "let us stand"; and likewise prohibition, and from it is the saying of the poet:
2602 - إذا ما خَرَجْنا مِنْ دمشقَ فلا نَعُدْ ... بها أبداً ما دام فيها الجُراضِمُ
(When we have left Damascus, let us never return to it so long as the glutton is in it.)

Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted from Ibn ʿĀmir that he read «فَلْتَفْرحوا» in the second person, but this is not well known from him. Al-Ḥasan and Abū l-Tayyāḥ read «فَلِيفرحوا» with kasra on the lām, which is the original.

His saying: {هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ}: «هو» refers to the bounty and the mercy, although they are two things, because they are in the sense of one thing expressed with two words by way of emphasis; for that reason they are pointed to with the demonstrative for one. Ibn ʿĀmir read «تَجْمعون» with tāʾ in the second person, which admits two views. One: that it is an instance of iltifāt (shift of person), in which case its meaning is like the reading of the group, since the pronoun is meant to refer to those to whom the pronoun in «فَلْيفرحوا» refers. The second: that it is addressed to His saying: {ياأيها الناس قَدْ جَآءَتْكُمْ} [Yūnus: 57], and this reading fits the reading in the second person in His saying «فَلْيفرحوا»; it has already been mentioned that Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted that from him also.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: this has the meaning of «أخبروني» ("tell me"). His saying «ما أنزل»: «ما» may be a relative noun meaning «الذي», with the returning pronoun omitted, that is «ما أنزله», in the position of accusative as the first object, and the second is the clause of His saying: {ءَآللَّهُ أَذِنَ لَكُمْ}, the pronoun returning from this clause to the first object being omitted, its implied form being: «اللَّهُ أَذِن لكم فيه». This has been objected to on the ground that His saying «قُلْ» prevents the clause after it from being a second object; it was answered that it is repeated for emphasis. It is also possible that «ما» is interrogative, in the position of accusative by «أَنْزَلَ», and then it is suspended from «أَرَأَيْتم»; al-Ḥawfī and al-Zamakhsharī took this view. It is further possible that the interrogative «ما» is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the clause {ءَآللَّهُ أَذِنَ لَكُمْ} as its khabar and the returning pronoun omitted as before, that is, «أَذِن لكم فيه», and this interrogative clause is suspended from «أَرَأَيتم». The apparent one of these views is the first, because it keeps «أرأيت» in its basic usage of taking two objects, and of operating on the first of them, in contrast to making «ما» interrogative, which suspends «أرأيت» and fills the place of the two objects.

And His saying: {مِّن رِّزْقٍ}: it may be a ḥāl from the relative noun, and «مِنْ» may be for explanation of the kind, and «أنزل» is in its basic sense, on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: He sent it down from a cause of provision, namely rain. It was also said that "sending down" is used loosely for creation, as in His saying {وَأَنزْلْنَا الحديد} [al-Ḥadīd: 25] and {وَأَنزَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ الأنعام} [al-Zumar: 6].

His saying: {أَمْ عَلَى الله تَفْتَرُونَ}: there are two views on this «أم». One: that it is the connected «أم», conjoining, its implied form being: "tell me: did Allah permit you to make lawful and unlawful, for they do that by His permission, or do you lie against Allah in ascribing that to Him?" The second: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that the hamza is for denial and «أم» is disconnected, meaning: rather, do you fabricate against Allah? by way of affirming the fabrication." The apparent view is the first, since the equivalence between these two clauses, which are in the sense of two single elements, is clear, the implied form being: which of the two matters occurred: Allah's permission to you in that, or your fabrication against Him?

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا ظَنُّ}: «ما» is an interrogative mubtadaʾ, and «ظنُّ» is its khabar; «يومَ» is accusative by the very word «الظن», the maṣdar being annexed to its agent, and the two objects of «الظن» are omitted. The meaning is: what do those who fabricate think on the Day of Resurrection that I shall do with them? Shall I save them from the punishment, or take vengeance on them?

ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «وما ظَنَّ الذين», making it a past verb with the relative noun as its agent. On this reading «ما» is also interrogative, in the position of accusative as a maṣdar, and it is fronted because the interrogative has the front of the speech; the implied form being: "What thought did the fabricators think?" The interrogative «ما» may take the place of the maṣdar, and from it is the saying of the poet:
2603 - ماذا يَغيرُ ابنَتْي رَبْعٍ عويلُهما ... لا تَرْقُدان ولا بؤسى لمَنْ رَقَدا
(What good does the wailing of the two daughters of Rabʿ do them? They do not sleep, and there is no misfortune for the one who sleeps.)
And you say «ما تَضْرب زيداً», meaning: what beating are you beating? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He brought it as a past verb because it will inevitably happen, so it is as if it had already happened and passed." This is not right here, because it has become explicitly future by its operating on the future adverbial, namely the Day of Resurrection, even though it has the form of the past.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا تَكُونُ فِي شَأْنٍ وَمَا تَتْلُواْ}: «ما» is negative in both places, and for that reason he conjoined by repeating the negative «لا», and made «إلا» obligatory after the verbs because they are negated. «في شأن» is the khabar of «تكون»; the pronoun in «منه» refers to «شأن», and «مِنْ قرآن» is an explanation of the pronoun, singled out from the general because the Qur'an is the greatest of his affairs ﷺ. It was also said that it refers to the revelation (tanzīl), and is explained by the Qur'an because every part of it is Qur'an, and it was made a pronoun before mention only to honour it. It was also said that it refers to Allah, that is: "and you do not recite from Allah any Qur'an." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«من الشأن», that is, on account of it; and «من قرآن» is the object of «تتلو», and «مِنْ» is redundant." He means that it is added to the direct object, and the first «من» is a preposition for the object of purpose, its implied form being: "and you do not recite, on account of the affair, any Qur'an"; it is added because the speech is not affirmative and the genitive noun is indefinite. Makkī said: "«منه»: according to al-Farrāʾ the hāʾ refers to the affair, on the implied omission of a muḍāf, the implied form being: «وما تتلو من أجل الشأن», that is: an affair occurs to you and you recite the Qur'an on account of it."

«الشَّأْنُ» is the maṣdar of «شَأنَ يَشْأَنُ شَأَنَه», that is, «قَصَد يَقْصِدُ قَصْدَه» ("he aimed"); its original has a hamza, and it may be lightened. «الشأن» also means "the matter", and its plural is «شُؤُون».

And His saying: {إِلاَّ كُنَّا}: this clause is a ḥāl clause, and it is a complete exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). A past verb follows «إلا» here without «قد» because a verb has preceded it, and that permits it.

His saying «إذ»: this adverbial is governed by «شُهودا». Since the preceding verbs are meant to express the continuous state and extend over the past actions, the adverbial is past, and the meaning is: "You were not, you are not, and you did not do, except that We were witnesses over you, except that you plunged into it." «إذ» restricts the imperfect to the past sense.

His saying: {وَمَا يَعْزُبُ}: al-Kisāʾī read here and in Sabaʾ «يَعْزِب» with kasra on the ʿayn, and the rest with ḍamma; they are two dialects in the imperfect of «عَزَبَ». One says «عَزَب يَعْزِب» and «يَعْزُب», that is: he was absent until he was hidden, and from it is «الروضُ العازِبُ» ("the remote meadow"). Abū Tammām said:
2604 - وقَلْقَلَ نَأْيٌ مِنْ خراسانَ جَأْشَها ... فقلتُ اطمئنِّي أَنْضَرُ الروضِ عزِبُه
(Distance from Khurasan unsettled her heart; I said: be at ease, the greenest meadow is the remote one.)
One who is absent from his family is called «عازِب», until they called one who has no wife «عازب». Al-Rāghib said: "«العازِبُ»: one who goes far in seeking pasture. One says «رجل عَزَبٌ» and «امرأة عَزَبة»; and «عَزَب عنه حِلْمُه», that is, it was absent; and «قوم مُعَزَّبون», that is, their camels have strayed from them. In the ḥadīth: «من قرأ القرآن في أربعين يوماً فقد عَزَب», that is, his acquaintance with finishing it has grown remote." Al-Harawī said something close to this, for he said: "that is, his acquaintance with what he began of it grew remote and he was slow in reciting it." And in the ḥadīth of Umm Maʿbad: «والشاءُ عازِبٌ حِيال», he said: "«العازِب»: one who goes far in the pasture. And «الحائل»: the one the male has covered but which has not conceived because of the barrenness of the year." And in the ḥadīth also: «أصبحنا بأرضٍ عَزيبةٍ صحراءَ», that is, a land remote from pasture. Absent property is called «عازِب», and present property «عاهِن». The meaning in the verse: "nothing is remote from, or hidden from, or absent from your Lord."

«مِنْ مِثْقال» is the agent, with «مِنْ» added to it, that is: "no weight of an atom is remote from Him." «المثْقال» here is a noun, not an adjective, and what is meant by it is weight, that is, the weight of an atom.

His saying: {وَلاَ أَصْغَرَ مِن ذلك ولا أَكْبَرَ}: Ḥamza read «أَصْغر» and «أكبر» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and the rest with fatḥa. As for the fatḥa, there are two views. One, held by most of the grammarians who parse, is that it is genitive, and it has fatḥa because it is a diptote on account of the pattern and the adjective, the genitive being because it is conjoined to a genitive, either «مثقال» or «ذرة». The second view is that «لا» is the lā of generic negation and «أصغر» and «أكبر» are its noun, both being indeclinable on fatḥa. As for the ḍamma, it also has two views. The better known of the two among the grammarians is: conjoining to the position of «مثقال», since it is nominative as agent and «مِنْ» is added to it, as you say «ما قام مِنْ رجل ولا امرأة», with «امرأة» genitive or nominative. The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The better view is the accusative for generic negation, and the nominative as mubtadaʾ so that it is a speech in itself. In conjoining to the position of «مثقال ذرة», or to the form of «مثقال ذرة» with fatḥa in the position of genitive because of the prohibition of tanwīn, there is a difficulty, because your saying «لا يَعْزُب عنه شيءٌ إلا في كتاب» is problematic." End of quotation. These two views are al-Zajjāj's choice. It is problematic according to him because the implied form becomes: "except in a clear book, then it is absent", which is a speech that is not valid. This difficulty may be removed by what Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned, namely that {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ} is a disconnected exception. He said: {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ}, that is, "except that it is in a book", and the exception is disconnected.

Imām Fakhr al-Dīn said, after relating the difficulty mentioned: "Some of the investigators answered in two ways. One: that the exception is disconnected. The other: that absence is an expression for absolute remoteness, and created things are of two kinds: a kind that Allah brought into being directly, without an intermediary, such as the angels, the heavens and the earth; and a kind He brought into being through the first kind, such as events occurring in the world of generation and corruption. This latter may be far removed, in the chain of cause and effect, from the rank of the existence of the Necessarily Existent. So the meaning is: the weight of an atom on earth or in heaven is not remote from the rank of His existence without being in a clear book, which Allah wrote and in which He established the forms of those objects of knowledge."

I say: the matter has come down to his making it a complete exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), which is a ḥāl from «أصغر» and «أكبر», and it is in force like a connected exception; one does not say of this that it is connected or disconnected, since of a complete exception that is not said.

Al-Jurjānī said: "«إلا» has the meaning of the wāw, that is: «وهو في كتاب مبين»; the Arabs put «إلا» in the place of the conjunctive wāw, as in His saying: {إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 148] and {إِلاَّ الذين ظَلَمُواْ مِنْهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 150]." This which al-Jurjānī said is very weak; the discussion of this question has already preceded in al-Baqara, and that it is something al-Akhfash said, and it has not been established by sound evidence. The Shaykh Abū Shāma said: "The difficulty is removed by implying, before His saying {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ}, «ليس شيء من ذلك إلا في كتاب», and likewise you imply in the verse of al-Anʿām."

In Sabaʾ it is read only with the nominative, and that strengthens the view of those who say that it is conjoined to «مثقال», and it is made clear by the fact that «مثقال» there is nominative, there being no preposition before it. The discussion of the counterpart of this question and the difficulty in it has already preceded in Sūrat al-Anʿām in His saying: {وَمَا تَسْقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ} [Yūnus: 59], up to {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ} [Yūnus: 59]. [Translator's note: the source says "al-Anʿām" while citing a verse of Yūnus; translated as written.] There, the author of «al-Naẓm», this al-Jurjānī, referred the discussion of it to the discussion in this sūra, and Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If we made it so, the meaning would be corrupted"; and I explained the demonstration of its corruption and the answer to it at length there, so you should consider it and transfer what can be transferred here.

semin-durr:63-63.t: His saying, the Exalted: {الذين آمَنُواْ}: there are several views on its position. First: that it is nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "they are those who believed"; or as a second khabar of «إنَّ»; or as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause of «لهم البشرى»; or as an naʿt of the position of «أولياء», since its position is nominative as mubtadaʾ before «إنَّ» entered; or as a badal (substitute) for the position also. Makkī mentioned the latter two, and these two views are according to the school of the Kufans, because they treat all the followers as the conjunction of «ʿaṭf nasaq» in taking the position into account. «[Translator's note: the source text appears truncated or garbled here]» in the position of genitive as a badal from the hāʾ and mīm in «عليهم». It was also said: accusative in position, as an naʿt of «أولياء», or as a badal for them according to the form, or by an implied suitable verb, namely «أمدحُ» ("I praise"). Thus nine views are obtained: nominative from five, genitive from one, and accusative from three. And if you do not make the clause of His saying «لهم البشرى» the khabar of «الذين», it may be resumptive, or it may be a second khabar of «إنَّ», or a third.

semin-durr:64-64.t: His saying, the Exalted: {فِي الحياة الدنيا}: two views are possible for it, the more apparent being that it is attached to «البشرى», that is: the glad tidings occur in this world, and they were explained as the righteous dream. The second: that it is a ḥāl from «البشرى», and so it is attached to an omitted element, the governing element in the ḥāl being the abiding in «لهم» because it occurs as a khabar. His saying «لا تبديلَ» is a resumptive clause. His saying «ذلك» points to «البشرى» although it is feminine, because it is in the sense of «التبشير» (giving glad tidings). It was also said that it points to the bliss; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ذلك» points to their being given glad tidings in both abodes."

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ العزة}: the common readers read «إنَّ» with kasra, as a resumption, which suggests causation. It was also said that it is the answer to an implied question, as if someone had said: why does their saying not grieve him, when it is a thing that would grieve? And it was answered with His saying: {إِنَّ العزة للَّهِ جَمِيعاً}, none of it belongs to them, so why should you care about them and their saying?

The stop at His saying {قَوْلُهُمْ} should be relied upon and intended, and then one begins with His saying «إن العزَّة», although it is impossible for anyone to imagine that this is part of what they said, except someone whose understanding is not taken into account.

Abū Ḥaywa read «أنَّ العزة» with fatḥa on «أنَّ». There are two analyses of it. One: that it is on the omission of the lām of cause, that is: "let their saying not grieve you, because all might belongs to Allah." The second: that «أنَّ» and what is in its scope is a badal from «قولهم», as if it were said: "and let it not grieve you that might belongs to Allah." But how can this analysis be apparent, or how can it be permissible to hold it, and how could the Messenger of Allah ﷺ be forbidden this in meaning when he did not engage in any of those causes? Moreover, what kind of badal is this? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Whoever made it a badal from «قولهم» and then denied it, the thing to be denied is his analysis, not the reading that he denied." He means that his denial of the reading is itself objectionable, because its meaning is sound, as I mentioned to you in the causal explanation, and what is objectionable is only this analysis.

A group denied this reading and ascribed it to error, and worse. Al-Qāḍī said: "Its fatḥa is anomalous, approaching disbelief, and when it is read with kasra it is a resumption; and this indicates the merit of the science of i'rab." Ibn Qutayba said: "Fatḥa on «إنَّ» is not permissible in this place; it is disbelief and exaggeration." Abū Ḥayyān said: "They said that only on the basis that «أنَّ» is governed by «قولهم»." I say: how could it be governed by «قولهم», when kasra is obligatory after saying if it is a quotation by it? How could that be imagined? And just as this meaning is not imagined with its kasra, it is also not imagined with its fatḥa, so long as there is a sound analysis for it.

«جميعاً» is a ḥāl from «العِزَّة», and it may be an emphasis; it is not feminised with tāʾ because the pattern «فعيل» is the same for masculine and feminine, owing to its resemblance to maṣdars; its exposition has already preceded in His saying: {إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ الله قَرِيبٌ} [al-Aʿrāf: 56].

And His saying: {قَوْلُهُمْ}: it was said that its adjective was omitted because the meaning is understood, the implied form being: "let not their saying, which indicates their denial of you, grieve you"; omitting the adjective while retaining the qualified noun is rare, in contrast to the reverse. It was also said: rather it is general, with the particular intended.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {مَن فِي السماوات وَمَنْ فِي الأرض}: it is possible that [by it] rational beings specifically are intended, and it would be of the chapter of alerting through the higher to the lower: for if He, the Exalted, owns the noblest of creatures, namely the two weighty groups (al-thaqalān), the rational beings among angels, humans and jinn, then He owns what is other than them all the more so and with greater right. It is also possible that generality is intended, with the rational given precedence over the non-rational.

His saying: {وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ}: «ما» here may be negative, which is the apparent view. «شركاء» is the object of «يَتَّبع», and the object of «يَدْعون» is omitted because the meaning is understood, the implied form being: "and those who call upon gods other than Allah do not follow partners"; so «آلهةً» is the object of «يَدْعون» and «شركاءَ» the object of «يتبع». This is al-Zamakhsharī's view. He said: "The meaning of «وما يَتَّبعون شركاءَ» is: they do not follow the reality of partners, even though they call them partners, because a partnership with Allah in lordship is impossible; «إن يتبعونَ إلا ظنَّهم» ('they follow only their conjecture') that they are partners." Then he said: "«ما» may be interrogative, meaning: what thing do they follow? and «شركاء» on this is accusative by «يدعون», while on the first view by «يَتَّبع»; and its due form would be «وما يتبع الذين يَدْعُون من دون الله شركاءَ شركاءَ», but one was sufficient because of the indication."

What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned has been rejected by Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Abū l-Baqāʾ. As for Makkī, he said: "«شركاء» is accusative by «يَدْعون», and the object of «يَتَّبع» stands in for it: «إنْ يتبعون إلا الظنَّ», because that is it; and «الشركاء» is not accusative by «يَتَّبع», because you would be negating that of them, while Allah has reported it of them." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«شركاء» is the object of «يَدْعون», and it is not permissible that it be the object of «يتبعون», because the meaning comes to be that they did not follow partners, and that is not the case."

I say: the sense of their words is that the meaning ends up as a denial of their following the partners, whereas in fact they have followed the partners. The answer is what preceded: the meaning is that even if they follow partners, they are not partners in reality, only in their naming them so; so it is as if they had not taken partners or followed them, because the real attribute is stripped from them. The like of it is your saying «ما رأيتُ رجلاً», that is, "one who deserves to be called a man", even if you have seen a male of the children of Adam. It is also possible that «ما» is interrogative, and is then accusative by what follows it; al-Zamakhsharī's saying on that has preceded. Makkī said: "If you made «ما» an interrogative with the meaning of denial and rebuke, it would be a noun in the position of accusative by «يتَّبع»." Abū l-Baqāʾ said something similar.

It is also possible that «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي», conjoined to «مَنْ» in His saying: {ألا إِنَّ للَّهِ مَن فِي السماوات}. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to «مَنْ», as if it were said: and to Allah belongs what those who call upon partners other than Allah follow, that is: and to Him belong your partners."

It is also possible that this relative «ما» is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, with the khabar omitted, its implied form being: "and that which the polytheists follow is falsehood." So these are four views.

Al-Sulamī read «تَدْعُون» in the second person, and al-Zamakhsharī attributed it to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a reading without a sound analysis." I say: Abū l-Qāsim has mentioned its analysis, saying: "Its analysis is that «وما يتَّبع» is taken as an interrogative, that is: what do those whom you call partners, from among the angels and the prophets, follow? meaning that they follow Allah the Exalted and obey Him, so what is wrong with you that you do not do as they do, as in His saying, the Exalted: {أولئك الذين يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إلى رَبِّهِمُ الوسيلة أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Isrāʾ: 57]."

His saying: {إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ}: «إنْ» is negative, and «الظن» is a direct object, so it is a complete exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh); the object of «الظن» is omitted, its implied form being: "they follow only the conjecture that they are partners". According to the Kufans, the «أل» is a substitute for the pronoun, the implied form being: "they follow only their conjecture that they are partners". It is better not to imply an object for «الظن», since the meaning is: "they follow only conjecture, not certainty."

And His saying: {إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ}: whoever reads «يَدْعُون» with yāʾ of the third person has brought «يَتَّبعون» in agreement with it; and whoever reads «تدعون» in the second person, then «يتبعون» is an iltifāt (shift of person), since it is a departure from address to the third person.

semin-durr:67-67.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الليل}: ... the verse. Consider the eloquence of this verse, where from each clause he omitted what is established in the other. For he mentioned the reason for making the night for us, namely His saying «لتسكنوا», and omitted it from the making of the day; and he mentioned the description of the day, namely His saying «مُبْصِراً», and omitted it from the night, because the counterpart indicates it. The implied form is: He is the One who made the night dark for you so that you may rest in it, and the day bright so that you may move about in it for your livelihood. So «مُظْلماً» was omitted because «مبصراً» indicates it, and «لتتحَرَّكوا» was omitted because «لتسكنوا» indicates it; and this is the most eloquent of speech.

And His saying: {مُبْصِراً}: seeing is attributed to the time-word figuratively, as in their saying «نهارُه صائم وليله قائم ونائم». He said:
2605 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ونِمْتِ وما ليلُ المَطِيِّ بنائمِ
(... and you slept, though the night of the riding camels is not sleeping.)
Quṭrub said: "One says «أَظْلَمَ الليلُ»: it became possessed of darkness, and «أضاء النهار»: it became possessed of light, so this would be of the chapter of nisba (relation), like their saying «لابن» and «تامر» ('possessor of milk', 'possessor of dates'), and His saying, the Exalted: {عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 20]; except that that occurs only in the triliteral, and in the pattern «فعَّل» with doubling, according to some, in His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ} [Fuṣṣilat: 46], on one of the views."

semin-durr:68-68.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِنْ عِندَكُمْ مِّن سُلْطَانٍ}: «إنْ» is negative. «عندكم» may be a fronted khabar and «مِنْ سلطان» a delayed mubtadaʾ; or «مِنْ سلطان» may be nominative as agent of the adverbial before it, because it relies on the negation. «مِنْ» is redundant on both analyses. On this, it is possible that it is attached to «سلطان», since that means proof and demonstration, or that it is attached to an omitted element as an adjective of it, so that its position is judged as genitive according to the form and nominative according to the position, because its qualified noun is genitive by a redundant preposition; or that it is attached to the abiding. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The bāʾ should properly be attached to His saying «إنْ عندكم», by making the saying a place for the authority, as in your saying «ما عندكم بأرضِكم مَوْزٌ» ('you have no bananas in your land'), as if it were said: you have no authority in what you say." Al-Ḥawfī said: "«وبهذا» is attached to the meaning of abiding," meaning that to which the adverbial is attached.

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَتَاعٌ فِي الدنيا}: the nominative of «متاع» is possible in two ways. One: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the answer to an implied question, so it is resumptive, as if someone had said: how can they not know, when they are prospering in this world with the kinds of things they enjoy? Then it was said: that is a brief enjoyment. The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "for them is an enjoyment". «في الدنيا» may be attached to «متاع» itself, that is: an enjoying in this world, or it may be attached to an omitted element as an naʿt of «متاع», in which case it is in the position of nominative. The accusative is not read here, in contrast to His saying «متاع الحياة» at the beginning of the sūra.

And His saying: {بِمَا كَانُواْ}: the bāʾ is causal, and «ما» is a maṣdar particle, that is: because of their being disbelievers.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ قَالَ}: «إذ» may be governed by «نَبأ», and it may be a badal of «نبأ», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that it be a ḥāl from «نبأ», but that is not apparent. It cannot be accusative by «اتلُ», because that is invalid, as «اتلُ» is future and «إذ» is past. As for «لقومه», the lām is either for conveying, which is the apparent view, or for cause, which is not apparent.

His saying: {كَبُرَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَّقَامِي} is of the chapter of figurative predication, as in their saying «ثَقُل عليَّ ظلُّه» ("his shadow weighed upon me").

Abū Rajāʾ, Abū Mijlaz and Abū l-Jawzāʾ read «مُقامي» with ḍamma on the mīm. «المَقام» with fatḥa is the place of standing; with ḍamma it is the place of residing, or the residing itself. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is not read here with ḍamma on the mīm," as if he had not come across the reading of these fathers.

His saying: {فَعَلَى الله} is the apodosis of the condition.

And His saying: {فأجمعوا} is conjoined to the apodosis, and Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned nothing else. It was found problematic that he relies on Allah always, whether his standing is burdensome to them or not. It was also said that the apodosis of the condition is His saying «فأجمعوا», and His saying {فَعَلَى الله تَوَكَّلْتُ} is a parenthetical clause between the condition and its apodosis, like the saying of the poet:
2606 - إمَّا تَرَيْني قد نَحَلْتُ ومَنْ يكنْ ... غَرَضاً لأطراف الأَسِنَّة يَنْحَلِ
فلرُبَّ أبْلَجَ مثلِ ثِقْلِكِ بادِنٍ ... ضخمٍ على ظهر الجَوادِ مُهَبَّلِ
(If you see that I have grown thin, and whoever becomes a target for the spear-points grows thin, then many a bright-faced man, stout and massive like your heavy weight, has sat on the back of the steed, sluggish.) It was also said: the apodosis is omitted, that is: "so do what you will".

The common readers read «فَأَجْمعوا» as an imperative of «أَجْمع» with hamzat al-qaṭʿ. One says «أَجْمع» for abstract matters and «جَمَع» for concrete things; so one says «أجمعت أمري» and «جمعت الجيش»; this is the more frequent usage. Al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza said:
2607 - أَجْمَعُوا أمرهم بليلٍ فلمَّا ... أصبحوا أصبحت لهم ضَوْضَاءُ
(They settled their affair by night, and when morning came, there was an uproar from them.)
And another said:
2608 - يا ليت شعري والمُنَى لا تَنْفَعُ ... هل أَغْدُوَنْ يوماً وأَمْري مُجْمَعُ
(Would that I knew, though wishes do not profit: shall I one day set out with my affair settled?)
Is «أجمع» transitive by itself, or by a preposition that was then omitted for latitude? Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is from your saying «أجمعتُ على الأمر» when you have resolved on it, except that the preposition was omitted so the verb reached it directly." It was also said: it is transitive by itself in origin, and he cited al-Ḥārith's verse. Abū Fayd al-Sadūsī said: "«أجمعت الأمر» is more eloquent than «أجمعت عليه»." Abū l-Haytham said: "«أجمعَ أمرَه» means he made it gathered after it had been scattered," and he said: "its scatteredness is that he says at one time 'do such', and at another 'do such'; when he resolves on one matter, he has gathered it, that is, made it a whole. This is the original sense of ijmāʿ; then it came to mean resolve, until it was connected with «على», and so one said «أَجْمَعْتُ على الأمر», that is, 'I resolved on it', while the original is «أجمعت الأمر»."

The common readers read «وشركاءَكم» in the accusative, and there are several views on it. First: that it is conjoined to «أَمْرَكم» with an implied omitted muḍāf, that is: "and the affair of your partners", like {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82]; and what I stated earlier indicates this, that «أَجْمع» is for abstract matters. Second: that it is conjoined to it without implying an omitted muḍāf; it was said: because one also says «أجمعت شركائي». Third: that it is accusative by an implied suitable verb, that is: "and gather your partners", with connecting hamza. It was also said that its implied form is «وادعوا» ("and call"), and so it is in Ubayy's codex, «وادعوا»; so he implied a suitable verb, as in His saying, the Exalted: {والذين تَبَوَّءُوا الدار والإيمان} [al-Ḥashr: 9], that is: "and held faith"; and like it is the saying of another:
2609 - فَعَلَفْتُها تِبْناً وماءً بارداً ... حتى شَتَتْ هَمَّالةً عيناها
(I fed her straw and cold water, until she spent the winter with streaming eyes.)
and as in his saying:
2610 - يا ليت زوجَك قد غدا ... مُتَقَلِّداً سَيْفاً ورُمْحاً
(Would that your husband had set out girded with a sword and a spear.)
and the saying of another:
2611 - إذا ما الغانياتُ بَرَزْنَ يوماً ... وزَجَّجْنَ الحواجبَ والعيونا
(When the fair ladies appear one day, having lengthened the eyebrows and the eyes.)
He means: "and carrying a spear", and "and having kohled the eyes". It has already been mentioned that in these places there is an analysis other than this. Fourth: that it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), that is, "together with your partners". Al-Fārisī said: "The partners may be accusative with the wāw of accompaniment, as they said «جاء البردُ والطَّيالسةَ»." Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing other than Abū ʿAlī's saying. Abū Ḥayyān said: "This analysis should be as a mafʿūl maʿahu from the agent, which is the pronoun in «فَأَجْمعوا», not from the object, which is «أَمْرَكُمْ», and that is according to the better-known of the two usages, because one says «أجمع الشركاءُ أمرَهم», and one does not say «جَمَع الشركاء أمرهم» except rarely." I say: he means that if we make it a mafʿūl maʿahu from the agent, it is permissible without disagreement, because some grammarians stipulate for the validity of accusative as mafʿūl maʿahu that it be suitable to be conjoined to what precedes; if its conjunction is not suitable, its accusative as mafʿūl maʿahu is not valid. So if we made it from the object, it would not be permissible according to the well-known view, since it cannot be conjoined to what precedes it, as one does not say «أجمعت شركائي», but rather «جَمَعْت».

Al-Zuhrī, al-Aʿmash, al-Aʿraj, al-Jaḥdarī, Abū Rajāʾ, Yaʿqūb and al-Aṣmaʿī from Nāfiʿ read «فأجْمَعُوا» with connecting alif and fatḥa on the mīm, from «جَمَع يَجْمَع»; and on this reading «شركاءَكم» is clearly accusative as a conjoined element to what precedes, and the views mentioned in the first reading are also possible for it. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "«أَجْمَعْتُ الأمر» means: I made it whole, while «جَمَعْتُ الأموال جمعاً»; so ijmāʿ is for events and jamʿ for concrete things, although each may be used in place of the other; and in the Revelation: {فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ} [Ṭāhā: 60]." I say: the readers differed over His saying, the Exalted: {فَأَجْمِعُواْ كَيْدَكُمْ} [Ṭāhā: 64]; the six read it with hamzat al-qaṭʿ, making it from «أجمع», which agrees with what was said, that «أجمع» is for abstract matters. Abū ʿAmr alone read «فاجمعوا» with connecting alif; and they all agreed on His saying «فَجَمع كيدَه ثم أتى», for it is from the triliteral, although it operates on an abstract thing and not a concrete one. Some of them gave the triliteral a meaning other than the quadriliteral's, and said of Abū ʿAmr's reading that it is from «جَمَع يَجْمع», the opposite of «فرَّق يُفَرِّق», and made the reading of the rest from «أجمع أمرَه» when he made it firm and resolved on it, and from it is the saying of the poet:
2612 - يا ليت شعري والمنى لا تَنْفَعُ ... هل أَغْدُوَنْ يوماً وأَمْري مُجْمَعُ
(Would that I knew, though wishes do not profit: shall I one day set out with my affair settled?)
It was also said that the meaning is: "so agree on your plot", with the preposition omitted.

Al-Ḥasan, al-Sulamī, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Sallām and Yaʿqūb read «وشركاؤكم» in the nominative. There are two analyses of it. One: that it is conjoined to the nominative pronoun of «أَجْمِعُوا» before it, and this was permissible because the separation by the object made the conjunction allowable. The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "and your partners, let them settle their affair".

A group read anomalously «وشركائكم» in the genitive, and it was analysed as the omission of the muḍāf and the retention of the muḍāf ilayhi genitive as it was, as in the saying:
2613 - أكلَّ امرِىءٍ تحسبين أمرَأً ... ونارٍ تَوَقَّدُ بالليل نارا
(Do you count every man a man, and every fire that is kindled at night a fire?)
that is: "and every fire"; so the implied form of the verse is «وأمر شركائكم», the word «أمر» being omitted while what follows it is retained as it was. Whoever follows the Kufans' view allows conjoining it to the pronoun in «أمركم» without interpretation, and the views on this, I mean conjoining to a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition, have already been given in Sūrat al-Baqara.

His saying: {غُمَّةً}: one says «غَمٌّ» and «غُمَّة», like «كَرْبٌ» and «كُرْبَةٌ». Abū l-Haytham said: "It is from their saying «غَمَّ علينا الهلالُ» ('the new moon was obscured from us'), and it is «مغموم» when it is sought but not seen." Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd said:
2614 - لعَمْرك ما أمري عليَّ بغُمَّةٍ ... نهاري ولا ليلي عليَّ بسَرْمَدِ
(By your life, my affair is not obscure to me by day, nor is my night endless for me.)
Al-Layth said: "One says «هو في غُمَّة مِنْ أمره» when it is not clear to him."

His saying: {ثُمَّ اقضوا}: the object of «اقضوا» is omitted, that is: "carry out to me that affair which you intend to inflict", as in His saying: {وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ الأمر} [al-Ḥijr: 66], where He made it transitive to an explicit object. Al-Sarī read «ثم أفْضُوا» with hamzat al-qaṭʿ and fāʾ, from «أفضى يُفضي» when something reaches an end; one says «أَفْضَيْتُ إليك». The Exalted said: {وَقَدْ أفضى بَعْضُكُمْ إلى بَعْضٍ} [al-Nisāʾ: 21]. So the meaning is: "then proceed to your secret", that is, bring it to me. It was also said that its meaning is: "hasten with it to me". It was also said that it is from «أفضى», that is, he went out into the open space, that is: "bring it out to the open against me, and show it to me", as in the saying:
2615 - أبى الضيمَ والنعمانُ يَحْرِقُ نابَه ... عليه فأفضى والسيوفُ مَعاقِلُهْ
(He refused injustice while al-Nuʿmān gnashed his tooth at him, so he went out into the open, with swords as his strongholds.)
The lām of «الفضاء» is a wāw, because it is from «فَضَا يَفْضُو», that is, to be wide. And His saying «لا تُنْظِرون» means "you do not delay", from «النَّظِرة», which is delay.

semin-durr:73-73.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {فِي الفلك}: two views are possible for it. One: that it is attached to «أَنْجَيْناه», that is: the saving took place in this place. The second: that it is attached to the abiding to which the adverbial «معه» is attached, because it occurs as a ṣila (relative clause), that is: "and those who abode with him in the ship".

And His saying: {وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ}, that is, "We made them"; the pronoun in «جَعَلْناهم» is plural, following the meaning of «مَنْ»; and «خلائف» is the plural of «خَلِيفة», that is, they succeed those who were drowned.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن بَعْدِهِ}: that is, after Nūḥ (Noah). «بالبينات» is attached to «جاؤُوهم», or to an omitted element as a ḥāl, that is: accompanied by the clear proofs. His saying «ليؤمِنوا»: he used the lām of denial for emphasis. The pronoun in «كَذَّبوا» refers to those to whom the pronoun in «كانوا» refers, namely the people of the messengers. The meaning is that their state after the sending of the messengers was like their state before it, in their being people of ignorance (jāhiliyya). Abū l-Baqāʾ and Makkī said: "The pronoun in «كانوا» refers to the people of the messengers, and in «كَذَّبوا» it refers to the people of Nūḥ, and the meaning is: the people of the messengers would not believe in what the people of Nūḥ denied, that is, in the like of it. It is also possible that the hāʾ refers to Nūḥ himself, without omission of a muḍāf, the implied form being: the people of the messengers after Nūḥ would not believe in Nūḥ, since had they believed in him they would have believed in their own prophets. «من قبل» is attached to «كَذَّبوا», that is, before the sending of the messengers. It was also said: all the pronouns refer to the people of the messengers in another sense, which is that they hastened to deny their messengers; whenever a messenger came they persisted in disbelief and continued in it, so they would not believe in what their denial had preceded, from before their persistence in disbelief and their continuance."

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In my view, the wording admits another meaning, which is that «ما» is a maṣdar particle, and the meaning is: they denied their messengers, so their punishment from Allah was that they would not believe because of their denial before, that is, because of its cause and its recompense. «كذلك نطبع» supports this interpretation, and it is a speech that requires reflection." Abū Ḥayyān said: "The apparent view is that «ما» is a relative noun, and for that reason the pronoun refers to it in His saying {بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ بِهِ}; had it been a maṣdar particle, the pronoun would be left without a mentioned referent, and one would have to go to the trouble of finding what the pronoun refers to." I say: the Shaykh built this on the view of the majority of grammarians that the maṣdar «ما» is not a noun, so that a pronoun could refer to it; and I have alerted you more than once that the view of al-Akhfash and Ibn al-Sarrāj is that it is a noun, so the pronoun may refer to it.

The common readers read «نَطْبع» with nūn, indicating the magnification of the speaker. Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Faḍl read it with yāʾ of the third person, referring to Allah the Exalted, and for that reason He stated it explicitly in another place: {كَذَلِكَ يَطْبَعُ الله} [al-Aʿrāf: 101]. The kāf is an naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl from the pronoun of that maṣdar, according to the disagreement you know, that is: "in the manner of that firm sealing, whose removal is impossible, We seal the hearts of those who transgress against Allah's creation."

semin-durr:76-76.t: Mujāhid, Ibn Jubayr and al-Aʿmash read «لساحر» as an active participle; the demonstrative «هذا» then points to Mūsā, who is pointed to because his mention has preceded. In the reading of the group, what is pointed to is the thing that Mūsā brought, of turning the staff into a serpent and bringing out his hand white like the sun. It is also possible, in Ibn Jubayr's reading, that «هذا» points to the matter that Mūsā brought, by way of exaggeration, in that they described meanings with the attributes of concrete things, as in their saying «شعرٌ شاعرٌ» ("poetic poetry") and «جَدَّ جَدُّه» ("his luck was lucky").

semin-durr:77-77.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَتقُولُونَ}: there are two views on what this saying governs. One: that it is mentioned, namely the clause of «أسحرٌ هذا» to its end, as if they said: "Have you come with sorcery, seeking success by it, when sorcerers do not succeed?", like the saying of Mūsā, upon our Prophet and upon him and upon all the prophets the best of prayers and peace, to the sorcerers: {مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السحر إِنَّ الله سَيُبْطِلُهُ}. The second: that its object is omitted, and is indicated by what has preceded, namely «إن هذا لسحرٌ مبين». The object of saying is often omitted because of the indication, as saying itself is often omitted. Like the verse in the omission of what is said is the saying of the poet:
2616 - لَنحن الأُلى قُلْتُمْ فأنَّى مُلِئْتُمُ ... برؤيتنا قبلَ اهتمامٍ بكمْ رُعْبا
(We are the ones of whom you said...; so how were you filled with terror at the sight of us before any concern for you?)
In the book of Sībawayh: «متى رأيت أو قلت زيداً منطلقاً», giving operation to the first and omitting the object of saying; and it is also permissible to give operation to saying in the sense of quotation, so one says «متى رأيت أو قلت زيد منطلق». It was also said that "saying" in the verse has the meaning of faulting and disparaging, and the meaning is: do you fault the truth and disparage it, when it was your duty to honour it and submit to it? as in their saying «فلان يخاف القالة» and «بين الناس تقاوُلٌ», when some say to others what pains them; and like saying is "mention" in His saying: {سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 60]. All of this is summarised from al-Zamakhsharī's words.

semin-durr:78-78.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَجِئْتَنَا لِتَلْفِتَنَا}: the lām is attached to the coming, that is: did you come for this purpose? They denounced his coming for this reason. «اللَّفْتُ» is twisting and turning away; «لَفَتَه عن كذا» means he turned him away and twisted him from it. Al-Azharī said: "«لَفَتَ الشيءَ وفَتَلَه»: he twisted it, and this is of the metathesised words (maqlūb)." I say: metathesis is not claimed for it until one of the two forms comes to be used in preference to the other; for that reason they did not count «جَذَبَ» and «جَبَذَ», or «حَمِدَ» and «مَدَح», as of this kind, because they are equal. The reflexive of «لَفَتَ» is «التَفَتَ». It was also said «انفتل», as if they dispensed with the reflexive of «فَتَل» in place of the reflexive of «لَفَتَ»; and «امرأة لَفُوت» is one who turns to her child away from her husband when the child is from another; and «اللَّفِيْتَةُ» is what is thick of porridge.

His saying: {وَتَكُونَ لَكُمَا الكبريآء}: «الكِبْرياء» is the noun of «كان», and «لكم» is the khabar. As for «في الأرض», Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed five views for it: first, that it is attached to «الكبرياء» itself; second, that it is attached to «تكون» itself; third, that it is attached to the abiding in «لكم», because it occurs as a khabar; fourth, that it is a ḥāl from «الكبرياء»; fifth, that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لكما», because it carries it.

«الكِبْرياء» is a maṣdar on the pattern «فِعْلِياء», and its meaning is grandeur. ʿAdī ibn al-Riqāʿ said:
2617 - سُؤْدُدٌ غيرُ فاحِشٍ لا يُدا ... نِيه تَجْبارَةٌ ولا كِبْرِيا
(A lordship not excessive, which neither tyranny nor arrogance approaches.)
And Ibn al-Ruqayyāt said:
2618 - مُلْكُه مُلْكُ رأفةٍ ليس فيه ... جَبَروتٌ منهُ ولا كِبْرِياءُ
(His kingship is a kingship of compassion, with no tyranny in it and no arrogance.)
He means: it is not what kings are on of tyranny and haughtiness.

The majority read «تكون» in the feminine, following the feminine form of the word. Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan, Ismāʿīl, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read «ويكون» with the yāʾ of two dots below, because the feminine is figurative.

semin-durr:79-79.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {بِكُلِّ سَاحِرٍ}: the two brothers [Translator's note: i.e. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «سَحَّار», and this is also the reading of Ibn Muṣarrif, Ibn Waththāb and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السحر}: Abū ʿAmr alone, of the seven, read «آلسحرُ» with the hamza of interrogation followed by a pure alif, which is a substitute for the connecting hamza that enters upon the lām of definiteness; it may also be made intermediate (bayna bayna). The verification of these two views has already preceded in His saying: {ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ} [al-Anʿām: 143]. This is the reading of Mujāhid and his companions and of Abū Jaʿfar. The rest of the seven read with a connecting hamza that drops in running speech. As for Abū ʿAmr's reading, it has several views. First: that «ما» is interrogative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and «جِئْتُمْ به» is the khabar, the implied form being: "What thing have you brought?", as if it were an interrogative of denial and belittlement of the thing brought. «السحر» is a badal of the interrogative noun, and for that reason its particle is repeated with it, for what I have established in the books of grammar. Second: that «السحر» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "is it sorcery?" Third: that it is a mubtadaʾ with khabar omitted, its implied form being: "the sorcery is it". Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned these two views, and Makkī mentioned the second; both are remote. Fourth: that «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي», with «جئتم به» as its ṣila, and the relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and «السحر» in its two aspects, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ or as a mubtadaʾ with omitted khabar, the implied form being: "that which you have brought, is it sorcery?" or "that which you have brought, the sorcery is it"; and this pronoun is the link, as in your saying «الذي جاءك أزيدٌ هو». Abū Ḥayyān said this.

I say: Makkī prohibited «ما» from being a relative noun in Abū ʿAmr's reading, saying: "Abū ʿAmr read «آلسحرُ» with the lengthening, and on this reading «ما» is an interrogative mubtadaʾ, «جئتم به» the khabar, and «السحر» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, «أهو السحر». It is not permissible that «ما» mean «الذي» on this reading, as it would then have no khabar." I say: it is not as he said; rather its khabar is the clause one of whose two parts is implied. Likewise al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted it to be a relative noun only in the reading of those other than Abū ʿAmr, but neither of them addressed why it is not permissible.

Fifth: that «ما» is interrogative in the position of accusative by an implied verb after it, because it has the front of the speech, and «جئتم به» explains that implied verb, so the question is then of the chapter of ishtighāl; the implied form being: "what thing did you bring, you brought it?", and «السحر» as before. Had «السحر» been read in the accusative as a badal of «ما» on this implied form, it would have had a valid analysis, but it was not read so, as far as I know. What Makkī related from al-Farrāʾ regarding the permissibility of its accusative, on a different ground, will come, as being a reading transmitted [from al-Farrāʾ].

As for the reading of the rest, it also has several views. First: that «ما» means «الذي», in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, with «جئتم به» as ṣila and its returning pronoun, and «السحرُ» as its khabar; the implied form being: "that which you have brought is sorcery". This implied form is supported by Ubayy's reading, as in his codex: {ما أتيتم به سحرٌ}, and by the reading of ʿAbdallāh and al-Aʿmash: {مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السحر}.

Second: that «ما» is interrogative in the position of accusative by an implied verb, as established, and «السحر» the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ or a mubtadaʾ with implied khabar. Third: that «ما» is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and «السحر» as before, being a mubtadaʾ or a khabar, the clause being the khabar of the interrogative «ما». Abū Ḥayyān said, after mentioning the first view: "In my view, it is possible that in this view it is interrogative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, or in the position of accusative by ishtighāl, and it is an interrogative of belittlement and diminishing of what they brought, and «السحر» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: it is sorcery."

I say: the apparent sense of his expression is that no one else saw this, since he said "in my view", whereas Abū l-Baqāʾ and Makkī allowed it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said, after mentioning the reading of those other than Abū ʿAmr: "It is read in the form of a statement, and has two views", and then said: "It is possible that «ما» is interrogative and «السحر» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ." And Makkī said of the reading of those other than Abū ʿAmr, after mentioning that «ما» means «الذي»: "It is possible that «ما» is nominative as mubtadaʾ and is interrogative, «جئتم به» the khabar, and «السحر» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, «هو السحر»; and it is possible that «ما» is in the position of accusative by an implied verb after «ما», its implied form being: what thing have you brought [it], and «السحرُ» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ."

Fourth: that this reading is like Abū ʿAmr's in meaning, that is, it is on the intention of interrogation but its particle is omitted because it is known. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is read in the form of a statement, and has two views. One: that it is interrogative in meaning also, and the hamza is omitted because it is known." On what he mentioned, the i'rab would be as previously given. Know that if you make «ما» a relative noun meaning «الذي», its accusative by an implied verb in ishtighāl is impossible. Makkī said: "It is not permissible that «ما» meaning «الذي» be in the position of accusative, because what follows it is its ṣila, and the ṣila does not operate on the relative noun, nor does it serve as an explanation of the governing element on the relative noun." This is a sound statement. The summary of this is that if it is interrogative, it may be in the position of nominative or accusative, and if it is a relative noun, its position must be nominative as mubtadaʾ.

Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ allowed the accusative of «السحر», making «ما» conditional, and putting «السحرَ» in the accusative as a maṣdar, implying the fāʾ with «إن الله سيُبْطِله», and making the alif and lām in «السحر» redundant; all of that is remote. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān has allowed the omission of the fāʾ from the apodosis of the condition in prose, and cited as evidence for its permissibility His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَآ أَصَابَكُمْ مِّن مُّصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ} [al-Shūrā: 30]; but no one else permitted it except in poetic necessity." I say: if we go along with al-Farrāʾ, «ما» is conditional, meant as a maṣdar, the implied form being: "whatever sorcery you bring, Allah will nullify it", and what shows that «ما» is meant as sorcery is his saying «السحر»; but his saying "if «السحر» is put in the accusative as a maṣdar" is uneasy, so its interpretation is that it is accusative as a maṣdar standing in the place of the ḥāl, and for that reason he implied it as indefinite and made «أل» redundant in it.

It has been transmitted from al-Farrāʾ that this alif and lām is for definiteness, a definiteness of previous mention (taʿrīf al-ʿahd). Al-Farrāʾ said: "He said «السحر» with alif and lām only because an indefinite, when repeated, is repeated with alif and lām", meaning that the indefinite had preceded in His saying: {إِنَّ هذا لَسِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ}; Ibn ʿAṭiyya explained it likewise.
