Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The definiteness here in «السحر» is more fitting because it has preceded as indefinite in their saying «إنَّ هذا لسِحْر», so it comes here with the lām of previous mention, as one says at the beginning of a letter «سلامٌ عليك»." Abū Ḥayyān said: "What they mentioned about «السحر» here is not a case of an indefinite preceding and then being reported about, because the condition of that is that what is made definite with «أل» is the preceding indefinite itself and nothing else, as in His saying, the Exalted: {كَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَآ إلى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولاً فعصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرسول} [al-Muzzammil: 15-16], and you say «زارني رجلٌ فأكرمت الرجل»; since it is the same, it may be replaced by its pronoun, and you say «فأكرمتُه». But the sorcery here is not the sorcery in their saying «إنَّ هذا لسحر», because what they reported to be sorcery is what appeared at Mūsā's hands of the miracle of the staff, whereas the sorcery in Mūsā's saying is their own sorcery that they brought; so the two referents differ, since they said it of Mūsā's miracle, and Mūsā said it of what they had brought. For that reason it is not permissible to bring the pronoun here in place of «السحر», so that it would refer back to their saying «لسِحْر»."

I say: the answer is that al-Farrāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya meant only the sorcery previously mentioned in the wording, even if the second is not the same as the first in meaning; but since the word «السحر» was applied to both, that may be said. This is indicated by their saying about His saying, the Exalted: {والسلام عَلَيَّ} [Maryam: 33] that the alif and lām is for previous mention because of the mention of peace in His saying, the Exalted: {وَسَلاَمٌ عَلَيْهِ} [Maryam: 15], even though the peace upon ʿĪsā is other than the peace upon Yaḥyā, since each peace is specific to its owner in respect of its being specific to him. And this transmission mentioned from al-Farrāʾ concerning the alif and lām contradicts what Makkī related from him concerning them, unless it is said: he may have had two views, which is not remote, for as knowledge increases, views multiply.

And His saying: {المفسدين} is an instance of the overt noun placed in the position of the second-person pronoun, since the original would be: "He will not set right your work"; so He brought them out in this blameworthy description as a testimony against them for it.

semin-durr:82-82.t: It was also read «بكلمته» in the singular, and its counterpart has already preceded.

semin-durr:83-83.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَمَآ آمَنَ}: the fāʾ is for immediate succession, and it suggests that their belief was not delayed after the casting but took place right after it, because the fāʾ indicates that. The explanation of making «آمن» transitive with the lām has already preceded. As for the pronoun in «قومه», there are two views on it. One, the apparent, is that it refers to Mūsā, because he is the one being spoken about and because he is the nearest one mentioned; had it referred to Pharaoh, He would not have repeated his name overtly, but the construction would have been «على خوفٍ منه». Ibn ʿAbbās and others took this view.

The second: that it refers to Pharaoh, which is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya preferred this and weakened the first, saying: "Among the things that weaken the pronoun's referring to Mūsā is that what is known from the reports of the Children of Israel is that prophecies were widespread among them, and extreme humiliation had befallen them, and they hoped for its removal by the appearance of a newborn; so when Mūsā came to them they rallied to him and followed him, and it is not recorded that any group of the Children of Israel disbelieved in Mūsā. So how does this verse give that the lesser part of them was the one who believed? So the preferred view is that it refers to Pharaoh, and what preceded of Mūsā's dialogue and his rebuttal of them and rebuke of them also supports it."

His saying: {على خَوْفٍ}: a ḥāl, that is: they believed while in fear. As for the pronoun in «وملئهم», there are several views on it. First: that it refers to «الذرِّيَّة» (the offspring); this is the saying of Abū l-Ḥasan and the choice of Ibn Jarīr, that is: fear of the notables of the offspring, who are the nobles of the Children of Israel.

Second: that it refers to «قومه» in both of its aspects, that is, whether we make the pronoun in «قومه» refer to Mūsā or to Pharaoh, that is: "and the nobles of the people of Mūsā" or "the nobles of the people of Pharaoh".

Third: that it refers to Pharaoh, and it was objected to this: how can a plural pronoun refer to a singular? Abū l-Baqāʾ excused that in two ways. One: that since Pharaoh was great in their eyes, the pronoun referred back to him in the plural, as the great one says "we command"; and this requires consideration, because had that occurred in their speech as quoted from them, it could be accepted. The second: that Pharaoh became a name for his followers, as Thamūd is a name for the whole tribe. Makkī stated two other views close to these two, but purer than them. He said: "The pronoun in «مَلَئهم» is plural only because it is a report about a tyrant, and a tyrant is reported about with the plural form; and it was said: when Pharaoh was mentioned it was known that others were with him, so the pronoun returned to him and those with him." I say: something like this has preceded at His saying: {الذين قَالَ لَهُمُ الناس إِنَّ الناس} [Āl ʿImrān: 173], where the speaker meant is Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd, because he was not without someone who aided him in that saying.

Fourth: that it refers to an omitted muḍāf, namely «آل» (the family), the implied form being: "in fear of the family of Pharaoh and their nobles"; al-Farrāʾ said this, as it was omitted in His saying {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82].

Abū l-Baqāʾ said, after relating this without attributing it to anyone: "This is, in our view, a mistake, because a pronoun does not refer to what is omitted, for if that were permissible it would be permissible to say «زيد قاموا» meaning «غلمان زيد قاموا»." I say: his saying "because a pronoun does not refer to what is omitted" is not conceded; rather, when a muḍāf is omitted the Arabs have two practices: attending to it and not attending to it, the latter being the more frequent. This is indicated by the fact that He combined the two in His saying {وَكَم مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا} [al-Aʿrāf: 4], that is, "the people of a town", and then said «أو هم قائلون». I have verified that in its place referred to. And his saying "it would be permissible to say «زيد قاموا»" is not parallel, for that involves omission without an indication, in contrast to the verse.

Abū Ḥayyān said, after relating al-Farrāʾ's words: "It was rejected on the ground that fear is possible from Pharaoh, whereas asking the town is not possible, so nothing is omitted except what an indication shows; but it may be said that the plural of the pronoun in «ومَلَئهم» indicates this omitted element." I say: he means that they rejected al-Farrāʾ by distinguishing between {وَسْئَلِ القرية} and this verse, in that asking the town is impossible so we are compelled to imply the muḍāf, whereas in the verse fear can be directed at Pharaoh, so there is no compulsion indicating to us an omitted muḍāf. The answer to this is that omission may be on the basis of a rational or a verbal indication; moreover, it was said of «واسأل القرية» that it is literal, since it is possible for the Prophet to ask the town and for it to answer him.

Fifth: that there is an omitted conjoined element here, omitted because of the indication, the indication being that a king is not alone but has retinue, armies and troops; so the implied form is: "in fear of Pharaoh and his people and their nobles", that is, the nobles of Pharaoh and his people. This is also transmitted from al-Farrāʾ. I say: omission of the conjoined element is rare in their speech; among it according to some is His saying {تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81], that is, "and the cold"; and the saying of another:
2619 - كأن الحصى مِنْ خلفها وأمامِها ... إذا حَذَفَتْه رِجْلُها حَذْفُ أَعْسَرا
(As if the pebbles behind her and in front of her, when her foot flings them, are flung by a left-handed man.)
that is, "and her hand".

His saying: {أَن يَفْتِنَهُمْ}: there are three views on it. First: that it is in the position of genitive as a badal from «فرعون», a badal of inclusion, the implied form being: "in fear of Pharaoh, his tempting them", like your saying «أعجبني زيد علْمُه». Second: that it is in the position of accusative as a direct object of the maṣdar, that is: fear of his tempting them; and the operation of an indefinite-nunated maṣdar is frequent, as in His saying: {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً} [al-Balad: 14-15], and the saying of another:
2620 - فلولا رجاءُ النصرِ منك ورَهْبَةٌ ... عقابَك قد كانوا لنا بالمَوارد
(Were it not for the hope of victory from you and fear of your punishment, they would have been at the watering places against us.)
Third: that it is accusative as an object of purpose after the omission of the lām, and the well-known disagreement applies to it.

Al-Ḥasan and Nubayḥ read «يُفْتِنَهم» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, and that has already preceded.

And «في الأرض» is attached to «عالٍ», that is: overpowering in it, or unjust, as in the saying:
2621 - فاعمِدْ لِما تَعْلُوا فمالك بالذي ... لا تَسْتطيع من الأمور يَدانِ
(Aim for what you can overpower, for you have no power over what you cannot manage of affairs.)
that is, "what you overpower". It is also possible that «في الأرض» is attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «عالٍ», in which case its position is nominative; and the first view is made preferable by His saying: {وَإِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ لَعَالٍ فِي الأرض}.

semin-durr:84-84.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِن كُنتُمْ آمَنتُمْ بالله فَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلوا}: this is the apodosis of the first condition, and the second condition, {إن كنتم مسلمين}, is a condition within the first; this is because whenever two conditions are not ordered in existence, the second condition is a condition of the first, and for that reason it must precede the first. The verification of that has already preceded.

semin-durr:87-87.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن تَبَوَّءَا}: «أَنْ» may be the explicative (mufassira), because what has the sense of saying has preceded it, namely the revelation (īḥāʾ); and it may be the maṣdar particle, in which case it is in the position of accusative as the direct object of «أوحينا», that is: "We revealed to the two of them the taking up of dwellings."

The majority have the hamza in «تبوَّآ». Ḥafṣ read «تَبَوَّيا» with a pure yāʾ, a substitute for the hamza, which is a non-analogical lightening, since the analogical lightening of such a hamza is for it to be between the hamza and the alif. A group of readers have denied this transmission from Ḥafṣ, and some restricted it to the case of pausing, which is the only one that Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī and al-Shāṭibī reported; and some say without restriction that it is replaced by yāʾ in his reading both in connection and in pause. In sum, it is a weak reading in Arabic and in transmission, and I have left the texts of the reading scholars out of fear of tedium, and as I have no need of them given what I set down in «Sharḥ al-Qaṣīd».

«التبوُّءُ» is settling and returning, and the verification of the root has already preceded in His saying {تُبَوِّىءُ المؤمنين} [Āl ʿImrān: 121].

His saying: {لِقَوْمِكُمَا}: the lām may be redundant in the first object, with «بيوتاً» the second object, in the sense of «بَوِّآ قومكما بيوتاً», that is, settle them; and «فَعَّل» and «تفعَّل» may have the same meaning, like «عَلَّقَها» and «تَعَلَّقها»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. There is weakness in it in that the lām is added while the governing element is not derivative and the object has not been fronted. The second: that it is not redundant, and then there are two views: one, that it is a ḥāl from «البيوت»; the other, that it and what follows it is the object of «تَبَوَّآ».

His saying: {بِمِصْرَ}: Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed several views on it. First: that it is attached to «تَبَوَّآ», which is the apparent view. Second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of «تبوَّآ», which he considered weak and did not explain the reason for its weakness because it is obvious. Third: that it is a ḥāl from «البيوت». Fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «لِقومكما». He made the pronoun dual in «تبوَّآ», plural in His saying «واجعلوا» and «أقيموا», and singular in His saying «وبشِّر»; because the first is a command to the two of them, the second to the two of them and their people, and the third to Mūsā alone, since his brother is a follower of him; and as the act of giving glad tidings is noble, He specified Mūsā for it, because he is the principal.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
The discussion of the disjointed letters has already preceded at the beginning of this work, as has the difference of the readers over inclining (imāla) these letters when an alif is at their end, namely: رَا، طَا، هَا، يَا، حَا. The Kufans, except Ḥafṣ, and Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir inclined «را» fully in all its sūras. The two Brothers and Abū Bakr inclined «طا» in all its sūras, as in «طس»، «طسم»، «طه», and «يا» in «يس». Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Sūsī agreed with them on «يا» in «كهيعص», with a difference reported from al-Sūsī. The two Brothers, Abū ʿAmr, Warsh and Abū Bakr inclined «ها» in «طه»; likewise Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr inclined it in «كهيعص», but not Ḥamza and Warsh. Abū ʿAmr, Warsh, the two Brothers, Abū Bakr and Ibn Dhakwān inclined «حا» in all its seven sūras, except that Abū ʿAmr and Warsh incline it in between (bayna bayna). [The readers have much work in this], which I explained in «Sharḥ al-Qaṣīd».
«الحكيم»: it may be in the sense of fāʿil, that is, the judge/ruler, and may be in the sense of mafʿūl, that is, "made firm" (muḥkam). al-Aʿshā said:
2558 - وغريبةٍ تأتي الملوكَ حكيمةً ... قد قلتُها لِيُقالَ مَنْ ذا قالها
(And a rare piece that comes to kings, wise and firm; I composed it so that it would be asked: who said it?)

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَآ}: the hamza is of denial, and «أن أوحينا» is its subject (ism), and «عجباً» its khabar. «للناس» is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «عَجَباً», because in origin it is an adjective of it; or it is attached to «عَجَباً», and its being a maṣdar does no harm because latitude is allowed in the ẓarf and its equivalent that is not allowed in other things. It was also said: because «عجباً» is a maṣdar standing in the place of the active or passive participle, and whenever it is so, fronting its governed term is permissible. It was also said: it is attached to the defective «كان», and this is according to whoever allows that in it; and this depends on the disagreement over whether the defective «كان» indicates an event: if we say that it does, it is permissible; otherwise not. It was also said: it is attached to an omitted element by way of clarification (tabyīn), and the estimate in the verse is: "Was our revelation to a man from among them a wonder for them?" «منهم» is an adjective of «رجل».
Ruʾba read «رَجْل» with a sukūn on the jīm, which is the dialect of Tamīm; they make fuʿul silent, as in «سَبُع» and «عَضُد». ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read «عَجَبٌ». There are two explanations for it. The clearer: that it is the complete «كان», that is: "Has a wonder occurred to the people?", and «أنْ أَوْحَيْنا» is attached to «عَجَب» with an omitted causal lām, that is: «عَجَبٌ لأَِنْ أوحينا», or on the omission of «مِنْ», that is: «مِنْ أَنْ أوحينا». The second: that it is the defective «كان», and he would have made its subject indefinite and its khabar definite, as in his saying:
2559 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يكونُ مزاجَها عَسَلٌ وماءُ
(…its mixture being honey and water.)
al-Zamakhsharī said: "The best is that it be the complete one, with «أنْ أَوْحَيْنا» a badal from «عجب»", meaning a badal of inclusion or of the whole for the whole, because this was made the very wonder itself, for emphasis. The second explanation is Ibn ʿAṭiyya's.
His saying: {أَنْ أَنذِرِ}: it may be the maṣdar-forming «أن» and may be the explicative one. Then for the maṣdar-forming you have two considerations. One: that you make it the lightened form of the heavy «أنّ», its subject being the omitted pronoun of the matter and affair. So said the Shaykh, and in it is something to consider, in that the predicates of these particles cannot be a request clause; even if something appears to suggest that, it is interpreted with an implied saying, as in his saying:
2560 - ولو أصابَتْ لقالَتْ وَهْي صادقةٌ ... إنَّ الرياضةَ لا تُنْصِبْكَ للشِّيبِ
(Had she hit the mark she would have said, truthfully: training will not set you against grey hair.)
and the saying of another:
2561 - إنَّ الذين قتلتُمْ أمسِ سَيِّدَهُمْ ... لا تحسَبوا ليلَهم عن ليلِكم ناما
(Those whose chief you killed yesterday, do not suppose their night has slept as yours has.)
Also, the khabar in this chapter, when it occurs as a verbal clause, must be separated by things I mentioned in al-Māʾida, but that separator is impossible here. The second: that it is the one that is about to govern the imperfect verb in the subjunctive, which is joined to a conjugated verb in general, such as «كتبت إليه بأَنْ قم» ("I wrote to him: arise"). We have had a discussion on that earlier too. The thing warned of is not mentioned, while the thing of good tidings is mentioned, as will come, because the situation calls for that.
His saying: {أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ}: «أنَّ» and what is in its scope is the good tidings, that is: "give them good news of the establishment of a firm footing of truth (qadam ṣidq)", the bāʾ being omitted, so the two schools apply in its place. What is meant by «قدم صدق» is precedence, merit and an elevated rank. To this al-Zajjāj and al-Zamakhsharī went, and from it comes the saying of Dhū l-Rumma:
2562 - لهمْ قَدَمٌ لا يُنْكِرُ الناسُ أنها ... مع الحَسَبِ العاديِّ طَمَّتْ على البحر
(They have a footing which people do not deny, together with their ancient nobility, that rose above the sea.)
Since striving and outstripping are done by the foot, praised striving was called «قدم», as the hand was called «نعمة» (favour) since favour issues from it; and it was annexed to truth (ṣidq) to indicate its merit, and it is of the type «رجلُ صدقٍ» and «رجلُ سوءٍ». It was also said: it is the precedent of good that they sent forward, and from it comes the saying of Waḍḍāḥ al-Yamanī:
2563 - مالك وضَّاحُ دائمَ الغَزَلِ ... أَلَسْتَ تخشى تقارُبَ الأَجَلِ
صَلِّ لذي العرشِ واتَّخِذْ قَدَماً ... تُنْجيك يوم العِثارِ والزَّلَلِ
(What is the matter with you, Waḍḍāḥ, forever composing love poetry? Do you not fear the nearness of the appointed term? Pray to the Lord of the Throne and take a precedent of good that will save you on the day of stumbling and slipping.)
It was also said: it is advancement in nobility, and from it comes the saying of al-ʿAjjāj:
2564 - ذَلَّ بنو العَوَّامِ مِنْ آل الحَكَمْ ... وتركوا المُلْكَ لمَلْكٍ ذي قَدَمْ
(The sons of al-ʿAwwām, of the family of al-Ḥakam, were humbled and left the kingship to a king of standing.)
that is, one of advancement and nobility. «لهم» is a fronted khabar, «قَدَمَ» is its subject, and «عند ربهم» is an adjective of «قَدَم». And whoever allowed the governed term of the khabar of «أنّ» to precede its subject when it is a preposition, as in the saying:
2565 - فلا تَلْحَني فيها فإنَّ بحبِّها ... أخاك مصابُ القلب جَمٌّ بَلابلُهْ
(Do not blame me over her, for with love of her your brother is stricken at heart, his cares abundant.)
said: «بحبها» is attached to «مُصاب» and has been put before the subject; so likewise «لهم» may be attached to «عند ربهم» because of the sense of being established it contains, with «عند ربهم» being the khabar.
Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «لَسِحْرٌ» and the rest «لَساحر». So «هذا» may be a reference to the Qur'an, and may be a reference to the Messenger on the first reading, but an interpretation is necessary on our saying that the one referred to is the Prophet, peace be upon him, that is, "possessor of sorcery", or they made him that itself for emphasis. As for the second reading, the reference is to the Messenger, peace be upon him, only.
